This lovely pair are ready to steal your hearts — could you offer them their forever home?

name: George
description:
George is a handsome, lovable chap who's searching for a patient and understanding home where he can truly thrive. With the right support, reassurance, and guidance, George has all the potential to blossom into the most loyal companion.

Once George gets to know you, you'll have a friend for life. He absolutely adores his people and loves nothing more than staying close by their side. As with many sensitive dogs, he can be a little wary when meeting new people, so he'll appreciate owners who can gently support and guide him through new situations, helping him build his confidence at his own pace.

George is a big fan of his daily walks, especially when they're nice and relaxed. Rather than rushing from A to B, he enjoys taking his time to sniff and explore the world around him - after all, every walk is an adventure when there are so many interesting scents to discover! He's happy to greet other dogs while out and about, but he'd be happiest as the only dog in his new home, where he can enjoy all the love and attention for himself.

If you're looking for a devoted best friend and have the patience, understanding, and enthusiasm to continue George's training, you'll be rewarded with a wonderful companion. By providing him with the reassurance, consistency, and stability he needs, you'll help him grow in confidence and become the happy, secure dog he's meant to be.

Could you be the special person George has been waiting for?

name: Bentley
description:
Bentley is a friendly, fun-loving boy who loves being part of family life. He enjoys spending time with his favourite people, whether that's heading out for a walk, playing tug with his toys or simply relaxing nearby after a busy day.

Full of character, Bentley is always keen to see what everyone is up to and likes being included in the action. He loves meeting new people, greeting them with plenty of enthusiasm, which is likely his way of seeking reassurance when he's feeling a little uncertain. Given calm introductions and a little time, he quickly settles and enjoys being close to his people.

Bentley enjoys his walks and loves getting out and about. He can be strong on lead when he's eager to get going, but he's equally happy spending time sniffing and exploring. He is looking for a family who can help him continue growing his confidence and social skills around other dogs. Bentley is very interested in making canine friends but can be a little enthusiastic and direct when saying hello. Bentley would benefit from building friendships with a few familiar dogs and gradually developing his confidence and social skills.

Bentley is looking for a calm but active home with secondary school aged children. He would prefer a home where he can be the only pet and have all the space he needs to settle in and thrive. A secure garden for playtime, training and relaxing in the sunshine would be a bonus.

Bentley is a loving, loyal companion who will bring plenty of fun, affection and personality to his future home.

name: Ned
description:
Ned is a playful, energetic young dog who is looking for an active home that can keep up with his zest for life. He loves spending time with his people and enjoys games of tug with a rope toy or chasing after squeaky balls.

Ned is a sociable boy who enjoys meeting other dogs and has shown friendly behaviour. As a young dog, Ned can be quite enthusiastic when greeting dog friends and will benefit from owners who can continue to guide and support him in these interactions.

Ned is looking for owners who are around for most of the day and can provide plenty of physical exercise, mental enrichment and ongoing training.  Food is a great motivator for him, and he enjoys learning when tasty treats are involved.

He will need a garden to explore and play and could potentially live with a well-matched dog who shares his enthusiasm for exercise and playtime. He would be suited to living in a home without cats and could live with older children who can give him the space when needed.

If you're looking for a fun-loving companion and have the time and commitment to help Ned reach his full potential, please apply today.

name: Basil
description:
Basil is a handsome Mini Dachshund with a huge zest for life and an even bigger heart. This charming little character loves being out and about, whether that's heading off on an adventure, meeting his doggy friends, or curling up on the sofa once the day is done.

Basil can be a little cautious when meeting new people and prefers to make friends at his own pace. Give him a calm, low-pressure introduction and you'll quickly see his affectionate side shine through. Once he knows you, he's a real cuddle bug who loves curling up on laps, and being close to his favourite people.

Basil enjoys sniffing and exploring on walks, and also has a playful side - especially when squeaky toys are involved! He's a clever boy who already knows his basics and settles well at home. He prefers a quick greet and move on style when meeting new dogs, and can be worried if other dogs are overly enthusiastic in their greeting. However, he is much more confident around dogs he knows, and loves a game of chase with his doggy pals.

Basil has lived successfully with children and could live with sensible children aged 10+. He may also be able to share his home with a calm, small dog, but won't be able to live with cats or small furries.

If you're looking for a fun, affectionate companion who will happily join you for adventures before snuggling up for cuddles, Basil could be the perfect match!

name: Alfie
description:
Alfie is a young, affectionate boy who loves nothing more than spending time with his favourite people. Playful and full of potential, he's equally happy chasing a toy or snuggling up on the sofa for a cuddle after a busy day.

As Alfie hasn't had many opportunities to explore the world so far, he's looking for a new home that can introduce him to new sights, sounds and adventures at his own pace. With gentle encouragement and positive experiences, we're sure this lovely lad will grow in confidence and enjoy discovering all that life has to offer.

If you're looking for a sweet, loving companion to share both cosy evenings and future adventures with, Alfie could be the perfect match.

name: Freddie
description:
Meet the wonderful Freddie - he's a handsome lad who is absolutely full of beans! Freddie does have an old cruciate injury to one of his hind legs. This is now healed, but will need ongoing management in his new home, as he can get stiff after lots of exercise and is also on a special diet to support his mobility.

He is a very playful boy and loves nothing more than carrying his toys around or playing fetch with you. Freddie also loves to swim and will sniff out any puddle, river, or lake that he can have a good splash around in!

He does have some ongoing training needs to be worked on in his new home, such as his recall, learning not to jump up at people he meets, and loose lead walking. When he is in a familiar environment, he settles well and has very good manners in the home. However, he can quickly forget himself in new situations and needs some support when things get a bit overwhelming.

He has experience of being around children but would prefer older children who can join him with his games of fetch and be a part of his daily care. He is social greeter with other dogs on his walks and will want to encourage them to play, but is likely to be too excitable for some dogs. He could potentially live with a well-matched dog who will join him in a game and tolerate his bounciness.

If you think Freddie sounds like a good match for you, please apply now!

name: Fly
description:
Meet Fly, a beautiful 8-year-old Whippet with a wonderfully gentle nature. Found as a stray, Fly has taken everything in her stride and has quickly won over everyone she meets. She adores people, happily leaning in for fuss and cuddles, and her favourite place is curled up beside you on the sofa.

She also loves her short walks, and entertaining herself at home with her soft squeaky toys, although she is still building up her fitness slowly. Fly is social with other dogs and could live with a well-matched, calm canine companion, although she would be just as happy soaking up all the attention herself. Fly cannot live with cats or small pets due to her typical lurcher prey drive.

In her new home, Fly will need some support with building up time left alone, and brushing up on her house training, but with her sweet nature she's sure to make a wonderful companion.

name: Rolo
description:
Meet Rolo, a charismatic and affectionate young dog who loves nothing more than spending time with his favourite people.

Whether it's enjoying plenty of fuss and cuddles or heading out on an adventure, Rolo is happiest when he's with those he loves. On walks, he's an enthusiastic explorer who likes to take in everything around him, from meeting new people to watching the world go by.

A playful and fun-loving companion, Rolo particularly enjoys a game of tug. He can become quite excited during play and may get a little vocal, but he has already started some positive training around play sessions and would benefit from this being continued in his new home.

Rolo is very interested in other dogs and would love to make new friends while out and about. Due to his strength and enthusiasm, he is still learning how to greet other dogs calmly and appropriately, so he is looking for adopters who are committed to continuing his training in this area. With the right introductions, Rolo could potentially live with a suitable canine companion in the future.

Having previously lived with older children, Rolo has shown himself to be gentle and affectionate around them and would enjoy being part of a family environment. However, he is unable to live with cats.

Full of personality, Rolo is loving, cheeky, and guaranteed to keep you smiling with his goofy antics. Once he's had the chance to play and burn off some energy, he is more than happy to settle down and enjoy some quiet time by your side, making him a wonderful companion. Due to his breed characteristics and training needs, Rolo would benefit from a home with breed experience.

If you're looking for a handsome, affectionate young dog with a big heart and an even bigger personality, Rolo could be the perfect addition to your family. Apply today to find out more about this wonderful boy.

name: George
description:
George is a lovely, gentle boy who enjoys the simple things in life: exploring on walks, sniffing his surroundings and spending time with his favourite people. He walks nicely on a loose lead, travels well and is housetrained, making him an easy companion to have around the home.

Although George may take a few minutes to get to know new people, he soon relaxes and happily accepts fuss and treats. He enjoys calm companionship and will often choose to settle close by once he feels comfortable. A true foodie, George already knows cues such as sit and paw and will be delighted to show off his skills for a tasty reward.

George has lived with children previously and could share his home with calm, older children who can give him time and space to settle into his new routine. He is happy being left for periods of time once settled and would suit a family looking for a relaxed and affectionate companion.

He has seasonal skin issues and has flare ups from time to time which can be managed well with medicated shampoo baths and if need be anti-inflammatories from the vets and regular gland emptying. He is currently fed on hypoallergenic food due to his skin sensitivities.

name: Milo, Mia & Maisy
description:
Meet Milo, Mia and Maisy! This adorable trio are looking for their new home together.

They enjoy going for walks and enjoy having time to sniff and explore while they're out and about.

They are quite worried around other dogs due to being under socialised and can bark at when they see them but can easily be moved on.

Milo, Mia and Maisy would be happy to live with any age children who can give them space when they need it.

They would be looking to be the only pets in the home so they can be the centre of all the attention.

This terrific trio are the perfect dogs for someone looking for companionship as they will give you just that!

name: Ralph
description:
Ralph is an American Bulldog cross puppy that is looking for a family with previous large breed experience to help him grow into a well mannered boy.

Ralph is a lively and affectionate boy, he loves to explore on his walks and will be a great adventure buddy as he grows up!

He can be excitable meeting new people and will pull towards them on walks, so it’s important that Ralphs family help teach him what to do when people don’t want to say hi to him. He can jump up and mouth when excited so will need owners who are confident in working on this with him as he gets older. Due to his breed mixes he will need his family to be able to physically manage his strength when he is older as he is likely to be a big boy.

Ralph loves to run off lead in our secure field and play chase with toys- soft toys are his favourite. He is still learning to play tug and fetch but shows he is keen to continue practising.

Ralph is very intelligent and needs a family that enjoy training to continue building his life skills as well as ‘fun’ training of tricks, to keep his big brain busy. Ralphs favourite thing in the world right now is tasty treats, which makes his training even more exciting!

Ralph could live with another dog that is older, calm and tolerant of young boisterous dogs. Ralph could live with older teenagers that are confident with the breed, mouthing and his energy levels. Ralph wouldn't be able to live with cats as they would be too fun to chase. Ralph could live with smallies if kept separately.

name: Claude
description:
Meet our curious Claude!

This handsome, country gentleman is on the lookout for a new home with active owners who are looking to share the great outdoors with a four-legged companion.

Claude LOVES his walks and he does so at one million miles an hour, we are simply holding onto the lead and tagging along. True to his breed, he loves to use his nose, so he would be ideal for new owners who either have previous gundog experience, or an interest in similar training or scent work to help him put that nose to good use.

He would be a great companion for people who are looking to cover many miles. His recall will need building up before being let off lead, and please be aware he can be strong on lead so will need a strong owner and some support with loose lead walking.

Claude is dog social, and can make canine companions whilst out and about, but needs to be the only dog in his new home as after saying a quick ‘hello’ to other dogs, he doesn’t want much more interaction. Due to his interest in chasing birds and rabbits, he cannot live with cats.

He could live with children who are comfortable with a bouncy dog and able to give him time and space to do important dog business when he needs to.

After exploring the countryside, Claude loves nothing more than curling up on a cosy bed and having a snooze. He has no experience of home life so would like someone home for most of the day as he loves to be in your company, but time left alone could be built up. He will need support with house training.

If you've got room in your heart and home for this gorgeous chap, then please get in touch today.

name: Blue
description:
Blue is a stunning Dogue de Bordeaux with an even bigger heart. Weighing around 60kg, this affectionate giant absolutely loves people and thrives on companionship. Friendly, confident and easy-going, Blue takes life in his stride and enjoys being involved in family life wherever possible.

Despite his impressive size, Blue is a gentle, well-mannered boy who seems convinced he's much smaller than he really is – he'd happily climb onto your lap for a cuddle if given the chance!

Blue is an incredibly social dog who enjoys spending time with both familiar faces and new people. He forms strong bonds with his family and is happiest when receiving attention and affection.

Blue loves meeting people and greets visitors with enthusiasm. He may bark when the doorbell rings and become excited when guests arrive but he settles quickly with guidance.

He plays appropriately, remains easy to interrupt and happily ends games when asked. If given a toy he may take it away to enjoy independently for a while but remains relaxed and co-operative.

Like many giant breeds, Blue often prefers cooler surfaces such as tiled or lino flooring to carpets.

He has not been allowed on furniture in his previous home, although he may still try to convince you that a 60kg dog belongs on your lap!

If you're looking for a loyal, affectionate and wonderfully sociable companion, Blue could be the dog for you. This gentle giant has so much love to give and is ready to find a new family who will cherish him as much as he will cherish them.

name: Noxy
description:
Noxy is a lovely young girl with a sweet and affectionate nature who is looking for a new family to help her settle into home life.

She is a friendly girl who enjoys meeting people and thrives on companionship, making her a wonderful addition to a home where she can be included in everyday activities.

Noxy loves getting out and about on her walks and is always ready for an adventure. She has excellent recall, making her a joy to exercise, and she enjoys exploring the world alongside her favourite people. Noxy is social with other dogs and enjoys canine company, and she could happily share her home with a calm, dog-friendly resident dog.

Due to her gentle nature, Noxy could live with older children who can understand when she needs a little space and help her build confidence in her new surroundings.

As she adjusts to a new home, Noxy will benefit from patient adopters who can give her time to settle at her own pace and provide plenty of reassurance. She forms strong bonds with those she loves and can find being left alone difficult, so she is looking for a home where someone is around for much of the day initially and can gradually help her learn that alone time is safe and predictable. In return, Noxy promises to be a loyal, loving companion who will bring lots of fun, affection and happy adventures to her new family.

Noxy is still waiting her health check and can be rehomed once this is completed.

name: Wookie
description:
Wookie is a sweet, energetic young dog who is looking for his forever home. Wookie can be a little underconfident at first but over time forms strong relationships with his human companions. He enjoys playing with a variety of toys and pottering along on his daily walks.

Wookie could live with a sociable, dog-experienced dog that could show him the ways of the world and help him develop into the perfect companion. A suitable existing dog would need to visit the centre and meet Wookie if your application is successful.

Wookie is looking for an owner dedicated to continued socialisation into the home and real world, to help develop him into a well-rounded adult dog.

Wookie would benefit from someone being around regularly to help settle him into the home and start implementing the important steps to help him settle into a new routine.

If you have a loving home to offer, please do apply!

name: Luna
description:
Meet the lovely Luna,

Luna is looking for a home to call her own. She is an affectionate little lady that loves to be around her familiar people and lap up all the fuss. She likes meeting new people, but can be a little sensitive at first. However, once she warms up to you, she will be your best friend

Luna loves to get out on her walks, sniffing and exploring! She would be best suited to being walked in quiet areas initially and will need ongoing support through training to help her become more comfortable when seeing/greeting other dogs.

Luna could live with older children, who are mindful of her body language and give her space when needed. However she cannot live with other dogs, cats or small animals.

If you feel you could give Luna the home she dreams of, please apply below!

name: Poppy
description:
Say hello to Poppy, a sweet middle aged lady who is looking for a new family.

Poppy is a very friendly dog, she enjoys meeting new people, introducing herself and having some fuss.  She is also super playful and loves chase her favourite ball around in the garden or on a walk, she is also partial to carrying a soft toy around with her or throw it in the air.

Poppy has experience of spending time with grandchildren in her family and had a good relationship with them so could live with children again pending meets at the centre.  She is social with other dogs on the whole but will show she is uncomfortable if they are too big and too OTT with her.  So we think she would be best suited as an only pet in her new home.

She will initially need owners who can help her settle and get into a routine with her housetraining and being left on her own, so owners who are around for most of the day would be ideal.

If you are looking for a playful little companion to join your home then Poppy could be the girl for you

name: Cloud
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, and would like to continue this in my new home!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

24-07-26 Cloud is a lovely little lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. Cloud has come on in leaps and bounds since arriving with us. She is now a lovely girl to handle and has built wonderful relationships with the people she knows and trusts. She absolutely loves a cuddle and will happily snuggle up beside her favourite people for plenty of affection. Although she can still be a little unsure in new situations, her confidence continues to grow every day.

Cloud gets on wonderfully with other dogs and enjoys spending time with different canine companions each day, which has really helped her confidence blossom. She is very well socialised and loves being out in the exercise yards with her doggy friends. She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can continue to guide and reassure her as she settles into family life.

As Cloud has never lived in a home before, she will still need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her time to adjust and help her learn at her own pace. She now walks beautifully on her harness and thoroughly enjoys getting out and about, and she would love to continue exploring the world with her forever family.

Cloud would like a quiet home and could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she may need a little time to settle into her new surroundings.

Cloud has truly blossomed into a happy, affectionate little girl. She adores being close to her people and loves nothing more than curling up beside them for a cuddle. She is an absolute diamond with so much love to give, and we know she is going to make a wonderful companion for one very lucky family.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Flash
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with ex-breeding experience to understand me

I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a good sized, secure garden to explore.

I can walk on a lead but find this very overwhelming at the moment.

I have entropion in both eyes, which have been repaired by the vets.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle with a big personality, a sensitive soul, and an oversized puppy spirit. He first came to us after his previous owners could no longer give him the time and exercise he needed. Since then, we’ve watched him grow from a worried boy into a much more confident and affectionate companion, and he continues to make us proud every single day.

Flash is still very much a character, goofy, playful, and full of energy but beneath his bouncy exterior lies a gentle heart that just wants to love and be loved. He can be sensitive in new situations and still finds the world a little overwhelming at times, but with people he trusts, his sweet and loyal nature shines through. Once Flash bonds with you, he is yours for life.

Recently, he’s been showing us more of his loving side. On rainy days when we huddle together out of the downpour, he rolls over for belly rubs, brings his toys for attention, and happily drifts off to sleep during a cuddle. It’s in these quiet moments that his true personality comes out, affectionate, trusting, and eager to please.

Flash’s training is going from strength to strength. He’s mastered “touch” (booping his nose to your hand) and is now learning “place.” He still gets a little mouthy when he’s overexcited, but he’s come a long way since his arrival and continues to improve with patience and consistency. He’ll need his future family to have ex-breeding experience and to continue this gentle guidance in the home so he can keep building on all the progress he’s made.

Being an active breed, Flash loves his walks and enjoys exploring the world at his own pace. He’s happiest in calm, quiet areas where he can relax and take everything in without feeling rushed. He will need to be the only pet in the home, as he prefers human companionship over other animals, and he’s not a fan of pigeons or seagulls either!

Flash has had successful surgery for entropion in both eyes, he received care for mild dermatitis around both eyes, but this has since cleared. He is currently being treated for sore and sensitive ears.

What Flash truly needs now is a calm, understanding, adult-only home with ex-breeding experience and with someone who’s around most of the time, someone who can offer him patience, structure, and all the love he deserves. With time and trust, Flash will repay his person a hundred times over with loyalty, affection, and that special spark that makes him so unforgettable.

Please don’t overlook this beautiful boy. Flash has come so far and is ready to start the next chapter of his life he’s just waiting for that one person to believe in him and bring him home.

Flash will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Flash has officially been waiting for a home for a whole year. After a first few months of (a lot of) patience and training, it's then blossomed into the most incredible remaining months where we’ve really seen Flash’s true heart and soul. This dog is phenomenal in more ways than one, and it’s so sad he’s now become part of the MT furniture, and that the rescue has now become his home.

So for Flash’s 1 year anniversary, I took him off site to the nearby country park for a lovely stroll, followed by a visit to McD’s for some chicken nuggets.

Flash was suuuuuuch a good boy on his walk. He took in all the new smells, and took the new environment in his stride. He was even approached by 3 off lead small dogs, and didn’t react at all. He trotted along the park, with the world at his feet and it was the most amazing thing to see.

He is an absolute darling in the car, so we made a swift visit to McD’s for a box of 20 nuggets to eat together in our on site flat.

It was so nice to see Flash in a home like environment, he jumped straight on the sofa, and wandered around inspecting every room. We sat on the floor together eating our nuggets, and he eventually rested on the raised bed and had a little snooze.

It was heartbreaking putting him back in his kennel, when he seemed so at peace and settled in the flat. I just wish there was someone out there who could see him for everything he is and more!!!

Our beautiful, bonkers Flash has learnt a new trick and we thought we would share.

Flash has also been enjoying the sunshine with lots of walks and plays in the yards this week.

Flash continues to work hard on growing his calmness around new people and he is doing ok. He has now been 10 months here at the rescue and has an increasing fan base amongst the staff but he of course longs for a home and people of his own.

When I first started working with him, I was apprehensive. He was a much larger dog than I was used to working with, and he would mouth you til his hearts content. Not because he is a nasty dog, or means any harm whatsoever, but simply because he has come from a home (just out of puppyhood) and he has become extremely anxious and unsettled being in a kennel environment. On top of that, he has been taught 0 manners which definitely didn’t help with the matter!!! I struggled to bond with him, I struggled to understand why he wouldn’t listen when being told, and why all he wanted to do was treat my arm like a toy…

However I found myself thinking, what has Flash been through in his life that was ever HIS fault? He didn’t ask to spend so much of his life in kennels. He never asked to be put in situations where his anxiety gets the better of him, it was never his decision to not be trained to behave normally. So I decided to buck up my ideas and realise he’s not as scary as he seems, and he’s probably just as anxious being around me as I was him. And from that moment on, our relationship has blossomed…

This boy is truly a superstar in every sense of the word. He is SUCH a goofball, and can have you in fits of laughter within seconds of being with him. His personality is infectious, and as soon as he is comfortable with you and realises you are no threat to him, he shines like the star he is. It’s gutting that Flash doesn’t allow every staff member to see all sides of him. The side that shows his softness, his sweetness, his kindness. But that just makes me so much more grateful that he feels comfortable enough around me to do so.

You can see from his pictures, Flash is muzzle trained. Not because he is an aggressive dog, not because he is a violent dog, it’s simply due to his anxiousness. On one hand, Flash is a super intelligent Poodle but on the other hand, he doesn’t really show it. His anxiety gets the better of him, and he puts himself in uncomfortable positions with new people & then panics whilst he’s in it. It is SUPER important that whoever adopts Flash’s main priority is keeping him safe, and keeping him from making decisions that he feels uncertain about. He wants to make friends with everyone, but also decides halfway through some interactions that he’s not to keen on the thought too!

Among (of course) all of the other precious angels I look after the rescue, Flash is one of the reasons I get excited to go to work. You shouldn’t really have favourites, but Flash does take the cake. I cherish every single moment I get with him. Our lovely strolls up the country lanes, our snuggles in the back of his kennel after a long day, our zoomies down our big play yard. Every single moment & memory I look forward to recreating every single day. Nothing tops being around this dog, nothing else matters when you’re with Flash.

If I was in a position to take him home & work with him through his quirks, I absolutely would, in heartbeat in fact. There is just something so special about him, and I truly envy whoever is fortunate to adopt this incredible young man. And for as long as Flash remains in kennels, I will advocate for him, make him feel safe, comfortable and most of all loved.

Flash has completely changed my mind about Poodles. I am absolutely in love with him. He might not be the sharpest boy in the bunch, but he more than makes up for it with his goofy charm and endless silliness.We are still working on his mouthing when he becomes overexcited. Progress is steady, and every small step forward feels like a real achievement. Flash loves his freedom. We take daily trips to the big yard where he runs around like the happiest whirlwind you have ever seen. He would really benefit from visits to private dog fields where he can safely zoom and explore to his heart’s content.Meeting new people can still be a little tricky for him, but we have a careful plan in place to help him do so safely and comfortably. For those of us who know Flash well, he shows a side many would not expect. Beneath his anxiousness and the need for a muzzle at times is the sweetest, softest boy who adores snuggles and head tickles.He loves to stay close, gently resting his head in your lap until he drifts off to sleep. At the end of each day, we share a quiet moment together, curled up side by side until his eyes close and he is peacefully dreaming.Flash truly is a special boy who deserves a very special home. He needs someone who can offer love, patience, and understanding. In return, he will give unwavering loyalty and companionship for life.

Flash is an absolute character, this boy is full of life and once he knows you he adores you but his introductions to new people always need to be slow as this sensitive boy can be easily overwhelmed.

Flash works well within a routine, he has an abundance of energy and a super inquisitive nature which can sometimes lead to him becoming quite lively, he will often revert to ‘mouthing’ and jumping up when he is uncomfortable or unsure.

Flash has a super inquisitive nature and loves to observe what’s going on at a distance. This boy can also be an absolute cuddle monster and adores a snuggle with his favourite people, and will fall asleep next to us when we have the opportunity to sit quietly with him. One of flash’s unique traits is his love of a pamper session! I have never known a dog who enjoys a bath and hairdryer the way he does and he becomes quite docile under the hair dryer whilst having a gentle brush.

Flash’s ideal home would be a quiet an experienced dog owning home (adults only) with humans that have the patience and time to help grow his confidence and who also understand the need to grow calmness in him. Flash has had a few dog friends at the rescue but his high spirted nature can be a bit much for some dogs and he does not seem to like male dogs, for this reason a home where he is the only pooch would suit him best.

Flash walks well on lead but can become very excited when he sees other dogs, walks in quiet areas would be perfect for him, he loves to be outdoors and often just enjoys sitting in the yard with me watching birds, but he will equally enjoy time spent just hanging out with his humans at home. Flash really is a wonderfully, lovable, giant puppy, looking for kind and understanding humans to provide him with the security and love he deserves.

Flash has had a brilliant few weeks. He celebrated his second Birthday and was treated with his first snow day, which he loved frolicking about in. Unfortunately, he did have to spend his birthday in kennels, but I made sure it was still a very special day for him. We hopped in the car, and I took him for a little walk before heading to the pet shop to pick out some birthday treats. He chose a dinosaur toy and a knuckle bone, which he thoroughly enjoyed. I also bought him some special birthday biscuits to keep him going through the week.

After that, I truly spoiled him, and we decided to go to Burger King for a burger! Flash was quite confused at first, but once he had a taste, he couldn’t get enough.

Flash truly is a special boy and will need a special home to match. He can be very wary of strangers and doesn’t always show clear signs if he’s uncomfortable. For this reason, he is muzzled when out on walks, which I make sure to do whenever we go out.

Flash will need an adult-only home with no visiting children. He cannot live with cats or any small animals

The stunning Flash had a little pamper today, which he absolutely loved. He was as good as gold whilst in the bath and sat very contentedly on the grooming table looking out the window enjoying the warmth of the blowers. I have never known a dog to enjoy bath time as much as he does, he becomes quite sleepy and cuddley, it’s the cutest thing.

After his wash and blow dry he got to open some Christmas treats out in the yard sent in from the lovely folks out there that support Many Tears, Flash particular enjoyed the food presents.

Flash really is the most wonderful boy once you get to know him, and we see improvement every day in his sometimes lively and skittish nature. This fantastic boy will make the most awesome and loyal of friend with the person or couple that are prepared to put the time and love into him he so deserves.

Today, Flash and I went on a little adventure to the local pet shop, finishing off with a much-needed pupcup! He was an absolute angel in the car—he hopped right in, buckled up, and sat calmly for the whole journey. I watched him in the mirror as he gazed out at the world passing by. When we arrived, we popped his muzzle on as a precaution since he can sometimes be wary of strangers. Flash wandered around the shop, taking in all the sights and smells, until he discovered the pick-and-mix treats—which of course we had to get. After choosing his goodies, he rummaged through the plushies and picked out a squeaky monkey to take home.

As we headed toward the till, another dog suddenly rushed around a corner and startled Flash, causing him to react. I managed to whisk him away with a distraction, but he became very on edge and tucked himself into me for comfort. A lovely lady then came around the opposite corner and, despite having seen his reaction, kindly stopped to say hello. She happened to be a previous Many Tears adopter, and her own pup is doing wonderfully. She chose to ignore Flash at first to give him space, and once he settled, he allowed her to gently stroke his head. After wishing us well, we carried on with our day.

We sat outside Costa in the sunshine, and Flash absolutely loved his pupcup, so much so that he managed to get it all over his nose.

I’m incredibly proud of Flash today. It was his first outing since arriving in kennels, and I could really see how scared he can be underneath it all, and how much he relies on his human for reassurance. Flash needs someone devoted, patient, and willing to put time into training and working through his reactivity toward other dogs. He truly is a special boy.

Another bleak day at the rescue with the rain pouring down non-stop, but it meant I got to spend some more quality time with the dogsI’ve never been one for poodles but Flash really has stolen my heartToday I really did see his loving and caring side as we cuddled away from the downpour. He rolled around, brought me his toys and chews before receiving belly rubs and head scratches until he fell asleep

If you’ve been to the rescue I’m usually walking Flash around the reception area in order for him to build his relationship with humans and other dogs but it was nice to just have some one on one time with him today, once you’ve created a bond with this boy he is yours for life.Flash’s’ training is still continuing and has managed to learn ‘touch’ where he boops his nose to the designated hand and is in the midst of learning ‘place’.

In a home will still need some training in order for him to thrive.

Flash is still a little mouthy when he gets super excited but is doing much better to when he first arrived with us.

It's been almost 4 months since Flash arrived here and I feel he has been very much overlooked. Deep down he’s a big cuddle bug and thrives on attention.

I tried spending most of my time with him today as kennel life is very stressful for him. We visited the big yard multiple times, went for a stroll and even met 2 dogs on a walk and greeted them with such kindness. Might I say he walks beautifully alongside you!

We met some new people in the reception area, which can sometimes make Flash a little uneasy but he did fantastically and even accepted some treats. For this he is muzzle trained as he can be mouthy when he’s a little too excited!

The last task of the day was to be groomed. I never thought I would see this boy sit still for more than a few seconds, but he amazed me and hopped up onto the grooming table ready to be pampered! And he now looks so good! Flash really doesn’t mind being groomed which will be helpful for the future.

I absolutely adore this beautiful boy. Flash is best described as an oversized puppy at heart. He has a playful, goofy nature but sometimes forgets his size, which can make him a little overexcited and mouthy, especially if he’s unsure or feeling frustrated.

Flash can be a sensitive soul who is often scared of his own shadow and needs plenty of reassurance and gentle confidence-building when faced with new experiences (like the umbrella he discovered today!). Because of this, kennel life is very tough for him, and I truly believe he will thrive so much more in a loving home.

Once Flash trusts you, he shows his affectionate side. He adores snuggling in for a cuddle and loves being pampered.

Flash’s ideal home would be an adult-only household where he can be the only dog. He isn’t aggressive with other dogs but can become boisterous and overwhelming. A quiet location with a secure, good-sized garden would be perfect, ideally with adopters who enjoy long walks and hikes.

He walks beautifully on the lead, enjoys all weathers, and has the stamina to go for hours. While he may sometimes react to new situations or get excitable around other dogs, his confidence and manners are improving every day. Flash will need adopters who are home most of the time or able to include him in their daily lives, as he finds being left alone difficult and may struggle with separation anxiety.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle who has come to us from a home as his owners no longer had time for him and couldn't offer him the exercise he requires. Although he has lived in a home before, Flash is a worried boy who finds new experiences and people quite daunting. Because of this, Flash is looking for an experienced, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time, patience, and love to give. He needs adopters who won’t give up on him and who will allow him to settle in at his own pace.Initially, Flash can be wary of new people and unsure of their intentions, but once you’ve gained his trust, he begins to show his affectionate and loyal nature. He forms strong bonds with those he feels safe around and shows a deep need for companionship. He does not cope well with being left alone and has shown signs of separation anxiety, getting very worried and anxious when left on his own. He will need an adopter who is able to be with him all of the time and who will work on this with him, slowly building up any time he is left. We are told he was crate trained in his previous home, which may help with this process.Flash is particularly sensitive to loud or sudden noises, which can cause him to panic. He feels safest in quiet, familiar surroundings and finds walks outside of the rescue grounds very difficult at the moment. When taken beyond his comfort zone, he becomes overwhelmed and spins in circles in an attempt to return to safety. While he can walk on a lead, his adopters will need to help him grow in confidence very gradually and may need to begin with simply enjoying time in the garden or short walks in peaceful areas.Flash would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as he can be grumbly when meeting other dogs. This is something his adopters will need to work on with him with patience and positive reinforcement. Because of this, he must only be allowed off lead in secure areas with no other dogs present. He also cannot live with cats or small animals and we are told he isn't a fan of pigeons or seagulls.Flash will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and where his adopters will help him settle into a consistent routine so he can feel safe and secure. We are told that he is house trained but he may need some reminders of this in his new homeAlthough he is currently worried about going for walks, he is an active breed who will need to be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. We have been told that he has previously done some agility and scent work, so once his confidence grows this is something he may like to explore again in the future. His previous owners also said he enjoyed being groomed and bathed, though we haven’t yet introduced this at the rescue.This beautiful boy has so much potential in the right hands. If you have the time, experience, and understanding to give Flash the security and stability he needs, he will reward you with trust, loyalty, and love. Please don’t overlook him, he’s waiting for that one special person to believe in him.Flash has an entropion in both eyes, which has been repaired by our vets but does have some dermatitis around his eyes.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Tippins
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a larger doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats yet!

I would like a large, and secure garden that I can settle into.

I do walk on a lead, but am still gaining my confidence and will need support.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

06-07-26 Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a little apprehensive when she first meets new people, but she is already showing signs that her confidence is growing. Once she knows you, she enjoys a fuss and is happy to be handled. Tippins has a big personality and is a fun girl to spend time with.

At the moment, Tippins is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with at least one other confident resident dog for support and companionship. She has always lived with bigger dogs and seems happiest around them. Tippins can be a little bossy with less confident dogs, so she wouldn't be suitable to live with smaller or younger dogs. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see if she could adapt to being an only dog. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience that can understand her needs.

As Tippins has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she settles in and learns what home life is all about. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that can allow her time to settle into a calm environment.

Tippins already walks on a lead, but doesn't seem to be overly confident on this so she will need continued support as she learns, and once she has settled into her new home, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog so that she can continue lead training.

Tippins is a lovely girl with lots of character. She's already showing us what a sweet dog she is, and we hope that, with time and patience, she'll continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.

Tippins is now receiving regular cleanings from the vets for waxy ears and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Dolly
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden, at least 6ft, while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home! Read below for more information!

17-07-26 Dolly is a sweet but shy little lady who has come into our care from a breeder and is still learning that people can be kind. At the moment, she isn't confident enough to approach you herself, but with patience, gentle reassurance, and time to build trust, she will happily accept a quiet fuss.

Dolly is a gentle, sensitive girl who is looking for a calm home with adopters who have experience and understand that confidence cannot be rushed. We would consider homing her with, older dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace. She will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can look to for reassurance as she settles in and learns about life as a much-loved family pet.

Having never lived in a home before, Dolly will need patient adopters to help her learn about house training, walking on a lead, and all the new experiences that come with home life. She will need the freedom to progress at her own pace, with plenty of encouragement and understanding along the way. She will also need an extra secure garden as she learns about the outside world.

Dolly is a truly sweet-natured little lady who simply needs someone willing to give her a chance. With time, patience, and the support of a confident canine companion, we're sure her true personality will shine through, making every small step forward incredibly rewarding.

Dolly has arrived with dry eyes, that she is receiving treatment for. She has also arrived with a skin irritation that has been cleaned. The vets are monitoring her eyes, and skin to ensure her health.

Dolly has been given the Gift of Life by Ceri Mann

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

07-07-26 Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him.

Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

Archie has settled back into rescue life well and is currently sharing his kennel with a lovely female dog, who he gets on very well with. He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet.

Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

name: Jenga
description:
I will need a home that understands I will need time to settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

17-07-26 Jenga is a pretty little lady who has come into our care from a breeder and is still feeling very unsure of her surroundings. At the moment, she prefers to curl up in her bed and quietly watch the world go by rather than join in. She is accepting of being handled, but this is more due to her gentle, submissive nature than because she feels confident, so she will need patient adopters who are happy to let her settle at her own pace.

Jenga takes great comfort from her kennel friends and relies on them for reassurance. Because of this, she will need a home with at least one kind, confident resident dog who can help guide her and give her the confidence to embrace life as a much-loved family pet.

Having never lived in a home before, Jenga will need support with house training and all the new experiences that come with family life. She has not yet learned to walk on a lead and may prefer to start by building her confidence with gentle garden adventures before progressing to walks when she feels ready.

Jenga is a sweet, sensitive little girl who simply needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With love, patience, and the support of a canine companion, we're sure she will blossom into the wonderful dog we know she can be.

Jenga has arrived with a small rash on her stomach, but this is clearing up nicely.

She is being monitored for suspected intermitten lameness in her back legs that the vets do not think is an issue at this time.

Jenga has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

name: Fox
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Fox is a nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. Since arriving, Fox has really started to blossom and is showing us more of her lovely personality every day. She is a wonderfully smiley girl whose confidence continues to grow, and she will now happily approach people for a gentle chin scratch before settling nearby and relaxing in their company.

Fox still takes a great deal of comfort from her canine companions and relies heavily on her kennel friends for reassurance. During her time at the rescue, she has shared her kennel with several different dogs and has been an absolute angel with every one of them, regardless of their size or gender. She is a gentle and social girl who clearly finds confidence from having another dog by her side.

Fox will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she continues to settle in and find her paws. A canine companion will be an important part of helping Fox feel safe and continue building her confidence.

As Fox has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. She walks well on a harness and is making great progress. She will need patient adopters who are happy to take things at her pace and allow her confidence to build gradually.

In the right home, Fox could share her space with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Fox is a sensitive and gentle girl who is trying her best to be brave. She has already come such a long way, and with continued patience, support, and the companionship of another dog, she will continue to blossom into a happy and confident companion.

Fox has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

Fox is really blossoming during her time at the rescue. She’s a wonderfully smiley girl whose confidence grows a little more every day. She will now happily approach people for a gentle chin scratch and is content to lie down and relax nearby.Fox still takes a great deal of comfort from her canine companions and relies heavily on her kennel friends for reassurance. During her time at the rescue, she has shared her kennel with several different dogs and has been an absolute angel with every one of them, regardless of their size or gender.

Fox is a nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is currently too worried to ask for fuss, but her confidence is slowly beginning to grow. At the moment, she will only approach when she has the reassurance of hiding behind one of her kennel friends, showing just how much she relies on their support.

Fox gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies heavily on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Fox has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. She will need patient adopters who are happy to take things at her pace and allow her confidence to build gradually.

Fox is a sensitive and gentle girl who is trying her best to be brave. With time, patience, and the support of another dog, she will begin to feel safe and slowly blossom into a much more confident companion.

name: Pandora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home & I can live with teens, aged 16+.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

18-05-26 Pandora has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a scared little girl who is worried to find herself here at the moment, but she is trying ever so hard to be brave. If approached slowly and gently, Pandora is happy to enjoy a little fuss and is beginning to show what a sweet girl she is.

Pandora is looking for a calm and quiet home and would benefit from adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and reassurance as she settles into her new life. She gains confidence from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help show her the way. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be new to Pandora and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training. She walks well on a harness but it is advised to  initially further practice around the safety of the garden to help build her confidence. She will need an extra secure fence of at least 6ft to ensure her safety.

Although Pandora is not yet walking on a lead, we feel she will be best suited to an active home where, once she has gained confidence and learned all about the world around her, she will be able to enjoy lots of adventures with her family. With time, patience and the support of her doggy friend, we are sure Pandora will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Our vets have noted that she has a Grade 1 heart murmur, which doesn't require any medication but will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet going forward. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her face, which our vets diagnosed as a salivary mucocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this and it has remained stable so far. However, it is likely to gradually refill over the coming weeks or months and would need to be drained again if this happens. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Pandora's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.

Pandora has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

name: Jaffa Cake
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy children who respect my space.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I haven’t met cats

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

17-07-26 Jaffa Cake is an amazing little lady who has come into our care from a breeder, and she is quite possibly the cutest pocket-sized bean anyone could wish to welcome into their home. She is an absolute darling with a gentle, affectionate nature and a heart full of love.

When Jaffa Cake first arrived, she was understandably nervous and unsure of the world around her. However, she has blossomed beautifully and is now the ultimate lap dog! She adores cuddles and being close to her people, and her adopters will need to understand that she must be allowed on the furniture for plenty of snuggles and will need to sleep in the bedroom with her family. Being close to her people is very important to this affectionate little girl.

Jaffa Cake can be a little shy when being picked up or handled, so she will still benefit from a gentle approach and plenty of patience. Once she feels comfortable, however, her sweet and loving personality truly shines through.

Jaffa Cake could live as an only dog or with another kind and confident resident dog. She would also be suitable to live with gentle, dog-savvy older children who can treat her kindly and respectfully.

Having never lived in a home before, Jaffa Cake will need patient adopters to help her learn all the basics of family life, including house training. With the right support, we are sure she will quickly discover how wonderful home life can be.

Jaffa Cake is an absolute sweetheart and a truly special little lady. She has so much love to give and would adore nothing more than a home where she can be cherished, cuddled and included in family life. For the lucky family who welcomes her home, she will be a devoted and affectionate companion who brings joy wherever she goes.

Jaffa Cake has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Parmenter
