name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

18-06-26 Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Trixie
description:
I'll need an adult only home with adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs.

I am looking for a home where I can be the only dog & get all the love and attention.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I walk on a lead but will need my adopters to be extra secure.

I understand toilet training, but will need a reminder in a new home!

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home! Read below for more info!

Trixie is a very sweet lady who has come to us from a breeder in search of a new start. Although her tail is constantly wagging, she will shyly approach for a gentle fuss and tends to stay away and watch from a distance until she feels safe. Once she builds trust, she is affectionate and will enjoy a snuggle and a gentle fuss.

In foster, she shown herself to be a nervous girl in new environments who still needed encouragement to engage with new people. She would often hang back and observe, but once more secure she would come forward for interaction and enjoy fuss and attention from her fosterer.

Despite the fact that she is still a nervous girl, she also isn't keen on sharing her home with other dogs and so we feel she would be happiest as an only dog in her new home. Although she has been in foster with other dogs, she can be jealous when her fosterer is showing attention to other dogs and has reacted towards them on occasion. She is fine with socialising with other calm dogs, but can be reactive towards barking or yappy dogs ordogs that are in her face too much or too boisterous.For this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. She has met cats fine, but due to her tendency to become jealous, we would not look to home her with cats.

In the garden, she has shown signs of digging and has previously tried to escape a foster home, so very secure boundaries are essential. Her new home will need to have 6ft minimum fencing height and her new adopters will need to keep her on lead in the garden until she gains confidence outside. She might enjoy having a sand pit to play in so she can enjoy digging in appropriate areas.

Trixie had been mostly clean in the house in her foster home, and seemed to be a star at toilet training. However, she may need some reminders in her new home as she settles in new surroundings.

She is walking on a lead and harness, but can still become startled and may try to back out if frightened. She needs experienced adopters, a secure garden (6ft+ fencing) as she has been digging in her foster garden, and additional safety measures indoors.

She will need a calm, secure, adult-only home and a gentle introduction to home life.

She has had a small lump removed from her left mammary gland and is recovering well.

Trixie has been given the Gift of Life by Tanya Player

If every day was a Trixie day, life would be lovely. Trixie is the sweetest and loveliest of dogs. Her favourite pastimes include tummy rubs and cuddles, and if there’s a home out there with a Trixie-sized spot on the sofa and a human to shower her with fusses, she would be in heaven.

When Trixie is happy, you know it, and she will bounce around you outside for a little play before parking herself next to you for more belly rubs. She loves sitting outside and just relaxing with you.

Trixie does also enjoy a walk (in very quiet areas); however, she can be very, very easily spooked and, if startled, will bolt and has done so previously. Any adopters would need to be very aware of this and work on building her confidence at home before considering outings. Adopters will also need to ensure a very secure setup for her at home, i.e. secure entrances and exits from the house.

Trixie prefers to have a human all to herself and, for this reason, she would like to be the only dog with a human who will be home most of the time.

Trixie truly is a gem of a girl with a heart of gold. A special and sweet lady, who longs for safe hands (and laps) to snuggle into. This super dog needs a little time and a lot of security,  give her that and you will have a bond for life.

Trixie is looking for a home that is quiet, gentle, patient and super secure on a practical level. Trixie is incredibly spooky and even if she trusts you, the slightest of frights in her environment and she will bolt. Because Trixie is a high flight risk she would be suited to a dog experienced home, ideally with knowledge of flighty and/or ex-breeding dogs.

It’s important that her new people have a secure plan for getting her out of the car on arrival home after adoption and are able to keep entrance and exits to the house escape safe. In return for your kindness Trixie will be the cutest of best friends. Trixie is looking to be the only dog and is suited to an adult home with no visiting children.

Trixie has been in foster with me for three weeks now and is settling into our routine fairly well.

When she first arrived, Trixie was very human-oriented and showed signs of jealousy towards other dogs, which led to a few altercations. She would often growl if another dog came close to me, as she wanted all the attention for herself. This is something we’ve been working on, but we still feel it is best if she is homed as an only dog in her new home.

From her interactions with my resident dogs, it’s clear that Trixie isn’t comfortable with small, yappy dogs. She does seem to prefer female human company, although she is continuing to build confidence more generally. She currently sleeps downstairs in an open, covered crate, which she uses as her safe space.

For the first couple of weeks, Trixie has slept downstairs quietly through the night with no accidents. Over the last few nights, she has been a little more unsettled and has had a couple of accidents, which seems to be linked to wanting more human attention.

Trixie is fed on dry Arden Grange and is currently fed separately, as she will try to eat other dogs’ food if given the chance. She was also caught eating poo, so I have started soaking her food in hot water and letting it cool, which she seems to prefer.

In her first week, Trixie did try digging in the garden and looking for ways to escape, but this behaviour has now settled. She clearly recognises me and gets very excited when she sees me, running over happily for fuss and attention.

She has been out on walks and does reasonably well when accompanied by another dog, but she is still quite flighty and easily startled. For now, she should only be walked in secure areas, as she will try to back out of her harness if she feels unsure and has demonstrated this once already.

Trixie can be complex at times, so she will need a calm, experienced adopter who understands nervous, ex-breeding dogs and can handle her with patience and care. It will be important to give her time to settle at home and build trust before introducing too many new experiences, especially.

Trixie absolutely craves human attention and is happiest curled up next to me on the sofa. As her confidence continues to grow and her jealousy is managed, she has all the makings of a very loyal and loving companion who simply wants to feel safe and adored.

Trixie is now in foster and is settling in well. She travelled well and was clean on arrival with no issues noted in the car or on entering the home.

Once in the foster home, Trixie has shown herself to be a very nervous little girl who is still unsure of new environments and needs encouragement to engage with people. She will often hang back and watch, but once she feels a bit more secure she will come forward and seek interaction. On these occasions she has chosen to snuggle close to me and will sit gazing and enjoying contact, although she does need to be gently encouraged each time as confidence doesn’t yet seem consistent.

It has quickly become apparent that Trixie is quite a complex girl in the home. She is very focused on attention and has already shown signs of jealousy when sharing human interaction. On one occasion, when another foster dog came onto the sofa, Trixie reacted strongly and became defensive. She can also be particular about other dogs in general and can be especially reactive to barking dogs, and has shown a clear dislike of a small dachshund in the home. For this reason, she will now be looking for a home as an only dog where she can get all of the attention for herself.

Outside of this, she is an active little girl and has already shown she is a determined digger, having previously managed to dig under fencing and patio areas. This will need careful management going forward with very secure boundaries required.

Overall, Trixie is settling in but is still very much finding her feet.

name: Sally
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a larger, resident male dog to help me settle in and I have met cats fine.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Sweet little Sally has come to us from a breeder to begin her search for a loving forever home. When she first arrived, she was understandably feeling a little worried to find herself here, but she has been trying so hard to be brave and has really started to come out of her shell.

Sally is growing into the funniest and cutest little dog, and for such a small girl she certainly has a big personality that is beginning to shine through. Her confidence continues to grow, and she now happily enjoys receiving fuss and attention from people she knows and trusts. She has also made lovely progress with her harness training. While this was initially a brand-new experience for her, she now walks happily on her harness with people she feels comfortable with and enjoys exploring by their side. As with everything, she will need a little time to build the same confidence with her new family.

Sally is a super little dog who is just waiting for someone to give her the time, patience and love she needs to continue building her confidence. With the right home and lots of kindness, we are sure she will blossom into a wonderful companion.

She will be looking for a calm, kind and understanding home with adopters who are around most of the time and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She has never lived in a home before, so everything about family life will be new to Sally. She will need gentle guidance as she learns the routines of home life, including house training and continuing to build her confidence in new situations.

Sally absolutely loves other dogs and gains a great deal of comfort from having canine friends around her. She will need another dog in her new home to help her feel secure, but she would prefer the company of a smaller male dog. Sally can be a little bossy with female dogs, so she is best suited to living with a male companion. She has also met a cat at the rescue and coped well (please see the video in her gallery!), so she could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

This sweet little girl just needs someone to give her the chance she deserves, and we are sure she will repay that love tenfold with her own blossoming confidence and affectionate nature.

Sally has a lick granuloma on her left front leg, which is healing, and an old scar on her left hip. She had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay and is currently being treated for bilateral conjunctivitis.

Sally has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Super little Sally is doing so well. I absolutely adore this lovely lady. She grows in confidence every day, and it really hasn’t taken her all that long to come out of her shell.

Sally still needs a little time with new people to feel safe, but she tries so hard, and once she feels comfortable with you, her funny personality shines through, from showing you her full-body rolls, to running over for gentle fusses, or scrambling all over you for foodie treats. I’m very proud of how hard she tries each day to be brave.

Today, Sally enjoyed another little walk around the rescue with her new kennel companion. Sally is by no means confident on the lead yet and will need gentle encouragement and patience to continue her learning journey and start to relax on her walks.

Sally looks to her kennel buddies for support, and her perfect home will already have a friendly (male) resident dog to help show her the way. Sally is best suited to a quiet, adult-only home, ideally with knowledge and/or experience of ex-breeding dogs.

Sally is just the growing into the funniest, cutest of little dogs. For a small being she has a big personality and it’s really starting to shine through. She grows ever confident, and happily takes fusses from me and today successfully begun harness training.

Sally is a super little dog just waiting for a loving home to help continue bringing her out of her shell. Sally will need a friend in her new home but prefers the company of smaller male dogs, she can be a bit bossy with female dogs and is best suited to an adult only home.

Sweet little Sally has come to us from a breeder to begin her search for a loving forever home. She is a very gentle girl who is understandably feeling a little worried to find herself here, but she is trying so hard to be brave.

Sally will gently approach you for a little sniff and is already showing what a sweet nature she has, she just needs time, patience and reassurance to help her confidence grow. With the right home and lots of kindness, we are sure she will blossom into a lovely companion.

She will be looking for a calm, kind and understanding home with adopters who are around most of the time and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. Everything in a home environment will be completely new to Sally, so she will need gentle guidance as she learns about everyday life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead.

Sally absolutely loves other dogs and gains a lot of comfort from them, so she will need at least one other kind and gentle resident dog in her new home to be her friend and show her the way. Sally will need a larger, male dog in her home and cannot live with females or smaller dogs.

This sweet girl just needs someone to give her the chance she deserves and she will repay your love tenfold.

Sally has a lick granuloma on her left front leg, which is healing and an old scar on her left hip. She has had an umbilical hernia repair at the time of her spay and is being treated for bilateral conjunctivitis.

name: Grape
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I’ve learnt how to walk on lead but its still a bit scary for me.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training.

Grape came into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was a very worried little girl who clearly hadn't experienced much human interaction and found the world an overwhelming place. Despite her fears, she always tried so hard to be brave, gently accepting strokes while she learned that people could be kind.

Size wise Grape weighs approximately 14.5 kg. She's a lovely medium-sized girl, around the size of a cocker spaniel.

Fast forward a few months, and Grape has come on in leaps and bounds. She still has a sensitive soul, but each day we see more of the happy, playful little girl she was always destined to be.

When Grape first arrived, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, she recently enjoyed a proper makeover to show off what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped brilliantly, and by the end she was a gorgeous fluffy princess, looking every bit as special as she is.

One of Grape's biggest achievements has been her growing confidence. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she isn't quite 100% confident yet, particularly with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

She absolutely adores other dogs and gets on wonderfully with every dog she meets. Their company gives her confidence, and because of this shewill need a kind, confident resident dogin her new home to help guide and reassure her as she continues to settle into family life. We recently caught Grape playing for the very first time, doing joyful little bounces around a tennis ball. It may seem like a small thing, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step away from the life she once knew.

Although she's still a little nervous about human fuss, she now greets us every morning with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. She's also a complete sucker for treats, making winning her over much easier! She is still learning about life in a home, so her new family will need to continue her house training, build her confidence, and help her discover all the joys of being a much-loved pet. A calm, patient home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs would suit her perfectly.

When Grape arrived she was a little overweight, but with a healthy diet and gentle exercise she has been making great progress. She has also been through quite a lot medically since arriving with us. She has been spayed, had two teeth extracted, undergone a hernia repair, and had a small cyst removed during her spay. Her hormonal alopecia should continue to improve following her spay, and she has also completed treatment for an ear infection.

We truly cannot understand why Grape has been overlooked for so long. She has blossomed into such a sweet, gentle little dog, and while she will need a family willing to continue building her confidence, the rewards of watching her flourish will be immeasurable.

Grape has been given the Gift of Life Wendy Stewart

Sweet, sensitive Grape has now been with us for around three months, and we honestly can't understand why she hasn't had floods of interest. She is such a lovely little dog who has come on in leaps and bounds since arriving at the rescue.

When Grape first came to us, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, we thought she deserved a proper makeover to show everyone what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped so well, and she was an absolute star with the dryer (apart from preferring us not to fuss around her head too much!). By the end, she was transformed into a gorgeous, fluffy little princess, ready to strut around the rescue.

It's not just her appearance that's blossomed. Grape has grown so much in confidence over the last few weeks. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she's still not 100% confident, especially with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

One of the loveliest things about Grape is how much she adores other dogs. She delights in every dog she meets and loves having canine friends around her. We even caught her playing for the very first time, doing playful little bounces around a tennis ball. It might seem like an ordinary moment, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step further away from the life she once knew.

She can still be a little nervous about human fuss, but every morning she greets us with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. Each day she lets her guard down a little more, and we're seeing more of the happy, playful girl she was always meant to be. She's also very partial to treats, which definitely helps when making new friends!

Grape would make a wonderful addition to almost any family that's happy to give her a little patience and understanding while she continues to build her confidence. We truly cannot understand why this gorgeous little girl has been overlooked for so long.

Grape is still a nervous girlie and is taking longer to trust humans, given we know nothing of her past this is understandable.

I am trying to show her that all I want to do is help her and show her love, while also respecting her space and going slowly with her, which is what her adopters may have to do depending on where’s she’s at.

She will allow a gentle fuss when she’s in her bed but will not willingly come up and ask for one yet. I think maybe in a calm home she will start to feel more comfortable, kennel life isn’t for everyone, and learn to trust humans.

She is a beautiful girl and I hope she starts to trust soon so we can see that amazing and sweet personality that I’m sure is hiding in her somewhere just bursting to come out.

Grape has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a scared girl who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and clearly isn't used to much human interaction, so finds this quite worrying at the moment. Despite her fears she will let you gently stroke her and is trying so hard to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace and would benefit from adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs. She gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Grape has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Everything will be new to her, so a calm and consistent routine will be important.

Grape has arrived a little overweight, but with a good diet and gentle exercise, she should soon start to shed the excess. She has some hormonal alopecia, but this should start to grow back now she has been spayed. She has had 2 teeth extracted as well as a hernia repair and our vets have noted she has a small cyst, which was removed at the time of her spay. She is also being treated for a ear infection.

Grape is a very worried little girl at the moment, but with time, patience, and the support of another dog, she has the potential to slowly gain confidence and begin to show more of her true character.

name: Indie
description:
I would like an understanding home, and I can live with older children, 10+

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Indie is a gentle, sensitive little Poodle who came into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. When she first arrived, people were very unfamiliar to her and she found handling quite worrying. Although she was always trying her best to be brave, she would often shy away from people and needed time to learn that the world wasn't such a scary place.

Since moving into foster, Indie has already made wonderful progress. Like many ex-breeding dogs, she initially found life in a home quite overwhelming. For the first few days she struggled to settle, pacing around the house and barking during the night. However, after about a week she began to relax, and she has now settled beautifully into her foster home, sleeping soundly through the night and becoming much more comfortable with everyday household life.

Each day her confidence continues to grow. Indie is naturally very curious and enjoys following her foster carer around the house to see what's happening, especially if there might be something tasty involved! She's a big foodie, happily takes treats from your hand and, although she can be a little fussy with her meals, she's found a food she absolutely loves.

She's also discovering how much fun life can be. Indie enjoys playing with toys and absolutely loved exploring a secure field, where her foster carer saw her playful personality really beginning to shine. She is making steady progress with lead training, although she still finds walking on a lead quite frightening, so her new family will need to continue building her confidence at her own pace.

Although Indie enjoys gentle strokes, she isn't quite brave enough to approach people asking for affection just yet. She prefers to be close to her people without too much physical contact and continues to become more comfortable as her trust grows.

Indie has done brilliantly with her toilet training and is now mostly reliable, following a routine and toileting outside consistently during the day, although does have a puppy pad out at night incase.

One thing that has remained constant throughout Indie's journey is just how much she relies on other dogs. She absolutely must have at least one kind, confident resident dog in her new home. Having another dog gives her reassurance, helps her understand home life and encourages her to be brave enough to try new things.

She has met both adult visitors and visiting children in foster and has coped well, remaining calm and happy to share their space, although she tends to not actively seek attention. She has met older children in her foster home, and we believe she could live with older, dog-savvy kids who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

Indie is currently living in foster with a cat, but she isn't comfortable around cats and prefers to avoid them, so she is looking for a cat-free home.

When left for short periods, Indie may be a little unsettled initially but settles again quickly. She can wear a harness and use a crate with gentle encouragement and reassurance, and although she can still be a little wary of handling, her confidence continues to improve every day.

Indie is looking for a calm, patient family who understand that confidence can't be rushed. She will need adopters who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, celebrate the little milestones and continue showing her that people can be kind.

She has already shown just how much she can blossom when she's given love, patience and understanding. We truly believe that, with the support of another dog and the right family beside her, Indie will continue to flourish into a wonderfully loyal and loving companion.

Indie has been given the Gift of Life by Kimberley Page

Indie found living in a home quite overwhelming for the first few days and struggled to settle and would pace around. She also struggled to settle at night and would bark and howl. After a week of being here she has now settled and the barking at night has stopped completely. She toilets outside consistently during the day but at night needs puppy pads.Indie is very curious and will follow me everywhere checking on what I’m doing and wondering if I’m going to give her something nice to eat (she’s a big foodie). She will take treats nicely from me and does eat well although she is quite fussy with her food. I have found a food she loves so will discuss this with adopter.Indie likes to play with toys and has really enjoyed going to the secure field where she really showed her true personality. I am working on walking on a lead with her but it is slow progress as she is still quite frightened.Indie likes to be stroked but isn’t quite brave enough to approach me to ask for it.Indie will need a home where someone is willing to work with her and give her the space and time she needs to settle. Someone who won’t overwhelm her and just let her progress at her own pace. I truly believe that in the right home she will make someone a wonderful companion.Indie is very reliant on other dogs so will need at least one other dog in her new home to help her come out of her shell

Indie is a gentle and worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. At the moment, she is not comfortable approaching people in her kennel and will often shy away from her handlers. She is still learning that people can be kind and trustworthy, and she finds handling difficult right now, sometimes showing that she is touch-sensitive.

Indie will need a patient and understanding home with adopters who are experienced with, or knowledgeable about, ex-breeding dogs and the challenges they can face when adjusting to life in a home environment. She can live with older teens, aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her the patience she needs. She will need time to settle at her own pace and should never be rushed.

She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home. A friendly canine companion will help her learn about home life, provide reassurance, and support her as she continues to build her confidence.

As Indie has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, gentle garden explorations may be the best way for her to experience the world while she gains confidence.

Indie is a timid girl who will need plenty of love, patience, and understanding from her adopters as she learns about trust, companionship, and all the comforts of family life. In the right home, given the time and support she needs, we believe she has every chance of blossoming into a happy and devoted companion.

name: Disco
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy children who respect my space

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

17-07-26 Disco is a sweet girl who has come into our care from a breeder. She really enjoys the company of other dogs and loves playing with her kennel friends and takes a lot of comfort from being around them. Disco is easy to handle and will happily approach us, although she is still a little timid while she gets to know people. Although she looks very Maltese she is a bigger girl at 9.2kg.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where she can settle in at her own pace and learn all about life as a cherished family member. We would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

Disco gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Disco has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, walking on a lead and harness, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her to settle at her own pace.

Disco is a gentle little girl with a playful side that shines through when she's with her doggy friends. With a patient family and a kind canine companion, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything her new life has to offer.

Disco has received treatment for conjunctivitis and has had one tooth extracted at the time of her spay. She has had a cyst drained from the top of her head, which our vets will continue to monitor. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her neck/chest area, which our vets diagnosed as a sialocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this, however, it is likely to gradually refill over the coming weeks or months and would need to be drained again if this happens. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Disco's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.

description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

19-07-26 Unity has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a very frightened little girl who is finding all the recent changes in her life overwhelming. Everything around her is new and unfamiliar, so she will need patient, understanding adopters who can help her discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Unity is looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the time, patience and commitment they need. She will thrive with a family who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, allowing her confidence to grow naturally without putting her under pressure.

Unity is a gentle, sensitive girl who has so much potential. With a loving, experienced family, a confident canine friend by her side and all the time she needs to settle, we are sure she will gradually blossom into the wonderful companion she was always meant to be.

description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am underweight and have some fur loss as well as sore skin.

He will now come you greet you and see if you have any tasty treats for him and will even enjoy a gentle tickle once he gets to know you.

Jonah is an incredibly sensitive soul who simply hasn't had the chance to experience the love and security every dog deserves. With patience, understanding, and a family willing to let him progress at his own pace, we believe he has every chance of learning to trust and becoming a wonderfully loyal companion.

Jonah has arrived to us extremely underweight, with some hair loss and what seems to be old cuts on his ears as well as some dermatitis, which is being treated. This boy needs plenty of TLC as he continues to grow.

description:

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

17-07-26 Danube has come into our care from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a lovely girl who enjoys the company of both people and other dogs. Danube is very easy to handle and is happy to approach us for a gentle fuss. She especially loves spending time with her kennel friends and clearly takes a lot of comfort from having them around.

She will be looking for a calm and loving home, where she can settle in at her own pace and begin to learn all about life as a much loved family member.

Danube relies on the company of her kennel friends for comfort, so she will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Danube has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, walking on a lead, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her the time and patience she needs as she adjusts to her new surroundings and discovers all the comforts of living in a home.

Danube is a gentle girl who has already shown us what a sweet nature she has. With a friendly canine companion by her side and a patient family to help her along the way, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.

Danube has been given the Gift of Life by Tracey Phillips

name: Tinkerbell
description:
I need an adult-only home with ex-breeder experience that can show me love.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe but I haven’t met cats yet so I'm not sure

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and has never lived in a home before, so she is understandably unsure and very sensitive to touch. She can go into panic mode if handled too quickly and may try to nip out of fear as she is simply terrified and trying to protect herself. The initial handling is what scares her most, so patience and slow, careful introductions are essential.

Since being with us, Tinkerbell has begun to settle into a routine and is starting to show very encouraging signs of progress. While she is still too worried to accept touch and may move away if approached, she is becoming more comfortable being around people she knows. She will now approach to sniff fingers, gently take treats, and has even started to offer little kisses, which is a lovely sign that she is beginning to build trust. She is also happy to relax nearby, often choosing to lie close by, which shows she is starting to feel a little safer in our presence.

Tinkerbell has made particularly good progress with being picked up. This used to be extremely stressful for her, but she is now becoming more tolerant of this with calm and gentle handling, which is a huge step forward for her.

She will still need a very experienced, adult-only home with people who have handled very scared or sensitive dogs before. Tinkerbell will also need a kind, confident resident dog to guide her and help her feel more secure. Her adopters will need to understand that she may never be a typical dog who seeks constant cuddles or fuss, but with patience, love, and gentle guidance, she can form a very special bond.

As she has never experienced home life, Tinkerbell will need continued support with house training and learning to walk on a lead. Starting with calm, gentle garden time will help her confidence as she gradually explores her new environment.

Tinkerbell was recently groomed and found the experience very stressful, so it will be important for her adopters to gently and patiently help her build positive associations through gradual desensitisation. She will need regular grooming to keep her comfortable, and her new family should be prepared to work with an experienced, understanding groomer or may need to look at having her groomed under sedation until she becomes more comfortable with this. She has been making regular trips to our grooming room to have a brush and the fur around her eyes trimmed and is getting better with this each time.

Tinkerbell is a very special girl who needs an equally special home willing to invest time, TLC, and understanding. With consistency, patience, and love, she has the potential to form a unique bond and thrive in a safe, nurturing environment.

This week at the rescue we’ve had a big heatwave which resulted in a lot of our dogs needing to be shaved, including my beautiful Tinkerbell as she started to struggle having quite a thick coat. She has the most beautiful fur and she keeps herself so clean and dry, but it had to come off for her comfort. She was taken into the vets to be sedated again, but only because the weather has been so warm.. it would have been too hot to put her through the stress of shaving her all off with no sedation. I have been taking her into the grooming room regularly to brush her and trim the hair around her eyes, and she does definitely get better and better each time, so this is a good sign!! The next time she’s due a shave, I will try again without taking her into the vets to see how she does.

Even though Tinks is still a nervous girl, especially around people she doesn’t know, she is still progressing slowly and steadily. She’s still very reliant on other dogs and tends to copy them a lot of the time, so this has been good for her learning to trust me. She’s watched so many other dogs come up to me for a fuss, take treats from me, and just be comfortable in general being around me, and she is following suit.. just at her own pace. And that’s okay!

She is SUCH a sweet girl who has clearly been through a lot, and it’s not her fault she has such a strong guard up. I absolutely adore working with her and I understand and accept her for who she is. Seeing her get excited over toys and treats, and greeting me with a waggy tail in the mornings really makes me smile, and it gives me hope for her future. She deserves adopters who will love and cherish her the way she always should have been, regardless of if the feelings are mutual.. but I do think she is capable of loving and trusting.. she just needs to find herself with the right people.

Over the last few weeks, our lovely Tinks has reached a huge milestone. After seeing how well she has been progressing with her handling, we felt it was time to take the next step — harness training.

For a dog who finds handling so worrying, we knew there was a strong chance she might not accept wearing a harness. But unless we try, we’ll never know.

Tinks’ other kennel mummy and I took her into the grooming room, where we carefully introduced and fitted her harness. As expected, she was a little unsure and understandably a bit overwhelmed, but she made us both incredibly proud with how she coped. The next step was returning her to her kennel to see how she would manage wearing it throughout the day. Many of our more worried dogs will freeze or refuse to move in this situation, but not our Tinks. She carried on with her day as normal, moving around comfortably with the harness on.

To some, this might not seem like a huge achievement, but for Tinkerbell, it is a massive step in the right direction. Over the coming weeks, we will continue to build on this by practicing daily, with the hope that we can eventually begin introducing a lead in the yard.

With a dog like Tinkerbell, progress takes time, patience, and understanding. Thankfully, she has all of that in abundance, and we will never give up on her.

Tinkerbell has settled into my routine at the rescue beautifully now, so I’m finally starting to see glimpses of the real her. Her guard is definitely still up, but it has dropped slightly and I can tell she’s a lot more comfortable being around me than she used to be. She still won’t allow me to touch her and will bolt away if I go towards her, but she’s approaching me to sniff my fingers, sometimes give me kisses, and taking treats from me every single day now. She also feels content enough to lay near me when I’m sat in the yard eating my lunch, often with her back towards me which I guess is a sign that she does trust me!

One thing she has improved massively with is being picked up. I mentioned in my last update I still had to use a thick blanket and she would still sometimes try to bite (just not as often), but that’s even better again now. This week I was able to pick her up with no blanket, which is HUGE for Tinks!!

Because of how much better she had gotten, I thought I would attempt a full groom - going into it with absolutely no expectations. She allowed me to shave her back, but that’s as far as we could get. She started to get more and more stressed and I really didn’t want to push her and ruin the work we’ve done, so I took her into the vets so she could be sedated to complete the groom. So, she’s now shaved (minus her INCREDIBLE eyelashes), and I think she looks absolutely beautiful. Now that we’ve started fresh with her coat, I’m going to start taking her into the grooming room just once a week or so, and gently brush her etc to get her more used to it all.

Tinkerbell has made slow and steady progress since she’s been on my section and I’m so proud of how brave she’s trying to be. I can tell she wants to come out of her shell a bit more and join in with the rest of the dogs, but she’s not there just quite yet. Something big did happen last week though!! During dinner time I was hand feeding one of her friends, and Tinks came over and started licking the food off my hand for the first time!!!! I was absolutely over the moon and so happy that she felt comfortable enough to do that. Since then she’s done it nearly every day and has also started to take treats from me too if they’re yummy enough. I know this probably won’t sound like a lot to most people, but for a dog like Tinberbell it’s huge. For me, taking food from my hand is usually the first step in earning trust with my scared dogs, so I think we’re heading in the right direction.

We have also made a small amount of progress with Tinkerbell’s fear of being picked up. She still doesn’t like it - at all - but she’s not panicking as much any more and definitely doesn’t try to bite me as much as she did before. I still have to use a thick blanket and be very slow and calm with her, but I think she is starting to slowly realise that I’m not going to hurt her. I trimmed her fringe again a few days ago as her hair seems to grow quite quickly, so I took this opportunity to stroke her head gently for a little while once I was done. She actually started to close her eyes after a minute or so and I think she may have been enjoying it, or at least I hope she was.I adore this little lady and I’m going to do everything I can to show her what love and kindness is. I just hope a special someone will come along and feel the same way about her soon.

Tinkerbell has recently been moved to my section, as she struggles a great deal with being touched and handled by us humans. At present, she goes into complete panic mode whenever I go to pick her up, and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog at all; she’s literally just so scared she will do anything she can to stop it happening. Once I have her comfortably in my arms, she will actually settle really well and will allow me to do things such as give her a gentle fuss and trim the hair on her face. I think the initial picking up is what scares her the most so this is what we’ll work on slowly together.

Tinkerbell is going to need a very experienced home with people who have had terrified dogs before. She’s going to need a lot of work and TLC put into her, and also a lot of understanding. Her adopters will need to accept the fact that she may never be a normal dog, and she may never be a dog who wants fusses or cuddles, but love her anyway. She’s a very special girl, and she needs a home equally as special to help her and give her what she needs.

I’m going to work as closely as I can with her over the next couple of weeks, and hopefully I can earn her trust and prove to her that she doesn’t need to be afraid of me. I’ll keep you all updated!

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and can be a little unsure at first. She is touch-sensitive and may need time to feel comfortable, but once she calms down, she begins to show her gentle, sweet side. Tinkerbell will need an adult-only home that can handle her sassy personality and provide the patience she needs to settle in at her own pace.

She will also need a kind and confident resident dog to guide her and take her under their wing as she adjusts. Tinkerbell is looking for someone to teach her about trust, companionship, and the joys of home life.

As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be gentle and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Starting with a few gentle garden sniffs will be perfect for her confidence as she begins to explore her new world.

Tinkerbell is a little gem who, with time and love, will grow into a devoted and affectionate companion.

name: Uma
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy children who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk on a harness and would enjoy a daily walk when settled in to my new home.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

18-07-26 Uma is a gorgeous girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She can be a little shy when you first meet her, but it doesn't take long before her playful side begins to appear. After a few minutes, she'll often invite you to play with a sweet little play bow. Uma enjoys gentle handling and is happy to take treats from our hands, although she does appreciate people taking things slowly when picking her up. Her favourite thing is to sit right next to you for fusses

Uma loses confidence when she is away from her doggy friends, so she will need another kind and confident resident dog in the home to help her feel safe and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in. She has a lovely fun personality that's just waiting to come out. We would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

As Uma has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, practice her skills walking, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she adjusts to her new surroundings and discovers everything that home life has to offer.

Uma has arrived slightly overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home.

Uma is a real sweetheart with so much potential. She's already showing us glimpses of the happy, playful dog she is, and with the support of another dog and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow.

Uma has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Davies

name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

22-07-26 Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is an amazing girl who is full of joy, character, and energy! She absolutely loves people, enjoys giving kisses, and is always ready for a cuddle. She has a wonderful, affectionate nature and thrives on human company.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home, as she much prefers having all the attention to herself. She is happy to walk past other dogs but enjoys having her own space. She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over. She also needs a home without cats.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine. She walks well on the lead and will need an active home that can provide her with plenty of adventures and mental stimulation.

As a Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop's new family should have some experience with these breeds and understand their intelligent, active nature. She will thrive with owners who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive outlets for her energy.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give and will make a fantastic addition to a loving, active home.

name: Carry
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & have a Grade 3 patella luxation in my right hind leg.

Carry is a sweet and gentle girl who came to us from a breeder looking for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very scared and unsure of people, but she has already made wonderful progress and is continuing to grow in confidence since moving into foster care.

Carry has settled well into life in a home and is taking all the sights and sounds of everyday living in her stride. She sleeps soundly with the other dogs in the lounge each night and has settled into a good routine, although she is quite happy to let her foster carer know when she thinks it's time to start the day! She has a great appetite, happily accepts treats from your hand, and has been generally clean in the house.

Carry is still nervous of being touched and will often run away if someone tries to fuss her. However, she is becoming much braver and will now happily approach to sniff hands. If she is relaxing on a dog bed or in a smaller space where she feels safe, she is beginning to tolerate gentle fusses. She is trying so hard to be brave, and it has been lovely to watch her confidence slowly grow.

Carry relies heavily on other dogs for reassurance and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her forever home. They will help guide her through new experiences and continue to build her confidence as she settles into family life. She has also started taking her first steps with lead training and recently allowed her foster carer to attach a lead to her collar and enjoy a little walk around the garden, with plenty of encouragement and a generous supply of squeezy cheese!

She has also discovered the joy of playing with soft toys and can often be found happily throwing them around and giving them a good shred. Seeing her playful side emerge has been a wonderful milestone and shows just how much she is beginning to relax.

Carry will be looking for a calm and understanding home with resident dog companions and patient adopters who are happy to let her progress entirely at her own pace. We feel she could live with older, dog-savvy children who understand that she will need time and space to build trust. As she is in a foster home, she is beginning to learn about home life. But her adopters will need to continue helping her with house training, lead walking, and all the other adventures that family life brings.

Carry is an adorable little girl who is trying so hard to overcome her fears. She brightens the day of everyone who meets her, and with continued patience, kindness, and reassurance, we know she will continue to blossom into a happy and trusting companion.

Our vets have noted that Carry has a Grade 3 patella luxation in her right hind leg. This is not causing her any issues at present and may improve with gentle exercise, but it will need to be monitored by her adopters and their veterinary team. Should treatment be required in the future, this condition would not be covered by insurance.

Carry has been given the Gift of Life by Wendy Bowen

Carry has begun to settle into life in a home, she is accepting of the sights and sounds of home life. She sleeps well with the others in the lounge, but let's me know when she thinks I ought to get up, about 6.30.

Carry eats well, accepts treats from my hand and is generally clean in the house.Carry will come up to me and sniff my hands but runs away if I try to fuss her. If she is sitting on a bed or in a smaller area, she is starting to tolerate gentle fuss. She is trying so hard to be brave. Today she did allow me to attach a lead to her collar and have a walk round the garden aided by squeezy cheese!! She is starting to play with soft toys, ripping them and tossing them about, so lovely to see.

Carry will need a home with a resident dog/s, older children and adopters who are happy to go at her pace. She is an adorable girl and deserves the best

I’m lucky enough to get to work with Carry twice a week whilst her kennel mum is off for the weekend, and every week I get to spend with her the more in confidence she grows!Carry is such a character, and everyday she shows you how much she is blossoming and how much she appreciates feeling safe & loved. She absolutely loves cuddling up to her kennel friends, and tearing it up in the yard and the kennel. Her one true love is toys, and as long as you have toys around you needn’t worry if she is happy or satisfied!!We recently took Carry out on a harness for the first time, and as a beginner we think she smashed it. She didn’t freak out, and simply followed the lead of her kennel mum & another dog by her side. We think with another few more goes she will be enjoying her small adventures in no time. Carry broke up the walk with a few stops for some squeezey cheese which she simply couldn’t say no to!Carry is such an adoring girl, and watching her flourish infront of our eyes is so beautiful to watch. A loving family, a resident dog, and lots of understanding is all she needs, and she’ll be ready to take on the world, day by day & little by little.

Carry is coming out of her shell more and more every day and is now a very happy and lively girl who always has a waggy tail. She’s discovered toys and is learning how to play with them which she’s really enjoying, and she’s also turning into a massive foodie which is always very helpful with nervous dogs. She is still hand shy and will run away if I go towards her, but she’s extremely curious and always likes to be close to me watching what I’m doing. She’s happy to approach me to give me lots of sniffs and to take treats from my hand, so we’re definitely moving in the right direction and I really don’t think it’s going to be long until she starts to accept gentle fusses.

Carry is the type of dog that can put a smile on your face even on the darkest of days, and she really is a joy to work with and be around. In a home environment where she has lots of time with her new parents, I think she’ll absolutely blossom. She probably will be nervous at first of course, so as long as her adopters are patient with her and work with her through her worries and fears, I think it will work out so well.

I haven’t started harness training with Carry yet as she hasn’t been on my section for that long, but I do feel as though she may be ready to start exploring it soon. So, over the next couple of weeks I’ll get one fitted to her and see how she does. I’ll keep you all updated!

Carry is a sweet, gentle girl who has come to us from a breeder and is currently very scared, timid, and unsure of humans. She will need plenty of time, patience, and TLC in her new home to help her learn to trust and build a loving bond with her family. Once she gets to know you, she will approach you for a fuss but she isn't comfortable being picked up at the moment as this is very new for her.

Carry will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She relies on other dogs for comfort and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home. A canine companion will provide her with reassurance and help guide her as she learns about home life, giving her someone to lean on as her confidence grows.

As Carry has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be understanding while she learns the basics, such as house training and walking on a lead. The big wide world may feel overwhelming for her at first, so starting with calm, gentle experiences, like exploring the garden will help her gradually gain confidence.

With love, patience, and understanding, Carry has all the potential to blossom into a happy and trusting companion.

Our vets have noted that Carry has a Grade 3 patella luxation in her right hind leg, this isn't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise but it will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vets and should she need any treatment in the future it wouldn't be coverable by insurance.

name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am a beginner on the lead but I'm not ready for walks yet.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who was understandably overwhelmed when she first arrived and desperately needed kindness, patience and TLC as she began to settle and learn that the world could be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialled on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a typical dog.

Since moving to a new section of the rescue, Nora has made huge leaps in her confidence. She is now harness trained and happily wears her harness throughout the day. She has become much more comfortable with handling and confidently walks on her harness to and from the exercise yard. Although she is not yet ready to venture out on walks beyond the rescue, she is making steady progress and becoming braver every day. Another wonderful milestone is that she now chooses to sit at the front of her kennel, curiously watching people and dogs come and go, rather than hiding away at the back as she once did.

Since arriving with us, Nora has slowly begun to show glimpses of the gentle and affectionate dog she has the potential to become. Like many nervous dogs, she can be vocal when she feels unsure, and her deep, defensive howl is very much in keeping with her Beagle heritage. However, with patience and a calm approach, she soon settles and begins to reveal her softer side.

Although Nora is still learning to feel comfortable around people, she is making wonderful progress. She is beginning to choose to settle near her carers and, once she has had time to relax, becomes much more accepting of gentle interaction. In these quieter moments she happily allows us to stroke and handle her, which is a huge achievement for a dog who once found every interaction so overwhelming.

It is clear that Nora's worries stem not from a dislike of people, but from uncertainty. Having had such limited life experiences, she simply does not yet understand who we are or what to expect from us. As her confidence grows, she becomes increasingly willing to be approached and reassured, and each small step forward is a testament to her resilience.

Nora would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. She will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. We believe that what Nora needs most now is the stability, security and reassurance that only a loving home can provide.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence. While Nora has successfully shared her kennel with smaller dogs, we feel she would be happiest living alongside a dog of a similar size or larger.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She is now comfortable wearing a harness and walking around the rescue grounds, but she is not yet ready to explore the outside world. Her adopters will need to continue building her confidence gradually, beginning with familiar surroundings before introducing new places at a pace she is comfortable with.

Although Nora is still a sensitive and sometimes worried little girl, the progress she has made has been nothing short of remarkable. Beneath her fears is a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a dog like Nora slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences imaginable, and with love, patience and understanding, we know she will continue to blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every step of that journey worthwhile.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.
