name: Nuzzle
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with a dog my size or larger. I'm fine with cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have a Grade 1-2 heart murmur and have had 2 teeth extracted.

Nuzzle is a truly gentle, special little girl who has already come so far on her journey. She originally came to us from a breeder and, after a short adoption, sadly found her way back to the rescue as it was not the right fit for her. While in the home, she did make progress, but she was fearful of the man in the household and reacted out of fear on two occasions, showing that she needs very understanding, experienced adopters. She is now in a foster home where one of her fosterers is male and has settled in beautifully, which shows great progress for her.

When Nuzzle first arrived with us, she was an extremely nervous and flighty soul, spending most of her time hiding at the back of her kennel, too scared to join in or even accept touch. The world felt overwhelming, being in the yard, meeting people, or simply being handled was terrifying for her, and she lived in a constant state of panic and flight.

Since then, the transformation in Nuzzle has been truly heart‑warming. With patience, kindness, routine, and consistency, she has slowly begun to blossom. She now approaches her carers for gentle fusses and, when she feels safe, will even ask for more. She enjoys being groomed and is walking nicely on the lead.

She shared her kennel well with other dogs of a similar size and is now in a foster home where she is getting along well with the other dogs in the home. Nuzzle thrives when she has another kind, confident dog by her side and will need a resident dog, her size or larger, in her new home for emotional support and confidence-building. She can bond quite closely with her doggy friends and can get quite protective of them, so may prefer to be homed with just one other resident dog who can be her bestie. She is in foster with cats and is fine with them so could potentially live with a dog savvy cat.

Nuzzle is not a dog for busy or noisy environments and will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be patient, gentle, and consistent, allowing her to progress at her own pace.

Despite her fears, Nuzzle is a sweetheart who adores comfort, routine, and affection. She enjoys cosy beds, soft fuss, tasty treats, and the safety of familiar people and dogs. She is house trained and really enjoys the comfort of home life.

From a medical point of view, Nuzzle has a Grade 1–2 heart murmur which does not currently require treatment but should be monitored by a vet. She has had two teeth removed when she was spayed, and she also has a fatty lump on her side which currently requires no action.

Nuzzle has already achieved so much and continues to surprise everyone with her courage and gentle nature. She has incredible potential and, in the right home with the right support, she will continue to grow in confidence and trust. She is a quiet, affectionate companion who simply wants a safe, loving place where she can feel secure and cherished.

With the right family who will celebrate every small step and understand her past, Nuzzle will flourish beautifully and become a deeply rewarding companion.

Today I've had a very busy day. I'm so tired that, as I'm typing this, I'm falling asleep.

I've been for a walk with my foster brother, and it wasn't our usual walk, so I had lots of new smells and sights to check out. Afterwards, we both went to my foster brother's groomer, and I had another groom. I was so good and looked beautiful afterwards (as always!).

Then we visited Foster Nanny, where I had a treat and got to test out her sofa.

Nuzzle recently went out with her foster parents to visit some friends and was such a good girl. She happily accepted treats from everyone, enjoyed playing in the garden, and had a lovely time with their little dog, Beau. She was a little nervous when their friends' sister and her husband arrived, but after a little time she found the confidence to let them give her a gentle fuss.

Nuzzle is such a lovely little girl who continues to make fantastic progress in foster care. She has become much more confident with her foster dad and now happily jumps up onto the sofa for cuddles with both him and his wife. She is house trained and is walking very nicely on the lead in quiet areas while she continues to build her confidence.

Today was my first grooming day with my foster brother. As my foster brother was due to be groomed my new foster parents thought they would treat me to one too and I was so brave and good. Although I wasn't very keen on the dryer and I'm still not very keen on being picked up, I did so well. Now everyone says I look so beautiful and fluffy!

Little Nuzzle has been with us for week now and it brings me to one question, and that question is why has this little darling not got a forever home already?She really is a little star from day one she has been nothing but a pleasure to foster. Her toilet training is 100% (only one accident on the first day she came), she gets on well with all the other dogs here and also gets on well with our cats. She's had 4 other dogs visit and was fine with them also.She sleeps well throughout the night, eats well, loves treats and will take them out of your hand. She walks on a lead with encouragement in quiet areas. She will allow you to fuss her but can be a little hand shy when putting on her harness and lead so does need vocal encouragement.Nuzzle is looking for preferably an adult only home with at least one other fur baby to help her continue with living her best life. Potential adopters must also be aware of her grooming needs.

Nuzzle is desperately missing her home comforts and I think she would love nothing more than to be back in a warm, cosy house. The weather at the rescue has been SO bad over the past couple of months and even though her kennel is set up like a palace because she’s so good, it’s still not the same as a home. She ADORES being snuggled up in bed and it’s definitely her happy place. I can only imagine how grateful she’ll be once she’s back on a sofa. We can dream!!!

This sweet girl completely has my heart and is breaking it at the same time. I cannot emphasise enough how easy she is to look after at the rescue. She quite literally doesn’t put a paw out of place in any aspect. She keeps her kennel and herself sparkling clean, she runs to and from the yard and back to her kennel perfectly every time, she shares everything including food and toys with her friends, and she’s easy to bath and groom. From the perspective of a kennel mum, she’s pretty perfect.

Her best friend got adopted a couple of weeks ago and she has been a little quieter since, but she now has a new kennel friend that she cuddles with a lot and has taken a shine to. I would so love for her to find her forever brother or sister soon because it would make her so happy to have a constant soulmate in her life.

Nuzzle has been back at the rescue for just over a month now and I have to say it’s been an absolute pleasure to look after her. She was on my section the first time she was here over a year ago and it’s been so lovely to see the difference in her. She was a very, very frightened girl back then and extremely panicky all the time. She was basically living in flight mode and it was so hard to have to watch. When she arrived back last month I was SO surprised when she approached me to ask for a little fuss on the first day. That is definitely not the same dog I knew!!

For the first couple of weeks I left her to decompress and settle back into my routine, and thankfully she did this pretty quickly. Since then, we’ve been doing lots of harness practice and she’s doing SO well. She’s been so much of a good influence that she’s even helped her best friend Denise learn how to walk too - so now they go out together on little strolls up the road and back. She’s still not perfect and won’t be up for going for big hikes anytime soon, but she’s getting better every day.

Her favourite thing in the world is being snuggled up in the back of her kennel under a heat lamp. She has a huge donut bed which she shares with Denise and you’ll find her tucked in for the majority of the day. They often enjoy a dental stick each while in the donut bed too, and it’s so sweet to watch!!

Nuzzle has SO much potential and I am so certain that in the right home with adopters who know what they’re doing with ex-breeders, she will thrive. She’s come such a long way and I know she has more to give, so please give her a chance soon.

She also has a fatty lump on her side which requires no action currently.

name: Arthur
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I am in foster with a cat!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I would love plenty of adventures once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

Please read below for more information about my health!

21-07-26 We are so happy to be able to introduce you to Arthur!

Arthur is a gorgeous lurcher who arrived to us under tragic circumstances. We received a call from the police, who asked us to help, Arthur’s owner had passed away, leaving him alone in the house, for an unknown amount of time. We quickly arranged for him to be collected by our staff and got Arthur safely to the centre.

Upon arrival, it was clear that Arthur was suffering from heatstroke; it was peak heatwave, and we had no idea when he last had a drink. He could barely stand and was immensely stressed. He was immediately seen to by our vets and he was placed on a drip. His kidney values were not good, and we were preparing for the worst.

However, there was something about Arthur, a little sparkle in his eye that told us his journey wasn’t finished… and so began his recovery!

Many hours on a drip, his bloods improved, slowly but steadily. Each day we saw a glimpse of his wonderful personality come out, but he simply would not eat. He was syringe fed diligently through day and night, offered so many platters of food.. we just knew that while his bloods continued to improve, we just needed to find the one thing to tempt him.. and over 2 weeks later we cracked it, starting with one particular brand of finest ham (no he didn’t like the cheap versions!!). Over a few days, that developed into getting him to eat proper food, he has flourished since then.

Throughout this whole process, Arthur has been a beaming light of joy. He took absolutely everything in his stride; being poked and prodded, syringe fed, etc. and still he greeted us with happiness and tail wags every time we saw him.

Once Arthur was stable, he was taken into foster by a staff member, where again he has been the perfect gentleman. He is has been mostly chilled in the home, follows his fosterer everywhere and loves a cuddle on the sofa! He loves a ball and will occasionally play by himself, watching him throw a toy up the air and catch it is brilliant entertainment!

What Arthur loves most is his walks: he knows how handsome he is and wants to say hello to everyone! He can get a bit excited when he sees dogs or cats, but is very sweet about it and just wants to play. He walks wonderfully on the lead and isn’t strong. Arthur can live as an only dog, or with other gentle dogs (pending a meet and greet). He could also live with older, dog-savvy, gentle children. He is in foster with a cat who he is fine with, so may be able to be homed with a dog savvy cat.

Although Arthur has shown as an incredible recovery compared with how he arrived, his bloods do still show some kidney damage. This could be ongoing and he will need regular monitoring with an adopters vet to ensure he stays comfortable. Arthur also has a “wonky” gait and uneven hips, we think this could be due to a previous injury. His gait has improved during his time with us and we hope that this would continue to improve in the home with exercise. His adopters will need to be aware of these conditions as they may not be covered by insurance.

Arthur has become a firm favourite with all of us here at Many Tears and we cannot wait to give him the happily ever after he deserves.

name: Nana
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a large male resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have some hormonal alopecia, but this should grow back. Read below for more!

Nana has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a sweet girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment and she is very nervous of being handled. We will continue gently helping her learn that human hands can be kind. If pushed out of her comfort zone, she may panic and choose to make the wrong decision, so it's important her adopters take things slowly with her.

Nana will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust. She can be quite vocal when she first meets you, but she is quick to make friends when you offer her some tasty treats.

She relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance, so Nana will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure. She gets along better with larger male dogs and so would need a larger male resident dog in her new home and cannot live with female dogs.

As Nana has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who will be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness, first practicing in the garden as she builds confidence.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nana will begin to leave the past behind her and let her true personality shine through.

Nana has some hormonal alopecia, but this should start to grow back once she has been spayed. She has a small inguinal hernia that has been repaired and has had several teeth removed at the time of her spay.

Nana has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

Millie is still a very worried girl who needs plenty of time and patience, but she is making gentle progress every day.

Millie spends much of her day relaxing in her favourite safe spot in the garden, where she feels most comfortable. She is still nervous around people and can become submissive when she is unsure, often lying down while she works out that she is safe. However, she is beginning to build trust with her foster carer and will now come over when called, lying down to allow a gentle fuss once she feels comfortable. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to help keep her safe while she settles.

Since moving into foster, Elana has settled in beautifully. She is a stunning girl with the sweetest nature. On arrival, she trotted straight into the kitchen, gently greeted all of the resident small dogs, and soon found herself a cosy dog bed where she was happy to relax and watch home life going on around her. She enjoys observing everything around her and is becoming more comfortable each day. She can still be wary if people approach her too quickly for a fuss and may choose to move away, so she will need adopters who are happy to let her build trust at her own pace.

She absolutely loves other dogs and really enjoys their company. Elana has spent her life living in a rural setting, mostly off lead, and has had very little experience of people outside of those she already knew. Because of this, strangers can still be quite worrying for her, but having confident canine companions gives her reassurance.

Elana has also started lead walking and is travelling well in the van to the secure exercise field. She enjoys having a run around, although she is currently a little less confident in large open spaces. With time and encouragement, we think she will soon learn to enjoy these adventures even more.

Although she was not used for breeding, she will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand the background she has come from. Elana will need another kind and confident dog in the home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system as she settles into family life and continues to build her confidence. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who will provide her with a calm and understanding home.

Elana has lived in a home before, so she is familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. She sleeps quietly all night in the kitchen, is crate trained, and is happy to be left alone for sensible periods. She is a quiet girl who isn't a barker and has discovered that she is rather fond of her treats! She may still need some help with house training and lead walking as she continues to settle into her new routine. She will also need an extra secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to help keep her safe.

Elana is a truly gorgeous girl who we think will adapt wonderfully to family life if given the time and patience she deserves. With kind adopters, a confident canine friend by her side, and plenty of understanding, we have no doubt she will continue to blossom into a lovely companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Wanda
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning all about wearing a harness and lead in foster.

I've done very well learning house training in my foster home.

I have been spayed & have had 13 teeth removed!

Wanda came to us from a breeder in search of the loving forever home she has always deserved. Like many ex-breeding dogs, she was a little worried when she first arrived and found all the changes in her life quite overwhelming. However, it didn't take long for her sweet nature to shine through.

Since moving into foster, Wanda has adapted wonderfully to home life. After a slightly shy start, she quickly realised that people could be kind and has settled beautifully into her foster home. She has fitted in perfectly with the resident dogs and has proven herself to be a truly lovely little companion.

Wanda absolutely loves the company of other dogs and is currently living happily alongside three Cockapoos. She enjoys playing with them, loves joining in with the zoomies and takes great comfort from having canine friends around her. Because of this, she will need at least one kind, confident resident dog in her forever home to continue giving her reassurance and companionship.

She has embraced home life incredibly well. Wanda is house trained, sleeps soundly through the night and has even claimed a cosy spot on her foster carer's bed. Around the home she's an easy little girl to live with, happily pottering about before settling down for a snooze. Her foster carer describes her as "an amazing guest" who has caused no trouble at all.

Wanda is beginning to learn all about the world beyond the home too. She is getting used to wearing a soft harness and has started her lead-walking journey, taking everything at her own pace. She's also enjoying visits to secure dog fields where she can continue to build her confidence through positive experiences.

She has a wonderfully gentle nature and has been a pleasure to care for. She eats well, although following extensive dental work she enjoys her food with a little added water and would benefit from using a slow-feeder bowl. She has also been beautifully behaved for bathing and grooming, taking everything in her stride.

When Wanda arrived with us, she underwent a full dental alongside her spay and had 13 teeth removed, having already lost another 10 teeth before arriving at Many Tears. Despite this, she eats well and doesn't let it stop her enjoying life.

Wanda is looking for a calm, patient home with adopters who understand the needs of ex-breeding dogs and will continue helping her discover all the joys of family life. She could live with sensible, dog-savvy older teenagers aged 16+ who will allow her to continue settling at her own pace.

Wanda is an incredibly sweet little girl with a kind, gentle personality. She's already shown just how well she can adapt when she's given love, patience and reassurance, and we have no doubt she'll make a wonderful companion for one very lucky family.

Wanda has been given the Gift of Life by Lauren Hyslop

Wanda arrived with hope and Wanda and has adapted well into our household with 3 cockapoos both male and females. She was a little shy at first but then she realised we were kind she is house trained and sleeps all through the night upstairs on my bed . She’s such a sweetheart with a kind nature she’s fitting in perfectly she’s eating well and will benefit from a slow feeder bowl we add a little water as she’s had 13 teeth removed and 10 others gone before arriving at many tears . She’s easy to bath clip . She mixes well and is playful with my 3 and gets the zoomies which is hilarious. She’s just learning to walk on a soft harness and tonight we’re off to a dog field we have booked. She’s been an amazing guest and she’s no trouble at all she potters around then settles and sleeps . She’s a little princess.

Wanda has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling a little worried and nervous at the moment and is understandably finding all the changes in her life rather overwhelming. However, if you spend some time with her she does begin to seek out a gentle fuss, although she is still unsure about being handled. With plenty of love, patience and kindness, we think this sweet little girl will soon begin to come out of her shell.

Wanda is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who will allow her to settle in at her own pace and help her build her confidence. She gains comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and take her under their wing.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be new to Wanda and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with new skills such as house training and will also need to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, with plenty of encouragement and positive experiences to help her gain confidence. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Wanda is a lovely little girl who simply needs a family willing to give her the time and reassurance she deserves. In return, we are sure she will reward them with a lifetime of love and companionship as she blossoms into the happy little dog she was always meant to be. She has had 13 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

name: Kira
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now spent a week in foster care and has made lovely progress. Her first day was understandably overwhelming, and she spent hours pacing around the garden, too frightened to come into the house. However, with patience and reassurance, she has already started to settle into her new routine.

Kira has grown in confidence over the past week and now happily follows her foster carer around the house, enjoying being nearby. She is curious about what is going on around her and is no longer fazed by everyday household noises. Although she is still a little shy, she will happily sniff an outstretched hand, gently take treats, and accept a little fuss as people pass by, even if she doesn't actively seek attention just yet. It seems that chicken is certainly the way to Kira's heart!

Kira has a healthy appetite and would happily help herself to the resident dogs' meals if given the opportunity! She enjoys the company of the other dogs and has even started joining in with their excited races up the garden whenever they spot a squirrel, although she's still learning exactly how the game works. She hasn't shown much interest in toys yet and hasn't quite discovered the sofa, but we are sure these milestones will come in time as her confidence continues to grow.

She has been wonderfully clean in the house from the very beginning, helped by having easy access to the garden, and she sleeps soundly through the night. However, she may some reminders of this in her new home. She is also happy wearing a harness, and her foster carers will soon begin introducing lead walking once she is ready.

Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can continue to blossom at her own pace. She will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. Her coat is also beginning to grow back nicely where she had alopecia, and she is looking healthier every day.

In the right home, we believe this gentle little girl has every chance of becoming a wonderful and devoted companion. With kindness, patience, and plenty of tasty chicken treats, Kira's future is looking brighter every day.

Kira has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

After a week in Foster Kira has made good progress. She found her first day here overwhelming and spent hours pacing the garden too frightened to come into the house.

A week later what a difference she now shadows her Foster Carer, is curious but not phased by household noises. Kira has a good appetite but given the chance will move in on the resident dogs food bowls.

She sleeps through the night and has been clean in the house from the start, helped by the back door always being open. Chicken is the way to win over the heart of this gentle little girl. She happily wears her harness and we will start lead training in the coming days. Kira will sniff a hand, take treats and accept a little fuss in passing but does not seek attention.

She has started joining in on squirrel alert racing up the garden with my girls but doesn’t understand the rules of the game. She has not shown any interest in toys and has not jumped up onto the sofa yet, Kira is not using a crate.

Kira’s coat is starting to grow back where she has alopecia.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. At the moment, she is feeling quite unsure of her surroundings and will often stand completely still when approached, as she is still learning to feel safe and confident.However, after spending some time with her, Kira begins to relax and will even give a little tail wag, showing that beneath her shy exterior is a lovely girl who wants to trust. With patience, kindness, and understanding, we are confident that she will continue to come out of her shell.Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace without any pressure. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, gentle garden explorations may be a great way for her to build confidence and start experiencing the world around her.Kira will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. In the right home, we believe this sweet girl has every chance of blossoming into a wonderful and devoted companion.

name: Luca
description:
I'd like an active home and enjoy human company!

I’d like to be the only dog in the home. I can't live with cats or small furries!

I will need a large secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! I have had 1 tooth extracted.

Luca is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. He already knows his name very well, so his new adopters should keep this the same to avoid confusing him as he settles into his new life.

Luca was previously used as a fake security dog and spent most of his life living outdoors, but beneath his impressive appearance is a real softie. He is easy to handle and genuinely enjoys human company, although he understandably found kennel life quite stressful when he first arrived and would often pace his kennel and the exercise yard, struggling to settle.

As Luca has become familiar with the routine, his surroundings and the staff at Many Tears, his confidence has grown enormously. One of the biggest changes we've seen is his newfound love of toys. For the first couple of weeks, he showed no interest in them at all, but now he absolutely adores them! His favourite game is a good game of fetch in the big yard, where he happily charges after his ball with great enthusiasm.

Like many large, playful dogs, Luca can occasionally become overexcited during play. He may jump up to catch the ball or become a little mouthy in his excitement, but this is never intended to cause harm. He is an incredibly gentle boy who simply gets carried away having fun. Because of his size and strength, we are helping him learn commands such as "sit", "wait" and "drop", as well as encouraging calmer play so he can enjoy himself without becoming overstimulated. This training will be important for his future adopters to continue, as an overexcited Luca could unintentionally knock over someone who is less steady on their feet.

Although he loves chasing a ball, Luca's absolute favourite toys are cuddly toys! He delights in carrying them around and showing off his softer side, which perfectly sums up his character.

Luca would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can enjoy all the attention, settle into a routine and build a strong bond with his new family. He will need adopters who have plenty of time to spend with him and who have experience of the breed or similar breeds. Luca cannot live with cats, small furries or small dogs.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life. With patient guidance and consistency, we are sure he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts that a family home has to offer.

Luca already walks on a lead, although he can pull initially, so this is something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an active, intelligent boy who would love a home where he can enjoy plenty of adventures, enrichment and quality time with his people. He is also a strong dog who can jump and even open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who can safely manage his strength.

Luca is an affectionate, loyal and wonderfully characterful boy who simply wants to be part of the family. Now that he has settled and his playful personality has begun to shine, it has been a joy to watch him embrace life. In the right home, with structure, ongoing training and plenty of love, Luca will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had one tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.

Luca has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Before they arrive at Many Tears, many of our dogs have never had toys, and, as strange as it sounds, may not know what to do with them. Fetching, licking, and chewing are important forms of enrichment for dogs and can help to regulate their nervous system and reduce stress, but it can take a while for these dogs to figure out how to use toys in these ways. It's one of the reasons many of our dogs are recommended to have a resident dog at home, as they can learn from each other.

When Luca arrived, he did not engage with toys for the first two weeks or so. He was also very anxious, pacing his kennel and the yard and struggling to settle. However, as he has become used to the routine, surroundings, and staff at Many Tears, Luca has settled very well and discovered a love of all sorts of toys!

We try to give our dogs a mix of toys and enrichment until we know what they like. Luca is not very interested in food-based enrichment like LickiMats or Kongs. He will tug-of-war hesitantly with a rope toy but doesn't really engage with it. However, Luca LOVES a game of fetch down the big yard. He may occasionally jump up to try and get the ball and become over-excited and mouthy, so we are working on balancing his stimulation so he can get his energy out without getting worked up, and on commands like "sit", "wait", and "drop". Luca is incredibly gentle and does not want to hurt anyone, but he is a big boy and could knock a vulnerable person down if he gets too over-excited, so this kind of training is important.

Luca's FAVOURITE type of toy, though, is cuddly toys! It just proves what a big softie he is, as he really loves nothing more than carrying around his stuffed pig toy or cwtching up with his favourite, a string of stuffed Brussels sprouts. It's really lovely to see him relax and enjoy himself this way. Even better when he's doing it on your lap!

Luca is loved by all the staff and volunteers who meet him, but he's definitely ready to be someone's best friend.

Luca was previously used as a fake security dog and has spent most of his life living outside, but beneath his big appearance he is a real softie. He is easy to handle and enjoys human company, though he has understandably found kennel life quite stressful and will often plead with us to come back when we have to leave him.

Luca would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where he can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with his new family. He will need adopters who have plenty of time to spend with him and who have experience of the breed or similar breeds. Luca cannot live with cats or small furries and he cannot be around small dogs.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life. He will need patient adopters who can help guide him through these new experiences as he adjusts to living in a home environment.

Luca can already walk on a lead, though he does pull at first and so this is something his adopters will need to work on with him. He is a very active boy, so he would love an active household where he can enjoy plenty of adventures and become a loyal companion once he is settled in. He is a strong dog and can both jump and open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who are able to manage his strength safely.

Luca is an intelligent, affectionate, and loyal boy who simply wants to be close to his people. In the right home, with structure, companionship, and plenty of love, he will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had 1 tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

02-06-26 Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment, but she is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had 7 teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Chewwie
description:
I’d like a quiet home filled with love and kindness!

I would like a home with another dog medium size or larger. I am fine with cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 2 teeth removed!

Chewwie originally came to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He was lucky enough to be adopted, but sadly, despite being very loved, it became clear that the home wasn't quite the right match for him and he has now returned to our care to begin his search once again. Chewwie was very worried of the adult sons in the home and also wasn't a great match with the smaller resident dog.

Chewwie is a sensitive boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and can find unfamiliar situations overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but remained worried around the adult sons in the household. For this reason, he is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Since returning to our care, however, Chewwie has been an absolute pleasure. From the day he came back, he has been nothing but gentle, loving and affectionate with everyone here. Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, we have seen a completely different side to him in kennels. He happily bounces over to greet us, is always looking for a fuss, and simply loves being around people. His affectionate nature shines through every day, and he has reminded us just what a special boy he is.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to family life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts of home, especially curling up in his cosy beds. He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and gradually build up any time spent alone as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium-sized or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has learnt to walk nicely on a lead and now really enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will benefit from ongoing encouragement as his confidence continues to grow.

Once Chewwie knows you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate companion with a wonderfully cheeky personality. He loves playing with other dogs and is especially fond of his kennel friend. He's also a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the paddling pool, making the most of every opportunity for fun. Like many mischievous youngsters, he has also been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially enjoys hard toys, while softer toys and enrichment items should be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. His return to rescue has shown us just how affectionate, gentle and resilient he is, and we know that in the right home he will continue to flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, fun-loving and wonderfully cheeky companion who will fill their days with smiles.

When Chewwie first arrived, he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. Following his return to the rescue, he began limping on the same leg and holding it up. X-rays at a local veterinary practice showed no abnormalities or injuries, so it is thought to be a soft tissue injury which should continue to improve. His adopters and their own vet should continue to monitor this as a precaution.

Chewwie has been given the Gift of Life by Paula Elliot

His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as we are told he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially loves hard toys, but softer toys and enrichment items will need to be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I haven’t met cats

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I still haven't mastered toilet training so please be patient with me.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has now spent a week back in foster care and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people and enjoy all the love and affection he has missed out on. While he is still worried by some men due to his past experiences, once he trusts you his affectionate nature really shines through.

Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in his foster home and sleeps happily alongside them through the night. Although he enjoys their company, his foster carer feels he could also be very happy as an only dog, where he can soak up all the cuddles and attention he so craves. In the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he would thrive.

One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He now walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. He has settled quickly into his foster home's routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, but this has already improved over the last few days as he has established a routine. His adopters should still be prepared to continue his house training with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.

Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly, and you would hardly know he has any issues with his eyesight. He has also had all of his teeth removed, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.

Crispin really is a special little boy who has had a difficult start in life but has so much love to give. He is looking for a very special family who will understand his worries, cherish the affectionate little dog he has become, and give him the love and security he so deserves. In return, they will gain the most devoted and loving companion.

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. He has had dental work and unfortunately did need to have all of his teeth removed, so he will need to stay on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

name: Holiday
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need a careful introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her as the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she came back into our care. Holiday has since moved to a foster home where she is settling beautifully and continuing to learn all about life in a home.

Holiday is a very sensitive girl who had very little socialisation before coming into our care. When she first returned to us, she found people incredibly worrying and was very hand-shy. Her first instinct was always to run away, and she wasn't comfortable being picked up or handled. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could react by nipping out of fear, and she did nip her previous adopter once when she became overwhelmed during handling.

Holiday will still be looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children. She will need adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, without pressure or expectations. She relies heavily on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her.

Since moving into foster care, Holiday has made some really lovely progress and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle nearby while her foster family relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where everyone is, often coming to find them and quietly checking in throughout the day.

She is now happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also greets us with a wagging tail and will happily sit and listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as anyone spoke to her, so this has been a huge milestone.

Although Holiday is becoming much more confident, she still isn't ready to be handled much and is not yet comfortable wearing a harness or going for walks. Her adopter will need to be happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace, allowing her to decide when she is ready for each new step.

Minus her brief adoption, Holiday had never lived in a home before, but she has settled brilliantly into foster care. She is now 99% clean in the house and has established a lovely routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs, taking great comfort from them and often following their lead. She enjoys spending time in the garden and small secure field, where she loves exploring, relaxing and watching the world go by. She has also been left at home with the other dogs for a few hours and has coped very well.

Holiday is a very special little girl who has already come such a long way. She is learning that people can be kind and that home life isn't so scary after all. She still has a journey ahead of her, but with plenty of patience, understanding and the support of another dog, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything her new life has to offer.

Holiday has been given the Gift of Life by Ellie Worron

Holiday has made some lovely progress since coming into foster care and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle close by while we relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where we are, often coming to find us and checking in throughout the day.

She is happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also wags her tail when she sees us and will happily listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as we spoke to her, so this is a huge milestone for her.

Holiday is now 99% clean in the house and has settled brilliantly into a routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs and takes great comfort from them, often following their lead. She loves spending time in the garden and our small field, where she enjoys exploring and relaxing.

At the moment, Holiday is not yet ready to wear a harness or go for walks, and she will need an adopter who is happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She is making steady progress and, with patience and kindness, continues to blossom.

Holiday is a very gentle, sweet little girl with the softest, kindest eyes. She has such a lovely nature, and it is a privilege to watch her confidence grow a little more each day.

Holiday has settled well into foster care. She is worried about being handled at the moment so we haven’t tried to stroke her or pick her up, we wanted to give her the chance to settle and feel safe first.

She will take treats from our hands, walk through doorways easily, even with us there, and she seeks us out if she doesn’t know where we are. This all indicates that it won’t be long until we can begin gentles strokes etc. When we are fussing our dogs she gets closer to watch and has touched my hand or sniffed my legs. Holiday is not as jumpy as I thought she would be, which is great, and we can walk quite close to her without her moving away.

When we are all settled in the evening, she comes into the sitting room to see where we all are and what we are doing. She isn’t phased by the TV and will often sit on a rug next to my chair.

We have a very small field which most new fosters are a bit scared of as they are not used to big spaces, Holiday loves spending time out there exploring and watching the other dogs play, we’ve even seen her do the odd little sprint!

She has been clean in the house and loves snuggling with the dogs at night in the kitchen, she is left overnight and we can go out for a couple of hours and she is fine as long as the dogs are with her too.

She has the potential to be the best dog and I don’t think it will be long before she is seeking attention and ready to try her harness again. She has very gentle eyes and you can see the sadness ebbing away a little more each day.

This week Holiday has been making lovely progress with lead work. We have been helping her get used to having a lead clipped onto her harness and trailing behind her, and she is becoming much more comfortable with this. Clipping the lead onto her harness is now far less of a concern for her, which is a big step forward, and when she is out in the yard she barely seems aware of it anymore.

She is also doing wonderfully with different people putting her harness on, which is a very significant achievement for Holiday given how sensitive she has been around handling. She is taking these steps in her stride and continues to make really encouraging progress.

Recently, I’ve been spending some dedicated time working with Holiday, and she’s making such lovely progress. She’s beginning to trust me more each day and has even allowed me to gently put a harness on her. Everything is done slowly and at her pace, with plenty of treats and reassurance, but this is a huge milestone for this sensitive girl.

We’ve also been working on gentle touch, always on her terms. When she chooses to come and sit beside me in her bed, we take things one small step at a time, building her confidence with each positive experience (and a few tasty rewards along the way!).

Holiday is starting to show more of her personality now. She’s often one of the first up for a treat and has even begun wagging her tail. It might sound like a small thing, but for Holiday, it’s truly something special.

She’s a wonderful dog who just needs a patient, understanding home where she can continue to grow in confidence and feel safe. Watching her come out of her shell is incredibly rewarding, and she’s so ready for someone to give her the love she deserves.

I am writing this update as someone who has not had much interaction with Holiday although I have worked with her on a few occasions. It is obvious from her previous update that there has been progress in her coming out of her shell and I was surprised to discover that Holiday would accept treats from my hand although when trying to smooth her coat, Holiday swiftly moved out of reach.

She is getting there but slowy and anyone wanting to adopt her will need to go slowly and earn that important trust. Holiday's regular carer can stroke Holiday when she is settled in a bed but only in one place. If a position is changed, Holiday will become scared and move.

It is apparent after speaking with Holiday's regular carer that for Holiday to make that important next step in her progress, it would be better for her to be in a home situation. Holiday is fantastic with other dogs and would definitely need to live with at least one other dog to give her that hope of progress and comfort. There is always someone out there for every dog and vice versa Holiday is waiting.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder a few months ago. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her and the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she is now back in our care.

Holiday is a very scared girl who is very overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She finds human interaction quite difficult at the moment and is very hand-shy, so she will need a patient and understanding home that can help her come out of her shell at her own pace. Holiday will run away from you when you enter her kennel and isn't keen on being picked up or handled. She finds this so scary, that if she feels like she is being pushed out of her comfort zone she can choose nip or bite, purely through fear. She did bite her previous adopter once when she was being handled as she became so worried.

For this reason, Holiday will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where there are no visiting children. She will need adopters who hav experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will let her settle in slowly at her own pace with no pressure or expectations.

Holiday finds comfort and reassurance from the company of her canine friends and so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing. This dog will need to allow her to snuggle up to them and will need to be happy for her to follow them around. A kind resident dog will be an important source of reassurance and companionship for her as she adjusts to her new life.

Although she spent some time in foster and was adopted for a short period, she had never lived in a home before this, so Holiday will still need to learn all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn to walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice wearing these around the home and garden, once her confidence with handling has grown a little more. She will then need to practice walking around the garden until she is confident enough to venture further.

Since arriving back with us, Holiday has started to make some more progress and will now take a treat from our hands as long as she has a doggy friend next to her for support. With time, love and patience she will start to leave her past behind her and will truly start to blossom. Holiday's journey won't be a short one, but it will be so worth it when you see her tail wag for the first time or when she first willingly accepts some fuss and attention. In the right home, she will thrive, so please don't keep her waiting too long.

name: Cassy
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I love going on walks, and would love plenty in my new home!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Please read below for more information about my health!

Cassy is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now ready to start her next chapter. She can be a little overwhelmed by new situations and may be unsure initially, but with time, love and patience she is already showing just how much progress she can make.

Cassy has now moved into a foster home where she is settling in well and learning all about home life for the first time ever. She is trying so hard to be brave, but doesn't actively seek attention yet. If she's on the sofa or in bed, she is happy to be fussed.

Cassy relies heavily on other dogs for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and provide support as she continues to learn about life in a home environment. She has met cats and was very good with them, so could potentially live alongside a feline friend, with sensible introductions.

She had never lived in a home before moving to foster and is already doing well with learning new skills like house training, but does need more practice. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she continues to build confidence and learn about the world around her.

Cassy gets so excited when it's time to go on her walks, and would love to continue this in her new home!

This lovely girl is simply looking for someone willing to take a chance on her, offering the love, patience and reassurance she needs to truly thrive. In return, you'll have the privilege of watching her blossom into the happy, confident dog she is meant to be.

When Cassy arrived with us, it was noted that she had a cherry eye, which was repaired. This has recently popped back out, but at this moment is too small to repair again and so this is something her adopters and their vet will need to monitor. She has also been treated for conjunctivitis. She has had a dental with one tooth extracted, and our vets have noted that one other tooth has a slightly exposed root. This does not require removal at present but should be monitored.

Cassy has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

After returning to the rescue to have her cherry eye assessed, Cassy has now moved to foster once again. She is making good progress but is still very nervous. She doesn't actively seek attention yet, but she is trying so hard to be brave. If she's on the sofa or in bed, she is happy to be fussed.

She had her first walk on the lead in garden this morning, with the help of lots of primula cheese!! She will now move past me in a relaxed manner and enjoys cuddles with the other dogs.

She likes to be in the same room as me. She eats well and is food orientated and happily takes a treat from my hand.

She will need  an experienced, quiet home where she can progress at her own pace and be fully supported.

Her cherry eye has not caused any problems, and though it has recurred the vet felt like it did no require a second repair at this time, though will need to be monitored. I wipe her eyes daily.

Cassy recently arrived here in foster and is settling in well. Unfortunately her cherry eye has recurred so she will need to head back to the rescue centre to have this assessed, but she has really enjoyed her week in foster.

She is a lovely girl who is very food motivated and will happily approach with a waggy tail when treats are on offer. If food is around, she’s always hopeful for a little taste! She is very hand shy and can be skittish when approached, but with gentle reassurance and patience she will allow strokes and appears to enjoy them, even though she doesn’t actively seek fuss just yet. Sudden movements can startle her, so she benefits from a calm, slow approach. She likes to quietly follow me around the house but will move away if approached too directly.

She enjoys playing with toys and has a funny habit of carrying a shoe around in her mouth. Like many dogs, she may chew items left on the floor, although she doesn’t go looking for things to chew.

Cassy would suit a calm and quiet household where she can be given the time and space she needs to relax and settle in. She really wants to be brave, and with patience and kindness her confidence should continue to grow. She enjoys the company of other dogs and loves snuggling up with them on the sofa.

She currently sleeps in the kitchen with my dogs at night. She is house trained, and confidently uses the dog flap to go outside to toilet.

Cassy is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is still building her confidence. She can be a little unsure at first and finds reassurance in the company of other dogs.

She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help guide her and give her the confidence she needs as she settles in.

Cassy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns all about house training and how to walk on a lead. Starting with gentle garden exploration and quiet outdoor time will help her gradually get used to the world around her.

This lovely girl is simply looking for someone willing to take a chance on her, offering the love, patience, and reassurance she needs to truly thrive.

Cassy arrived with cherry eye in her right eye that has since been surgically repaired at the time of her spay. She is also being treated for conjunctivitis. She has had a dental with one tooth extracted and our vets have noted that one other tooth has the root slightly exposed, but have advised that it is not removed at the moment and monitored going forward.
