name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

I'm fully vaccinated and have been neutered.

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I will need to be neutered when I am of age! It's important!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Gary
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home with 4ft boundaries.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am missing my left eye, and I have been castrated & have had 1 tooth removed.

Gary is a very sweet and sensitive boy who has come to us from a breeder. He has now moved into foster and, despite his worries around people, has taken to home life like a duck to water. Everything is exciting to him, and he approaches the world with curiosity, happily exploring every room and taking new sights and sounds in his stride. Household noises don't seem to faze him at all.

Gary has also discovered his playful side and has very much switched into "puppy mode". He is as cute as a button and is always looking for his next adventure. If you turn your back for a few minutes, there's a good chance he'll have found something interesting to carry around! Thankfully, he is happy for his foster carer to gently take items away from him. He enjoys his food and treats, loves playing with toys, appreciates the freedom of the garden, and has quickly decided that sleeping on the family bed is the perfect place to spend the night.

Gary takes enormous comfort from the company of other dogs and is very dependent on his resident canine companions. He has formed a particularly lovely bond with the older male Dachshund in his foster home and is wonderfully determined to persuade him to join in with a game. Because of this, Gary will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his forever home to help guide him, reassure him, and continue building his confidence.

Although Gary has settled brilliantly into home life, he remains extremely frightened of human touch and handling. If he feels pressured or overwhelmed, he may react defensively out of fear. His adopters will need to understand that there will be no quick fix for this. Instead, they must be committed to earning his trust, respecting his boundaries, and allowing him to build confidence at his own pace through gentle, positive experiences. He is already showing what an intelligent and resilient little dog he is, and every small step forward is a huge achievement.

As he is now in a home, he will begin to learn all about house training and lead walking when he is ready, lead walking. A secure garden will be essential, giving him a safe space to explore while he continues to gain confidence.

Due to his sensitive nature, Gary is looking for a calm, adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs, where he can settle without pressure and be accepted for who he is. Gary has come to us missing his left eye, but this doesn't slow him down in the slightest—if anything, it adds to his unique and endearing charm.

Gary is a truly special little boy. He has already shown just how well he can adapt to family life when given patience and understanding. With adopters who are willing to invest the time to earn his trust, we have no doubt that he will grow into an incredibly loyal and rewarding companion and become a wonderful ambassador for his breed.

At the time of his castration, Gary had one tooth removed.

Gary has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Little Gary arrived in foster and has taken to home life like a duck to water. Everything is exciting and is to be explored and conquered, with no household item or sound yet phasing him.

He has turned on his puppy mode, cute as a button but if you turn your back for 5 minutes, he is off with something new in his mouth, but is happy for you to take this away.

He enjoys his food and treats, loves his toys, and very much appreciates the freedom of the garden and the security of sleeping on the family bed at night.

He is very dependent on my resident dogs and has taken a real shine to our older much bigger male dachsie showing great determination in persuading him to play.

Gary does however remain extremely scared of human touch/handling and if you push this, he may act out defensively in fear. There will be no quick fix. Instead this will be a journey of earning his trust, respecting his boundaries and slowly desensitising him to these fears. However this little boy is going to be so worth the investment and in time, will be a credit to the dachsie breed.

Garry is just the funniest little dude, and works hard ever day to become braver with us humans. Thanks to the kindness and perseverance of staff at the rescue Garry slowly grows more confident with us.

Garry has been deeply affected by his rough start in life and arrived terrified of everyone, hating being touched or just being near us. But day by day Garry gets braver and will now allow a little scratch under his chin or take a treat (he loves his food). It’s hard not to fall for Garry there is just something about him and within a patient loving home I believe the true Garry will shine through.

When you seem him playing with his friends in the yard he’s just adorable and happy. Garrys ideal home would be experienced with nervous rescues, have a resident dog and no children, or visiting children.

Gary is a very sweet boy once he gets to know you, although this can take a few meetings. He is very shy and timid in his kennel but will put on a brave front when you're outside it.

Gary is currently undergoing muzzle training as he can be tricky when handled. He is doing really well and is now able to tolerate gentle touches under his chin during his training sessions. Thankfully, Gary is a big foodie, which makes muzzle training much more engaging and rewarding for him.

I’ve been at the rescue for a little while now, and I’ve started to make some two-legged friends. I love the food they give me, especially the squeezy paste in a tube, and I’ll go right up to them now for that tasty treat. Sometimes, when they’re not looking, I’ll creep up behind them and check to see if there’s any in their pockets (but they don’t know I do this, so don’t tell them!).

I prefer it when the two-legged ones move slowly and quietly. It’s very unsettling for me if they rush about, and I’ll find a corner to curl up in and make myself feel safe when they do. On the whole though, they’re okay, and I love it when they let me go out into the big yards. I may be quite tiny, but that doesn’t stop me roaming around for all the good sniffs, and I don’t mind if they sit and chat with me while I go about my business.

Yesterday, one of the two-legged ones sat in the kennel with me. I curled up in my bed and watched them, and I even let them give me a little scratch. I think I would quite like some of these two-legged friends of my own, as long as they’re quiet and gentle (none of the small, bouncy ones!). A cosy bed of my own does sound rather nice, and of course I’ll need a four-legged friend as well.

Perhaps I’ll find some lovely two-legged friends soon… let me know if you hear of any.

Gary is a very sweet and sensitive boy who has come to us from a breeder. He currently finds human interaction quite overwhelming and can be touch-sensitive, so he needs time and patience to build trust. He is very much on the worried side and can react by snapping if he becomes frightened when being picked up, so it’s important that his adopters take a gentle, hands-off approach and allow him to come to them in his own time.

Although he is still nervous, Gary is beginning to take treats from people he knows well and has spent time with, which is a lovely sign of progress and shows his potential to build trusting relationships.

Gary takes great comfort from his kennel friends and has always lived alongside other dogs, so he will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, reassure him, and show him the ropes as he settles in.

As Gary has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be understanding while he learns about house training and walking on a lead. He is not yet used to lead walking, so a secure garden will be essential, giving him a safe space to explore and build confidence at his own pace.

Due to his sensitive nature, Gary is looking for a calm adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where he can settle in at his own pace without pressure. He will need plenty of time, love, and reassurance, but with patience and consistency, he will continue to make progress and grow in confidence.

Gary has come to us missing his left eye, but this doesn’t slow him down at all, if anything, it adds to his unique and endearing charm.

Gary is a little superstar who is trying his best in a world he finds quite overwhelming. With the right support, he will continue to blossom and form a deep, loyal bond with his future family.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Davina
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

17-07-26 Davina came to us from a breeder and is now searching for a patient and understanding forever home. We have been told she is a Miniature Doodle (she weighs just under 10kg), but whatever her mix may be, one thing is certain, she's absolutely adorable.

Davina is a very gentle and sensitive little girl who is still finding the world quite overwhelming. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and relies on them for reassurance while she learns that people and new experiences aren't so frightening. Although she is beginning to observe what's going on around her, she is still a very worried girl who needs time to build trust and confidence.

Because of this, Davina is looking for a calm, quiet home with adopters who haveexperience of ex-breeding dogsand understand that confidence cannot be rushed. She will need people who are happy to let her settle entirely at her own pace, allowing her to make progress in her own time without any pressure or expectations.

Davinamust have another kind, confident resident dogin her new home. Having a canine companion is essential for her, providing reassurance, helping her understand home life and giving her the confidence to follow their lead as she discovers the joys of being part of a family.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be completely new to Davina. She will need help with house training, learning household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to everyday sights and sounds. Lead walking will also be something to build slowly, beginning with gentle introductions in the safety of the garden before venturing further afield when she feels ready.

Due to her nervous nature, Davina is looking for anadult-only homewhere she can enjoy a peaceful, predictable environment while she continues to blossom.

Davina is a sweet little soul who simply needs time, patience and understanding. Watching a frightened ex-breeding dog gradually discover that life can be safe and happy is incredibly rewarding, and we have no doubt that, in the right home, Davina will continue to grow in confidence and become a devoted companion.

Davina has been given the Gift of Life by Ceri Mann

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Raven
description:
I need an understanding, adult-only home with ex-breeder experience.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I am in foster with a cat!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead and will need more practice to build confidence.

I am in a foster home and doing well with house training!

I have Grade 2 luxating patellas, which may improve with exercise.

21-07-26 Raven is a sweet, curious girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived she was quite worried, but her confidence has steadily grown and her cheeky, comical personality is really starting to shine through.

She has been settling into foster life and continues to make slow and steady progress. Home life was completely new to Raven at first and she found it overwhelming, but she has adapted beautifully and is now fully house-trained. She has embraced many of the comforts of home and will happily jump up on the sofa to sit beside her foster carers, where she enjoys a gentle fuss.

Sadly, Raven was briefly adopted, but she struggled to form a bond with her adopters. As they found handling her difficult, Raven became frightened and, when she felt cornered, reacted out of fear by nipping. Since returning to her devoted foster home, it is as though she has never been away. She has settled straight back into her familiar routine, is happily enjoying her walks again, and continues to grow in confidence in an environment where she feels safe and understood.

Raven remains a timid and hand-shy little girl, and she can still be worried about handling. She will now approach her trusted people for a gentle fuss, although she still takes the greatest comfort from the company of her canine friends. Her curiosity is beginning to shine through, and when visitors come to the house she will quietly make her way over to introduce herself in her own time. She has such a lovely, gentle temperament and has never shown any issues in her foster home, where she feels secure. She has been very good for bathing and grooming and is becoming used to regular brushing as part of her routine.

Raven absolutely adores other dogs andmusthave at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide and reassure her. She relies heavily on canine companionship, gets on brilliantly with the dogs in foster, and is also living happily alongside a cat, who she ignores, so she could potentially live with a dog-savvy feline. She would find young children too much at the moment, but we would consider gentle, dog-savvy older teenagers who would allow her to settle at her own pace.

Raven is a curious little girl and a total foodie, with tasty treats still very much the way to her heart and a wonderful aid in helping her continue to build confidence.

She has made lovely progress with walking and has gone from beginner steps on lead and harness to genuinely enjoying her outings. It is a joy to see how excited she gets for walks and she walks very nicely without pulling. She has seen light traffic and has taken it in her stride, and foster has even begun recall work on a longline, which is going well so far. She also travels well in a crate in the car.

Raven is now looking for an experienced home with adopters who have previously lived with ex-breeding dogs and understand the unique challenges they can face. She will need patient, understanding people who are happy to let her settle at her own pace and allow a bond to develop naturally, without placing expectations on her too soon. Given the time, space and support she needs, Raven has all the potential to become a wonderfully loyal and rewarding companion.

Our vets have noted that Raven has Grade 2 patella luxation, which may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. She also had an abdominal hernia repaired at the time of her spay and has been treated for an ear infection.

I have been given the Gift of Life by Jean James

Raven is making sure and steady progress in foster. She is still timid and hand-shy, but will jump up on the sofa next to us and enjoys a fuss. She is a good girl to bath and groom. Raven has a lovely temperament and I haven’t seen her have even the slightest grumble at a human, cat or dog. She is now completely house-trained. It is so sweet watching her get excited to go out walking, she really enjoys it and is not a puller on the lead. We have started recall training on a longline and it’s going well so far. She has seen light traffic and been fine. Raven travels well in a crate in the car. She will definitely need a kind doggy companion in her new home. I hope her people find her soon, she’s so deserving of a loving forever home.

Raven has been in foster for just over a week. She was quite overwhelmed to start off with but is already starting to settle in and come out of her shell. She is a nosey little lady and her curiosity along with her love of yummy food helps her to overcome her fears. She is quick to learn about housetraining, and with good management accidents are rare. Raven gets along brilliantly with other dogs and ignores my cat. She would find children too much but could live with older teenagers who are patient and kind.

She is worried about being handled but tolerates it, If we put her on the sofa with us she settles down and likes a fuss.

We have started getting Raven used to being brushed. She will need owners that will take care of her thick curly coat and take her to the groomers regularly. Raven is a beginner on the lead but enjoys a walk and a sniff in quiet places. With time and love Raven will be just wonderful. Her temperament is lovely and we are starting to glimpse the comical, cheeky girl that she is destined to be.

Raven’s confidence has improved massively since she first arrived and her cheeky, curious and comical personality is really starting to shine through now. She is an absolute foodie and her favourite time of day is definitely treat time, or my dinner time!! She likes to see exactly what I have and figure out if she will like it too, and then politely ask me for a little share. She’ll put her two front paws on my lap and look at me with doting puppy dog eyes that I can’t say no to. She’s too adorable! She’s also a little thief and will try to steal things if you leave them out. This week she very sneakily stole a packet of crisps and started running around the yard with them!!! We were sat in the yard with her so she didn’t get very far with them, but it was so lovely to see her full of joy and almost like a ‘normal’ dog.

Raven is still hand shy with humans and will run away if you try to touch her or approach her, but she is okay to pick up once she jumps into one of her beds. She’s also had a bath and a groom since her arrival and she was a very good girl!! I don’t think it will take too long for her to get used to being touched and stroked, especially once she’s in a home. I think she will actually start to enjoy it in time!

Raven is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder. She can be a little worried at times, but she is easy to handle and very curious about the world around her.

Raven will need a kind and confident resident dog in the home to help boost her confidence and show her love and reassurance. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead, all at her own pace.

She could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers who respect her space as she settles in. With plenty of time, patience, and TLC, Raven will soon blossom into a loving and loyal companion.

Our vets have noted that Raven has Grade 2 patella luxation. This may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle, but it is something her adopters and their vet will need to monitor going forwards. She has had an abdominal hernia repaired at the time of her spay and is currently being treated for a ear infection.

name: Lemon Pie
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in as I get comfortable in my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and my right eye has been removed.

Lemon Pie is an absolute heartbreaker who came to us from a breeder and initially found it difficult to settle into her new environment. We believe this was partly due to discomfort in her right eye, which has since been removed. She has recovered well from her surgery and already seems much more comfortable. She has corneal scarring on her left eye that will need to be monitored for any future issues that may arise, but she is able to see around it well for now.

Lemon Pie has now spent a week in foster care and is making lovely, gentle progress. She arrived as a very scared little girl who adored the company of the other dogs but didn't want to be close to people. She would spend much of her day in the garden or the kitchen, quietly watching her foster carer from a distance. With time, patience, and understanding, she has already started to show just how brave she can be. She is now happy to stay in the same room as her foster carer and no longer feels the need to run away whenever someone moves nearby.

Lemon Pie can still be sensitive to touch and may shy away from hands, suggesting that she may not always have been treated with the kindness she deserves. She needs adopters who will allow her to build trust at her own pace and never rush or overwhelm her. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to grow in confidence each day.

Having never lived in a home before, Lemon Pie will need understanding adopters who can guide her through all the new experiences and routines of family life. At the moment, harness and lead walking are still a little way off, and her foster carers are allowing her to progress entirely at her own pace. She absolutely loves pottering around the secure garden, where she feels safe and can explore without pressure. As her confidence continues to grow, we are sure she will be ready to take on new adventures in time.

Lemon Pie absolutely adores other dogs and takes enormous comfort from their company. She loves sharing her food bowl and curling up to sleep alongside her doggy friends, so having at least one kind and confident resident dog in her forever home is essential. They will provide her with the reassurance and confidence she needs as she continues to blossom. She could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers who will respect her space and understand that she needs time to settle.

Lemon Pie is an incredibly deserving little girl who has already shown how much progress she can make when given patience and understanding. She is looking for a calm, loving home where she can continue to build trust at her own pace and finally enjoy the happy life she has always deserved.

Lemon Pie has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Hicklin

She loves to share her food bowl and sleep curled up with a doggy pal, so this is very important in her forever home. Harness and lead walking are a way off yet but she loves mooching in the garden.

With time, as she builds trust, these things will come but for now we are taking things at her pace as to not overwhelm her.

She may initially be too nervous for lead walks, so spending time exploring a secure garden at her own pace would be a great way to help her build confidence as she adjusts to her new surroundings.Lemon Pie will need at least one kind, confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the way and provide reassurance as she settles in. name: Jerry
description:
I need a calm and quiet adult only home with adopters with experience of collies.

I could live with another dog, or by myself. I cannot live with cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would like an active home and love to go for walks.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Jerry is a lovely boy who originally came to us from a breeder a few years ago and went on to find a wonderful forever home. Sadly, through no fault of his own, he has now returned to our care due to his adopters' ill health.

Jerry is a Collie lover's dream! He is affectionate, clever and eager to be part of the family. He is house trained, walks beautifully on the lead and we are told he has excellent recall too. He is a very smart boy who already knows a range of commands includingsit,wait,off,dropandleave, and he would thrive in an active home where he can be kept mentally and physically stimulated.

Since moving down to one of our field kennels, Jerry has become much more relaxed and settled. Being in a quieter environment has really allowed his wonderful personality to shine. He is incredibly loving and has shown us just how well he can socialise with other dogs. In fact, he has been so calm and sensible around them that he has even been used during one-to-one behaviour sessions with reactive dogs, where he has been an absolute superstar. Because of this, we feel Jerry could happily live with another well-matched dog, although careful introductions would still be important.

Jerry would still be best suited to an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of Collies and rescue dogs. He would love a rural or quieter home where he can continue to enjoy a peaceful lifestyle, and he would benefit from adopters who are around for much of the day and have plenty of time to spend with him.

Jerry has shown some signs of separation anxiety in the past, so his new family will need to continue building up the time he is left gradually. We are told that he is happy being left for short periods but will need patience and understanding while he settles into his new home.

One area where Jerry has made fantastic progress is with his noise sensitivity. While he can still notice unexpected noises, he is coping with them far better than before. Rather than becoming distressed, he is now much more likely to simply look towards his handler as if to ask, "What was that?" before moving on. His growing confidence has been wonderful to see, although his adopters should still be prepared to continue supporting him with gentle reassurance and positive experiences around unfamiliar sounds.

Jerry has settled back into rescue life beautifully. He loves a cuddle, enjoys a good play session and is an incredibly rewarding dog to spend time with. He is a truly special boy with so much love to give, and we know he has all the qualities to make an exceptional companion for the right family.

Jerry previously had a wound on his right paw which caused a limp. This has now healed well and he is no longer showing any signs of lameness.

Jer-bear, Jerry! This handsome boy is going to melt someone’s heart.

Jerry has come in from a home with a variety of noise related triggers but do not let this put you off meeting him, for he is one quick brave border collie. He was once visibly stressed at the sight of a can of pop and more stressed when carbonated drink cans/bottles were opened. He has improved and is not as stressed when he sees a can of pop and due to him moving around the rescue we have given him some time to settle as he wasn’t feeling himself in his previous kennel.

Since moving he has been showing us bit by bit his playful sassy side. He loves going for his morning walk to take a break from the overwhelming kennels, Jerry has even been socialising with other dogs. We have found that he gets on well with other dogs however if put into an overwhelming situation he is likely to redirect onto his kennel buddy so is safer for him and any other dogs if he is not homed with one. We have found that once he is comfortable with his people, he is quick to desensitise to certain triggers.

For example: one of his handlers is diabetic and uses cans of lucozade to treat hypos on walks and in kennels. He has become alert but has not reacted and is less anxious at the sight of cans or bottles now

When I first met Jerry I had heard about his triggers and was very curious, he is a very interesting young dog who is bound to be the light of someone’s life!

I have been working with Jerry for a little while now and have found that his can/bottle related trigger is a bit deeper than we were led to believe, the visual prompt causes him some stress, but found that he is quick to look for comfort. He really enjoys spending time with his doggy friends and looks to humans for comfort, and enjoys going out for walks, he seems to feel more relaxed on walks and have found once triggered by a noise he over analyses the indoor environment not so much the outdoor space.

During Jerry's stay here I plan to slowly introduce new noises and help him to understand that new noises are not necessarily a bad thing.

Jerry is a lovely boy who originally came to us from a breeder a few years ago and went on to find a wonderful forever home. Sadly, through no fault of his own, he has now returned to our care due to his adopters ill health.

Jerry is a Collie lover’s dream! He is affectionate, clever and eager to be part of the family. He is house trained, walks nicely on the lead and we are told that he has good recall too. He is a very smart boy who already knows a range of commands including sit, wait, off, drop and leave, and would thrive in an active home where he can be kept both mentally and physically stimulated.

Jerry would like to be the only dog in his forever home. He would be best suited to an adult only home and would benefit from adopters with collie and rescue dog experience. He would love a rural home, as he can be sensitive to certain sounds and so homes in busier areas wouldn't be suitable for him. He would really benefit from adopters who are around for much of the day and have plenty of time to spend with him.

Jerry does show some signs of separation anxiety, so his new family will need to continue building up the time he is left gradually. We are told that he is happy being left for short periods but will need patience and understanding while he settles. He isn’t keen on car travel, and he can be sensitive to sounds and may react to sounds such as fizzy drink cans or bottles opening, sneezing, coughing, nose blowing, printers, hoovers, microwaves, lorry reversing beeps, motorbike revving, army range noise and fireworks. He will bark towards you but with reassurance he settles quickly. He has never bitten and is just worried but his new owners will need to continue noise desensitization training in the home. It may never be something he entirely overcomes.

Jerry has settled back into the rescue well and is a wonderful boy who is already enjoying snuggles and really loves to play! He is a truly special boy who has so much love to give and is ready to find a calm, understanding home to call his own once again.

He has had a wound on his right paw that has caused a limp, which has since healed and he is no longer showing signs of limping.

name: Ulyssa
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fencing.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

19-07-26 Ulyssa has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a very scared little girl who is feeling overwhelmed by all the changes in her life. She will need plenty of kindness, patience and reassurance as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

Ulyssa is looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of helping scared ex-breeding dogs. She will need a family who understand that progress may be slow at times and who will allow her to build trust at her own pace without expecting too much too soon.

Ulyssa takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need to live with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who can help guide her, reassure her and show her that people and home life are nothing to be afraid of. Having a canine friend will be essential in helping her grow in confidence.

She has never lived in a home before, so her new family will need to be patient and understanding while she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She does not yet walk on a lead or harness and will need to first practice around the home and garden until she is feeling brave enough to venture further.

Ulyssa is a gentle soul who has a long journey ahead of her, but with experienced, compassionate adopters and the support of a confident canine companion, she will slowly begin to blossom. Watching a frightened dog learn to trust and enjoy life is incredibly rewarding, and Ulyssa deserves the chance to experience the love and security she has always missed.

Ulyssa has been given the Gift of Life by Lesley Beattie

name: Sara
description:
I will need a kind, adult-only home that will allow me to settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a Grade 1 Heart Murmur and a Luxating Patella.

24-07-26 Sara is a sweet and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a very pretty girl who is good with her kennel friends, all of whom are a similar size to her. Sara is easy to handle, although she can be nervous when approached and will need a little time to feel comfortable with new people.

Sara gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Sara has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her time to adjust to her new surroundings.

Sara will need a adult-only home where she can settle in at her own pace and who understand ex-breeders and have experience with nervous dogs.

Sara has a Grade 1 heart murmur, which does not currently seem to bother her, and a Grade 1 patella luxation. This may continue to improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle, and our vets will monitor her to ensure she remains comfortable.

Sara is a lovely, gentle girl who is still finding her confidence. With a confident canine companion and a patient family to help her along the way, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the lovely things that home life has to offer.

name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to be the only dog in the home, and I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

22-07-26 Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

name: Daisy
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a larger, male, doggy friend in my new home. I haven't met cats!

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I had an entropion on both lower eyelids, but these have now been surgically repaired

02-06-26 Daisy is a scared Cocker Spaniel who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.She is finding human interaction very difficult at the moment and will often move away if we get too close. Daisy is worried by handling, so she will need careful and gentle management while she learns that people can be kind. Having had very little life experience, much of the world is still new and overwhelming to her, and she will need patient adopters who are willing to let her progress at her own pace.

At the moment, Daisy is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be re-homed with another large, male dog for support and companionship. Having a confident canine friend by her side will help her feel more secure as she settles into home life.

As Daisy has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be understanding and prepared to guide her through these new experiences with patience and reassurance.

Daisy prefers to enjoy her meals on her own, so mealtimes are carefully managed here and should continue to be managed in the same way in her new home. Feeding her separately helps prevent any confusion over whose food belongs to whom and allows her to feel more relaxed. Treats should also be given thoughtfully and managed in the same way to ensure a positive experience for everyone.

Daisy could share her home with quiet, older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Daisy has arrived with bilateral entropion of the lower eyelids, which have now been surgically repaired by our vets. She is also underweight, so we will be helping her reach and maintain a healthier weight during her stay with us. This will need to be continued in her new home to ensure she remains happy and healthy.

Although Daisy is finding life quite frightening right now, there is a lovely girl underneath those worries. With time, patience, and the support of a canine companion, we are confident that she will begin to blossom and discover that the world is not such a scary place after all.

Daisy has been given the Gift of Life by Lynn Carrivick

name: Alfie
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I am fine with cats!

I would love a garden to potter around in.

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have age related cataracts, and have had 13 teeth removed.

24-07-26 Alfie is a wonderful older man who was originally adopted from us and has sadly found himself back in our care after spending many years in a home. He is now looking for a very special retirement home where he can enjoy all the comforts he loves.

As Alfie has got older, he has developed a few age-related quirks. He can become a little confused at night and, during a recent adoption, found it difficult to settle, often pacing and becoming restless. Since returning to us, we have found a routine that helps him feel safe and secure, and he now settles well to sleep in a crate. For this reason, his new home will need to provide him with a quiet space where he can rest undisturbed, and we would like his adopters to continue this routine.

Alfie is an early riser and is usually awake around 6am, although he has been making lovely progress with settling quietly for a little longer each morning. Once he's up, he still has a real spring in his step! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time for a walk and can be quite vocal while his lead is being put on, but as soon as he's out and about he is the perfect gentleman. He walks beautifully, enjoys exploring, and is friendly with everyone he meets, both people and dogs.

Despite being an older gentleman, Alfie still loves getting out and about and enjoys keeping busy. A good walk and plenty of things to keep his mind occupied help him settle well afterwards, and once he's had his exercise there's nothing he loves more than curling up on the sofa for a cuddle.

Alfie gets on well with other dogs and could happily live with calm canine companions. Equally, he is quite an independent little chap and would also be perfectly content as the only dog in the home. Like many older dogs, Alfie has become very enthusiastic about his food. He can be a little grabby with treats and has occasionally grumbled around mealtimes, but this has never escalated and is easily managed by feeding him separately from other dogs and allowing him to enjoy his meals in peace.

Alfie is a truly special little boy who has stolen the hearts of everyone at the rescue. He is looking for a kind and understanding family who will embrace his little quirks, continue the routine that helps him thrive, and give him all the love, comfort and adventures he still enjoys. In return, they will gain a happy, affectionate companion who still has so much love to give.

name: Jackie
description:
I can live with older children, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & have had 7 teeth extracted.

Jackie takes great comfort from her canine friends and gets on beautifully with all of the other dogs in her foster home.
