name: Whimsey
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teens who are sensible and will allow me to settle.

I could live as an only dog, or with a similar sized canine friend. No cats please!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead, but will need guidance in the outside world.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Whimsey came to us from a breeder as a very worried little girl who found the world quite overwhelming. When she first arrived, she was unsettled and skittish, needing plenty of time and reassurance to help her feel safe. Since then, she has made wonderful progress and has really started to show what a special girl she is.

Whimsey has formed a lovely bond with her carers and now greets those she knows and trusts with enthusiastic cuddles and kisses. It has been a joy to watch her confidence grow, and she is becoming more comfortable with the people around her every day.

While Whimsey has come on tremendously, she can still be nervous and unsure around new people. She will need a calm, patient and understanding home that is willing to give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle at her own pace. Once she feels safe, her affectionate and loving personality truly shines through. She could also live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can respect her need for a gentle introduction and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Whimsey walks nicely on a lead, but as she can still be sensitive to new experiences, her adopters will need to continue introducing her to the world gently and at a pace she is comfortable with, helping her build confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Whimsey really enjoys spending time with other dogs and loves socialising with her canine friends in the exercise yards. We now feel she could happily live with another resident dog of a similar size, provided they get along well during a successful meet and greet. Like many dogs, Whimsey can be a little selective about her friendships, so finding the right canine companion will be important. She would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home, where she could soak up all the love and attention from her family while continuing to enjoy opportunities to socialise with other dogs on walks. She cannot live with cats.

Whimsey has such a sweet heart and has already shown just how much progress she can make when given kindness, patience and understanding. With the right home behind her, we know she will continue to blossom into a wonderfully affectionate companion and a much-loved member of the family.

Whimsey arrived with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which has been treated by our veterinary team. Our vets have also noted that she has a fractured canine tooth with no root or nerve exposure. At this stage, no treatment is required, but it should be monitored by her adopters and their own vet. She has also received treatment for a urinary tract infection, which has been successfully managed under veterinary guidance.

Oh, my heart. Whimsey has completely stolen it.

She is honestly one of the most loving, affectionate, and gentle girls I've ever met. The moment I walk into her kennel or sit with her in the yard, she melts into me. All she wants is kisses, cuddles, and to be as close to you as possible. She has so much love to give!

She's doing so well with her dog socialising too and absolutely adores her best friend, Royal.

Whimsey is going to make the most incredible addition to a very lucky family. She deserves so much more than just being someone's dog. She deserves to be a cherished member of the family, included in all of life's little moments, loved unconditionally, and never made to wonder if she's enough again.

I truly can't wait for the day she finds the home she's been waiting for. Whoever gets to call this beautiful girl theirs is going to be incredibly lucky.

Whimsey has come on so well since she first arrived. She’s bonded with me so much and always welcomes me with a big kiss and cuddle.

She can be nervous and unsure around new people, but with time, patience, and understanding, she’s going to make the most wonderful addition to someone’s home.

Although she needs to be the only dog in the home, she can happily socialise with other dogs and loves going down to the big yard with her friends.

Whimsy has come to us from a breeder and is a very worried girl. When she first arrived, she was very unsettled at the moment and could be quite skittish, finding so many of the sights and sounds of the world quite overwhelming. Since arriving she has started to settle in and come out of her shell, but will still need time and TLC as she settles in to her new life. Once she gets to know you, she will quietly approach you and allow a gentle fuss.

Whimsy needs time to learn and to trust, and needs a calm and quiet home home that understands ex-breeding dogs and will allow her the space she needs to learn about trust at her own pace. She will need a calm, patient, and understanding family who are willing to let her take things slowly and gently as she begins to discover the comforts of home life.

She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her home that she can look to and rely on as she learns about home life and settles in. Having a canine companion to guide her will really help build her confidence and show her that the world can be a safe and happy place.

Whimsy does walk well on a lead, but as she can be a bit skittish, her adopters will need to take the outside world at her own pace, allowing her the time she needs to gain confidence in her surroundings without feeling pressured.

Whimsy seems like she has such a sweet heart, and with time, patience, and kindness, she will begin to show her loving and gentle nature. She just needs someone special to help her learn about trust and companionship and to show her that she is safe and loved.

Whimsy has come to us with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which is being treated by the vets. Our vets have noted that she has one fractured canine, but no root or nerve exposure and so it is advised to leave it at this time, but will need monitoring by her adopters and their vet. She is currently being treated for a UTI and will be rechecked once the course of medication has finished.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Nelly
description:
I will need an adult only home with breed-experience.

I’d like to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on the lead but I am strong, so I will need continued training!

I have lived in a home, but may need a few reminders as I settle in.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Nelly, also known as 'Nellyphant' amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

Nelly is a typical fun-loving Bulldog girl who is full of character. She loves attention, affection and being involved in everything her people are doing. She enjoys a good play session, especially when there is a ball involved! Tennis balls, footballs, honestly, anything she can throw around will make her happy. She is even learning that dropping the ball means the fun can start all over again. Once playtime is finished, she is just as happy settling down for a well-earned rest.

Sadly, the instability Nelly has experienced has left her feeling worried when she is left alone. She can become distressed when separated and will need a home where she is not left for long periods. Her adopters will need to build up time apart gradually, using patience and consistency to help her understand that her people will always return.

Nelly is currently learning about other dogs and is not yet comfortable around them. She is doing brilliantly with her muzzle training, which allows her to enjoy her walks safely while she learns that other dogs are not something to worry about. She can enjoy walking alongside calm, quiet dogs, but she may react if she feels overwhelmed, especially with larger dogs or if another dog barks at her first. Her new family will need to continue her muzzle training on walks and support her with positive, patient guidance.

Nelly can already walk on a lead, although she is a strong and enthusiastic girl who can pull when excited. She will need adopters who are confident handling her and who are happy to continue her lead training. She loves getting out for walks, having zoomies and exploring, but she is equally happy being a cuddle-loving couch potato afterwards.

Nelly has come from a home before, so she may already understand some household routines, but she may need gentle reminders as she settles into a new environment. She will need an adult-only home with breed-experienced adopters who understand her bouncy nature and can provide the boundaries, consistency and love she needs. She will need to be the only dog in the home, with no visiting dogs and no cats. She will also need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft+.

Nelly is wonderful at the vets and loves the attention she receives there. She enjoys spending time with the staff, soaking up the fuss and showing everyone what a friendly and affectionate girl she is.

Nelly is a resilient, loving dog who has been through more than she should have, yet she continues to greet the world with excitement and affection. She is ready for a family who will spoil her, make her feel safe and show her just how wonderful life can be. For lovers of Bulldog breeds, Nelly’s silly personality and loving nature are sure to bring endless joy.

*Nelly has been measured by our local Dog Licensing Officer and confirmed that she is not considered a banned breed.

Nelly, AKA 'Nellyphant', plays football and she’s amazing at it! She also absolutely loves a herding ball. In fact, Nelly would play with any ball or toy for hours if she had her way, and we have to remind her to take breaks and relax for a bit.

Nelly has an exuberant nature, and no day is bad when Nelly's about. Nelly is now muzzle trained and proudly trots along the lanes near the rescue, donning her bright pink muzzle.

Nelly really is a delightful, confident, and human-loving dog, and as much as she likes to play, she will settle down and chill, often contentedly hanging out with the office staff at the rescue whilst they're busy working away.

Nelly's ideal home would have no other dogs and adult humans who have plenty of time to play and hang out with her, as well as knowledge and experience of bull breeds.

This super lady really does deserve to find a lovely home of her own soon.

Nelly, also known as Hippo amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

name: Laurence
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I am fine with cats.

I'd like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 16 teeth extracted and would benefit from a soft food diet.

Laurence is a sweet boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a loving forever home. He has been described as an absolute gentleman, and it is easy to see why. Although he can be a little wary when meeting new people, with a gentle introduction he is quick to make friends and enjoys gentle fuss and attention. He has settled beautifully into his wonderful foster home, where he has been experiencing home life for the very first time, and he has embraced it far better than anyone could have hoped.

Laurence has made incredible progress in foster and his confidence has grown enormously. He now walks calmly by your side, taking in the world at a relaxed pace, and thoroughly enjoys getting out and about. He has also taken wonderfully to home life, sleeping soundly through the night and happily settling wherever he is shown. He thrives on the comfort of a routine and has become a fantastic house guest.

Laurence gets on wonderfully with other dogs and relies on their company for comfort, so he will be looking for a home where there is at least one kind resident dog to be his friend, ideally one of a similar size. He loves the company of his canine companions and is beginning to discover the joy of playing with dog toys. He is in foster alongside three resident dogs, two large dogs and one small dog, males and females, and gets along with them all brilliantly. He is also living alongside a cat and chickens, so in the right circumstances he may be able to live with a dog-savvy cat.

A true gentleman, Laurence has now met people of all ages. He is polite and appropriate when meeting new people and, once he feels comfortable, happily accepts gentle fuss and affection. At home, he quietly seeks out cuddles from the people he trusts and has so much love to give.

Laurence would love to find a patient and understanding family who will continue to build on the wonderful progress he has made. He has embraced family life beautifully and is sure to thrive in a loving home where he can continue to grow in confidence. He will need a secure garden with 6ft fencing to ensure he remains safe.

Laurence has had 16 teeth extracted at the time of his neuter and benefits from having some of his kibble soaked to make it easier to eat, although he has an excellent appetite and enjoys a varied diet. He has also had a cyst drained from his left hip, which may recur in the future but should not cause him any problems.

Laurence is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. If you are looking for a calm, kind-hearted companion to share woodland walks, cosy evenings at home and all of life's adventures, Laurence could be the perfect addition to your family.

Laurence has been given the Gift of Life by Deb Huggings

Laurence has made incredible progress since moving into foster care. His confidence has grown enormously, and he now walks calmly by your side, taking in the world at a relaxed pace.He loves the company of dogs of a similar size and is beginning to discover the joy of playing with dog toys. His appetite is excellent, and he enjoys a varied diet, with some of his kibble soaked to make it easier to eat.Laurence sleeps soundly throughout the night and is happy to settle wherever he’s shown. He thrives on the comfort of a home routine and has embraced family life beautifully.A true gentleman, Laurence has now met people of all ages. He is polite and appropriate when meeting new people, happily accepting gentle fuss and affection once he has been introduced and feels comfortable.At home, Laurence enjoys his cuddles and quietly seeks out affection from those he trusts. He has so much love to give and will make a wonderfully loyal companion for a patient family who will continue to help him flourish.If you’re looking for a calm, kind-hearted dog to share life’s adventures—from woodland strolls to relaxing evenings at home—Laurence is waiting to meet you.

Laurence has now been in foster care for just over a week, and he has settled into home life remarkably well. He quickly adapted to the household routine and has been fully housetrained since his very first day.

He currently lives happily alongside three resident dogs - two large dogs and one small dog, both male and female - and has had no issues with any of them. Although he prefers to sleep downstairs on his own, you can often hear him listening to the gentle snuffles of the household upstairs during the night.

At home, Laurence is becoming increasingly comfortable with his foster carers. He now happily accepts gentle strokes much of the time and is beginning to enjoy human affection more and more as his confidence grows.

As with many newly rescued dogs, Laurence is still very aware of open gates and exits. For his safety, his foster home uses a second gate as an extra layer of security, and his future home will need to be mindful of this while he continues to settle.

Overall, Laurence is a wonderfully calm, gentle soul with so much love to give. He is looking for a patient, understanding family who will allow him to continue building his confidence at his own pace. In return, they will gain a loyal and affectionate companion who is already showing just how much he has to offer.

Laurence is a sweet boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a loving new home. He has been described as an absolute gentleman, and it is easy to see why. Although he can be a little wary when meeting new people, with a gentle and patient introduction he is quick to make friends. Once he feels comfortable, Laurence will quietly slink over for more fuss and attention, showing his sweet and affectionate nature.

Laurence gets on wonderfully with his kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so he will need a kind resident dog in his new home to help guide him and give him the reassurance he needs as he settles in and finds his paws.

As Laurence has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. His adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he adjusts to a completely new environment and learns that home life can be full of comfort, kindness, and love.

Laurence is a gentle soul who thrives on calm companionship and reassurance. With the support of a canine friend and a family willing to give him the time he needs, we are sure he will continue to grow in confidence and blossom into a wonderful companion.

A truly sweet and loving boy, Laurence has so much affection to give and will make a lovely addition to a patient and caring home.

Laurence has had 16 teeth extracted at the time of his neuter and would benefit from a soft food diet going forward. He has also had a cyst drained from his left hip, this may recur in the future but shouldn't cause him any issues.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Crumble
description:
I need an adult-only, experienced home where I can feel safe and loved.

I want to be the only dog in the house. No cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I love my walks so one or two a day would be great!

I’ve never lived in a home, so I need to learn housetraining and lead walking.

I have Grade 2 luxating patella, which may improve with exercise.

Crumble is a lovely lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings. She seems to be gaining confidence each day, which is wonderful to see.

While she can still be sensitive and appreciates having her space respected, it’s clear that Crumble simply needed time to feel safe. With gentle reassurance and plenty of TLC, her true personality is beginning to shine through. She is a gentle soul who responds best to calm, kind interactions and slow introductions.

She would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where se can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with her new family.

As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training and learning everyday routines. She will need a home without cats as she is overly interested.

We are looking for an experienced, adult-only home where Crumble can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. A quiet household with understanding adopters who are happy to let her take things slowly will allow her to truly flourish. With the right people, time, and lots of love, Crumble will make a wonderfully rewarding companion.

Crumble has a previous bite wound inside her ear, which is currently being treated and our vets have noted that she has a Grade 2 luxating patella. She has been recommended for imaging and is being monitored for any potential treatment she may need.

There’s not a bad word you could say about this girly pop. She is goofy, affectionate, playful, friendly and gaining confidence by the day! She has been trying her best to be kennel clean, no encouragement needed.

She is a staff favourite and that girls little teefys are part of her personality! Nibbling at you to show you just how much she loves to play with you, entertains her pal Criss cross and her kennel mums in the yard.

She belongs in a home where her people can show her the best doggy life imaginable while also understanding that Crumble has also not known much of the world and requires a bit of patience and care when handling her.

Taking every opportunity to play and zoom around with her best friend, Criss Cross.Her confidence is growing and enjoying her walks and greeting new people at her own free will as long as she is guaranteed some fuss or treats.

She enjoys sprawling out on the floor with her chew toy just enjoying the vibes.When she finds her home she will be very eager in sharing her affectionate nature with her family

Crumble is becoming a very happy chow now and has recently discovered that there's no limit on zoomies. She does get along with her chow friend, Criss Cross, but isn't keen on other dogs, so is looking for a home as an only. She is wary of people initially, but once you've gained her trust she becomes your absolute best mate. She loves her walks and gets very excited when she sees you bringing her harness towards her. She's a big foodie too and loves treats.

Crumble is coming on so beautifully and it truly makes my heart melt. Today we had some cuddle and play time in her kennel, and it was such a special moment. For a girl who once wasn’t very happy with touch, she’s now rolling over for belly rubs, snuggling in her bed, and even playing “paw paw” with me.

She’s also learning about wearing a harness and is improving every day. If you have a Crumble shaped hole in your life, she really is something special.

Crumble is a worried lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings.

Crumble will need a confident and friendly resident dog who can help guide her and show her the ropes. As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training, lead walking, and learning everyday routines. But will need to take things slow to start with some garden sniffs adventures on the lead may be too scary to start.

Crumble has a previous bite wound inside her ear, which is currently being treated.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Toast
description:
I would like a quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I live with a cat in my foster home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in (6ft+)

I'm harness training currently but need to build my confidence around lead walking.

I will need to learn about house training and lead walking

Toast is a delicate little girl who came to us from a breeder and has been slowly finding her confidence in the world. When she first arrived, she was very nervous and overwhelmed by everything around her, often running to hide in her bed.

Since arriving in foster, it has become clear that Toast is an extremely nervous girl and remains very unsure of new situations. She does not enjoy handling and can panic when she feels pressured, so she will need careful, gentle management and time to feel safe.

Toast is currently living with a cat in her foster home and can live with a dog-savvy cat who respects her space.

She will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous ex-breeding dogs and can support her without expectation or pressure. A calm, predictable environment will be essential for her ongoing confidence building.

She has come on in some areas, but handling still needs to be approached very carefully. While she has previously shown some progress with being picked up and having a harness fitted, this must always be done with patience and awareness of her limits, as she can become overwhelmed.

Toast is currently working on her harness training, and does allow her foster mummy to put one on her now, but she is not comfortable on a lead just yet and will need continued support and encouragement to build confidence. She is still learning about house training, and seems to be clean in the home when her foster mummy is around but can have a few accidents when she is left alone. With time and patience, she will begin to pick this up and understand the rules of house training.

She need a kind, confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and provide reassurance as she adjusts to home life.

Toast arrived with a low-grade luxating patella on her left side, which may improve with gentle exercise. She has also been treated for mucky ears, right-sided otitis, hot spots, and dermatitis, all of which are improving with care. Her general health will need to continue to be monitored in her new home, with any future treatment provided as needed.

Behind her shy beginnings is a sensitive little dog who is still learning to trust the world around her. With patience, understanding, and the right experienced home, Toast will continue to take small steps forward at her own pace.

Toast has arrived in Foster and continues to be a very frightened little girl and can panic easily if anyone tries to pick her up, so she really doesn’t cope well with handling at this stage. Once she is settled in her bed, she is a little more comfortable and will allow gentle strokes and will accept quiet reassurance and talking.

She is extremely nervous overall and will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand how to support a dog like her at her own pace, without pressure. She is also currently living with a cat in her foster home.

I can't believe toast has been here so long that she was due another haircut with me!She has come on tremendously for handling and as long as you're gentle she is content with being picked up, as well as having a harness put on. She is on the journey of learning to walk on a lead and it shouldn't be long before she achieves it.

I've worked with Toast for a while now and I have been able to see how much she's grown over time, especially when it comes to being groomed. The bath is still not her favourite place to be, but she tolerates it, and I think she quite enjoys the warm air of the dryer. She ends up with such a cute haircut because she is so well behaved when it comes to the styling.

This small dog has such a big and beautiful personality and I believe in the right home with another confidence dog she will flourish tremendously.

Toast was such a nervous girl when she came in and she has come on really far since then. I had the pleasure of giving her a much needed groom and although she was nervous she took to it like a champ. She will need grooming upkeep in her forever home to look after her evergrowing locks and I think with a few more pampers she will feel so much more comfortable with it.

She's currently having harness training so she can be more comfortable with the sensation and has gotten much better at being picked up and handled although she can still be a bit jumpy at times but once she's in your arms she's quite calm. She still has a ways to go but I'm so proud of her progress so far and can't wait for when she flourishes with her forever family.

Toast is a delicate little girl who has come to us from a breeder to start her journey towards a brighter future. Right now, the world feels like a very big and scary place to her, and her first instinct is to run and hide in her bed. However, once in your arms, she is easy to handle and accepts gentle reassurance with quiet trust.

Toast will need a calm and understanding home with patient adopters who can give her all the time she needs to find her feet. A kind and confident resident dog will be essential to help guide her, show her that the world can be safe, and give her the courage to explore new experiences.

As she has never lived inside a home before, everything will be new to her, from walking on a lead to learning about house training and family life. Gentle encouragement and plenty of love will help her begin to understand how wonderful it feels to be part of a home.

Toast arrived with a low-grade (Grade 1) luxating patella on the left side, which may improve with gentle exercise. She is also being treated for mucky ears and right-sided otitis as well as dermatitis.

Toast may be shy now, but behind those worried eyes is a sweet girl who just needs the right people to help her shine. With kindness, patience, and a little guidance, she will blossom into a loving and loyal companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Margate
description:
I need an experienced adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, though may be able to live with a calm female.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I can resource guard and will need adopters who can manage this.

I’m fully vaccinated and neutered. I have received treatment for an ear infection.

Margate has now spent over2 and a half years in kennels. That’sover 900 daysof waiting. Waiting while thousands of people have walked past his kennel. Waiting while his friends have come and gone. Waiting for someone to truly see him.

Everyone here adores Margate - he’s smart, affectionate, and bursting with personality. But love from staff isn’t the same as a forever home, and Margate is more than ready for his next chapter.

Since staying with us, Margate has received a dental treatment and had a cyst removed from his back left leg.

Margate came to us from a breeder in November 2023. He'sincredibly intelligent,loves a challenge, and will do absolutely anything for a tasty treat. He picks up tricks like lightning - he knows “sit”, “paw” and “speak” and he’s always ready to learn more. He thrives when his brain is engaged and would be an excellent candidate for scent work or activities like cani-cross (on-lead only!). He’s been described asone of the smartest dogs we’ve ever worked with.

He'svocal, a bit cheeky, and loves to tell us when it’s breakfast time - you can hear his excited barks all the way from the car park. He may come off as bouncy and bold, but beneath the surface, Margate is a sensitive soul who, sadly, has beenlet down by humans before. He can get worried easily, especially in overwhelming environments like the vet, where he becomes a bit of a puddle of anxiety (though he's muzzle-trained and manages with support).

Margate does require avery specific kind of home, and we won’t sugar-coat it - he’s not a “starter dog.” He needs:

Margate ispossessive around food, toys, and bedding, likely stemming from insecurity in his past. These behaviours are manageable - we’ll give guidance - but his adopters will need tounderstand and work with him, never punish or push him beyond his limits. Setting him up for success is the key.

Margate will test you - not because he's difficult, but because he's clever, spirited, and sensitive. But once you have his trust, you’ll havea bond that’s unbreakable.

Because Margate isn’t a dog you can bring home on a whim. He’s forsomeone extraordinary. Someone who sees past the behaviours and looks into his big, soulful eyes and says,“I’ve got you now.”

Margate has come so far during his time with us - he’s learned manners, made friends, gained confidence, and shown us theincredible potentialhe holds. But he deserves so much more than life in a kennel, no matter how much we love him.

Margate isnot for everyone, but if he’s for you - truly for you - then you are in for the mostrewarding journey. He’ll love you with his whole heart, and you’ll wonder how you ever lived without him.

If you think you could behis person, please don’t wait another day.

Margate’s forever is long overdue. Let’s not make him wait another year.

Margate will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

“My boy, Margate… I see all of you, and I’ll love you like you’re my own until your forever person comes along. I’ll be so jealous of whoever gets to share their life with you.”

Mr Margate has utterly blown me away in recent times.Around a month ago, Margate had an unfortunate accident in the play yard, which lead to an emergency vet visit and his front paw needing stitches.

As one of the kennel managers, I see and interact with Margate regularly, but unfortunately I don’t get the luxury of working closely with him. But I think the story below highlights how much this beautiful boy wants to do the right thing.

I was the first person to get to Margate after his accident, do you know what he did when I got to the yard? He limped over to me, sat at my feet and cried out. I know some will say it’s anthropomorphism, but I am so sure in that moment, he was asking for help!

We had to carry Margate up to the top of the rescue to clean him off and assess his wounds, Margate is muzzle trained which meant we could safely assess his wounds without any risk - but honestly, he was SO well behaved. Yes he needed reassurance that he was, in-fact, being a good boy, but he blew me away with the trust he gave us.

We cleaned him up and quickly realised he needed to go for assessment with an out-of-hours vet. So, phone calls were made, and off he went, carried into a strange car and taken to a strange place and sedated for stitches… where again, he was such a good boy despite the pain he must have felt.

Upon return, poor Margate was on strict rest, with only short toilet walks, having bandage changes every few days, boots on and off for walks… his whole routine was turned upside down. Living in kennels, his world is already quite small, and these changes, although temporary and for his own good, made his world even smaller.

This is where Margate began to struggle a little; in pain and insecure, some of his guarding behaviours (which we haven’t seen for a long time) did resurface. Luckily, Margates main carer knows him inside & out, like the back of her hand, and created a plan for everyone to follow to help build his confidence back up. Just some small adjustments to keep him & everyone around him safe, which worked beautifully and we got to see the best of our boy again, despite still being on rest.

A few weeks have now passed, Margate has had his stitches out, his wound has healed beautifully - and he fully back to being our incredible, charismatic, clever, fun loving boy! It’s the highlight of my day to see Margate, he is so happy meeting everyone.

All of this is to say, Margate may not always be an “easy” dog, but he SO wants to do the right thing. Occasionally, his worries overwhelm him, but for someone with experience and patience, the love and joy you will receive in return will be so worth it.

Margate is, hand on heart, one of the most phenomenal dogs I’ve ever met, and after nearly nine years at Many Tears, I’ve met a lot of dogs! He is going to be someone’s absolute best friend and the most wonderful adventure companion.

His profile already covers all of his basic needs, so I won’t repeat those here, but I can honestly say that not a single day he’s spent in kennels has been wasted.

He has grown, learned, and loved so much during his time with us. His confidence has blossomed, he absolutely adores people, and he has made some lovely doggy playmates. He knows exactly which treats are his favourites, and he’s settled beautifully into his routine. He heads out to his yard at 9am, then off to reception to spend time with more people (and, of course, collect more treats!).

Throughout the day, different staff members make time to visit him for extra cuddles and attention, and he often spends my entire lunch break relaxing in the yard on sunny days. This is something he enjoys every second of.

Margate is such a genuinely lovely guy, which makes it all the more surprising that he’s had to wait so long. He has the sweetest nature and seems to want nothing more than to be everyone’s best friend. While he’s here, he’s made some great female play friends and absolutely loves spending time with them every day, soaking up the companionship and fun.

In one month's time Margate will have been waiting a full two years for his forever family to find him. He's been in our care for a full 23 months, that's around 700 days, he's never been adopted or gone to foster so he's not been returned to us, he just has been in the rescue for all that time, waiting.

The first picture is his original booking in photo, a very worried boy who arrived knowing nothing about what we would do for him and how much love he'd come to find in this place that should be a pit stop until their forever home is found. But he slowly grew to love people, he started to let his true personality shine through and he started to learn how to be the goodest boy in so many ways. We flash forward to today and I can still see his insecurities at times, these may never truly go away, but we help him through it all and he is one of the best dogs I have ever known.

I love him as I love my own adopted dogs and I try to let him have as much time and love as I can give him to help him not feel like a single day in kennels is wasted. Because this is two years of his life that he won't get back, so I damn well hope that I, and everyone else who has had a part in his journey, makes every single moment count!I know he'll always have his quirks and he does need a specific type of home with people who understand and can positively manage his guarding behaviours so that he doesn't feel the need to show these often. But he's such a good boy, he's so loved by all of us at the rescue, he's so smart and beautiful and funny and loving and such good company. I love every speckle of white he's grown on his face in these two years, I love every snuggle we have and every single moment he looks to me to let me know that everything is going to be okay.He needs the right home but more importantly, he deserves the right home, the right people. If I could move heaven and earth to give him his perfect life, I would.I do want him to leave the rescue, but only to people that can fully commit to keeping him safe and listening to every single guideline and boundary that we give them. One of which is that HE MUST be kept on a lead at all times when out of fully secure areas, his prey drive is very high and he deserves to be given everything he needs to be kept safe from being harmed, which means keeping him on a lead!I shall continue to love him with every day that he's in my care, as well as every day after he finds his perfect home and I wave him off.I'll be so happy that he was chosen but he's going to leave a huge hole in my heart. He's truly one in a billion.If you feel you may be the right fit, please read his profile completely and fill in a very detailed application form. We will be very particular about where he goes, because that is the least he deserves from us.My handsomest boy, Mr Margate

It's strange really, the bond you have with a dog on your section, especially if they're a long stayer.

They aren't your dog and yet you love them as though they are, you cuddle them and tell them how amazing they are, you pour your heart and soul in to them and try your very hardest to make each and every day special in some way because their time in kennels shouldn't be a waste or simply a means to an end.. it should matter and they should be living their life whilst waiting for a family of their own.

This is hard to do when there are so many dogs to care for, but you try to do the best for them and to make sure they know how truly special they are.

This is very much the case for my best friend, Margate (AKA Maggie, Margaret, Marjorie, Marge and he responds to all these names). He is the epitome of special, he does need a specific home with people who don't put him in bad situations, but when the right people come along, they'll be adopting a dog that will give them an absolutely smashing best mate and although I am desperate for his forever home to find him, the thought of saying goodbye to the most special boy with a heart the size of the moon and a brain that's double that still. I will feel as though I'm missing a huge chunk of my heart.

That's the job though, and in a strange way, that sadness is the most rewarding part. To be a part of finding them the perfect match that will not love them in spite of their quirks, but because of them. Someone who will choose them day in, day out with a certainty that just grows with every passing day. The love a dog shares with you, no matter for how brief or long, as many will know, stays in your heart forever.

I shall miss my best mate, Margate. His family will love him the longest, but I loved him first and I am so so grateful for that.

If you are interested in being the exceptionally lucky human that shares their life with this beautiful soul, then please read his profile and apply if you feel that you can give him all he needs.

Another day for Margate in kennels, after another week, another month... I'm just hoping that he doesn't have to wait until the another year mark.

Margate has been waiting for seventeen months for his ideal home to find him, that's 506 days in the same place, with people who adore him, but they're not just his people. He has to share his time with so many other dogs that are waiting for their forever homes, but none have been waiting as long as him.

He does require a special home, with people who can help him thrive and who will not fail him! But as long as they understand his needs and set him up for success, they'll get so much in return.

Margate needs a cat, child (resident and visiting) and small furry free home. He needs mental stimulation and he needs a good deal of exercise too, he is smart, so so soooo smart and this is where his humans will have to try and be smarter.

Margate learns everything very quickly and will need to have clear, set boundaries in his new home from the get-go. He will need to be given his own bed, that he learns is his bed and that he isn't allowed on the sofas or other furniture, especially to begin with. He will need a home that understands how to enrich his life, to use his brain and that LOVES a good walk. He could walk for miles. He could potentially do cani-cross as he loves to run, but Margate needs to be kept safe at all times, so he will need to be kept on a lead in anything he does (unless in a secure rented dog field area). He has a high prey drive and a nose that rivals the very best sniffer dog. If you had treats in your pocket at some point this year, he'll know.

The best set up for Margate would be a home that could adapt a room to be his area that is free of food and where he could go to sleep at night, if visitors came round or if you had to pop out to go shopping etc. He needs this to be his area that helps him feel safe and secure.

Although he can act like a big tough guy, underneath it all he is extremely sensitive and can get very worried by things.

How can we blame him for being this way? He's been let down by humans over and over again, he has had thousands of people walk by his kennel during his stay and no one chooses him.. I know that in a home that FULLY understands him and puts everything in place to set him up to succeed, then he will be the bestest boy you could ever wish to know. His heart is the size of the whole universe and he just needs someone to see him and commit to him, then they'll see what I see too. My boy, Margate, I see all of you and I'll love you like you're my own until your forever person comes along. I'll be so jealous of the person who gets to share their life with you.

Disclaimer - although he picks up agility things quite quickly, this is not something he should do to a competitive level as the environment of the events would not benefit him.

It is now over a year since Margate joined us here in Many Tears.  That’s 365 days of seeing the same kennel, and the same routine and watching his friends leave whilst he gets left behind. This year it’ll be the second Christmas in kennels and whilst others are snuggled up in a warm home and spoilt with presents, it’ll be another day in kennels for him.  Everyone here at the rescue loves Margate!

What can I say that already hasn’t been said about this wonderful boy ??

He’s a real character, smart and witty. Every morning I hear him from the staff car park and you know that he’s announcing breakfast time for the whole rescue!  At times he can be loud and bouncy but deep down he’s just a little baby who loves a good snuggle.

Margate really has improved over the year, learnt new tricks, muzzle trained, met loads of new friends and loves meeting new people! He’ll happily walk past volunteers and once instructed to sit and wait he will receive a fuss.

So far Margate has only needed the muzzle for the vets as a precaution, but he tends to turn into a puddle of mush as he’s actually quite scared of the vets.

Margate does have issues regarding high value treats, toys and beds. This is resolved by removing any food in the area, removing any toys from the yard before play time and using multiple blankets for bedding. This is something that can be discussed and helped with for potential adopters.

All Margate needs is for adopters to understand his requirement’s and who are willing to work with him in a home environment.  He is such a beautiful wonderful boy who really is wasted here in kennels?

Margate is still absolutely thriving and learning every day. He is such a clever boy who enjoys his training and the company of his kennel friend. He has come such a long way, but in a home he could truly excel as long as his new humans know how to keep his training progressing and his mind busy. I really hope he breaks free soon.

Margate is one of those dogs that once you know him, you fall head over heels in love with him. He is one of the smartest dogs I've ever worked with, picks things up incredibly quickly and tries very hard to please you. He would be the perfect only dog for someone who wants to pour lots of time in to training to build a strong bond with him and who will understand that he will train you if given a chance. He's a super special guy with so much love to give, he just needs the right person to choose him and fully commit.

Margate is a super cool bocker. He loves long walks and his time in the yard. He thrives with anything to get his brain working, so stimulation games are an excellent way of working Margate. The best way to work with him is definitely food, he will do anything for a tasty treat. Be careful though as Margate can be food possessive. As you can see by the pictures he is such an affectionate boy who loves a good fuss, to go with that he is just absolutely handsome! Margate has been in kennels for some time now and he does cope well with being in kennels, but he would just absolutely thrive in an active home with someone who is willing to keep him busy and stimulated. While he's been with us he's always had a female kennel friend but he would also be an excellent only dog, so you have the best of both worlds with Margate, but due to his exuberant nature he might grate on any resident dogs a bit . Margate is a stunning young man with bags of personality and he loves all the attention and will need an experienced owner as he is a rambunctious soul. Margate is an absolute star and deserves the best life possible, if you feel you can offer him his best life get in contact. Be sure to read all the previous updates on Margate also to get the best overall idea of this smart little man. This wonderful boy has been in kennels for far too long now and is ready to find his forever home and new loving family. Will you give him the chance to progress to the next chapter in his life?

Margate is a unique boy. Firstly, Margate will need an owner with some experience under their belt, to make sure his rehabilitation is successful. It is probably best that he is homed as an only dog, as Margate struggles to get along with some dogs due to his boisterous personality, which can be overwhelming. This doesn't mean he can't be homed with another dog, as he has had a few kennel friends at the rescue that he gets along great with, he just prefers human attention. Margate will not trust strangers 100% straight off the bat , he's always excited to see people and interact with them, but to build a bond of trust takes some time. However this is an experience that I've found extremely rewarding. I discovered this when I took him to the vets for an intimate checkup, and was surprised to discover that he would only allow me to carry out the checks. It absolutely melted my heart to know that he had complete faith in me. He really is a sweet, colourful personality with so much love and energy to give, he just needs some time, love and repetition with a regular owner to steer all that energy in a positive direction

Since his last update Margate has been enjoying learning tricks and enjoying fun little games. We have learnt to "sit" "paw" and to" speak". Margate enjoys his treats so was very keen to learn and being as smart as he is, picks up training in a flash. He is a very vocal boy and will bark until I give a treat. I do not give in and he will stop and wait patiently. Margate does need to learn manners so will need adopters to remind him of this and to show Margate right and wrong.

Margate has come on so well since being here and I must admit that I do have a soft spot for him. He enjoys his walks but does pull a little when he has found a sniff, but can easily be managed with lead training. I'm currently teaching Margate to sit when I stop walking, to get his pulling under control, and as Margate is food motivated, it’s easy to see that this can be managed with little trouble. He is already  getting the hang of it!

Margate does jump up on you and can jump quite high, so adopters will need to encourage Margate not to jump up, which I am currently showing him, but again he is a very smart boy who is eager to learn. He is a funny, friendly, and vocal boy who will needs adopters to be mindful of his needs and issues and redirect him properly for him to be the best boy he can. He is still kenneled with his friend who both still continue to share their bed and space together with no problems. He is still only young and I can't wait to see him flourish more than what kennel life can offer him. Please read Margate's profile and updates and see what an amazing boy he is. He is perfect for someone that loves to share an active lifestyle with their dog, and we can’t wait to see pictures of him on all his future adventures!

Margate is a gorgeous boy who I have spent a lot of time getting to know recently and has come along way since his last update. He greets you with a waggy tail and excitement when he knows you and does enjoy a gentle fuss. He is also getting used to his name and when you call him he will turn to you. Margate has very high energy and needs an active household who enjoys long walks and adventures and are able to stimulate him mentally as well as physically. He also walks on a lead but can pull, this can easily be managed with lead training and I believe will settle once he gets to go on regular adventures with his new family as he enjoys the sniffs of the world . Margate loves to learn and play and due to his breed, he will need adopters to understand the Bocker breed and the energy they have. Margate currently is kennelled with a female cocker and they spend their time together playing in the yard and rolling around in their beds together. They both get on very well!

Due to Margate's resource guarding, him and his kennel friend have bedding and blankets rather than plastic normal beds and they both share this with no problems. Margate does have food guarding issues  and is fed separately from his kennel friend. This can also be managed in a home with another dog if he is separated at feeding times. Margate does take treats from you when his kennel friend is present and has not shown any issues towards them but this still needs to be remembered. I have been visiting him when I'm not on the same section to issue treats around other dogs in proximity to get him used to being in the same space around other dogs with food and treats. With these small issues, Margate will need an adult home with no children.

Margate has mastered a few tricks with treats, learning to sit and give paw. He gets very excited when you ask him but need to tell him firmly. Margate can be jumpy and will jump on you so he will need a firm voice to encourage him manners. Margate learns quickly so I think teaching him house training, lead training as well as other tricks and manners will come quickly for him, especially with treats!

He is a stunning boy and overlooked here at the rescue. If you have a Bocker sized hole in your heart and are active, love long walks, adventures and fun. Please consider applying for Margate.

Hi! My name is Margate I am 2 years old male Bocker (Cocker X Beagle) and have found myself at this amazing place called Many Tears. When I first arrived, I was extremely worried with my new surroundings, and adapting back to kennel life was very tough. I have spent a little time in a home but because of my high energy levels and need for adventures my family wasn’t able to provide this so unfortunately through no fault of my own I have set out on an adventure to find my new forever home. In my new home I would need a child free home with no visiting children. In my new home I will need someone who understands my breed and have had experience with similar breeds. I am currently in a bedroom (Kennel) with a female Bocker called Nova. We don’t interact too much but we do enjoy one another’s company so I could be happy having another friend in my new home upon having a meet and greet at the rescue. I can also be an only dog as long as I have a loving owner who plays lots of games with me. I have mastered walking on a lead and I absolutely love to explore and go on walks so having a busy home who is as on the go as I am would really benefit my energy levels. I still struggle a little to find the toilet but if I’m shown I will definitely find a way to go in the right place. when I meet new people I can become a little shy and anxious so go slow with me, have a kind voice and I will wag my tail and ask you for some fuss. After spending a day with you i trust very easily and I will become your best friend. If you’d like to meet me I am currently at the many tears rescue.Margate is still waiting for his forever home at Many Tears and despite his struggles around food and resource guarding from humans and dogs when food is involved, all he needs is an experienced home with the ability to adapt and help Margate with this. He will bring so much joy into your home and he can't wait to be a cherished member of the family where he can go on lots of adventures and finally be loved.

Margate is a stunning but very confused boy who is overwhelmed to be here and has been through so much change recently. He has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. Initially when you first meet him he is mistrustful of strangers and unsure about being handled - he will make his worries known by growling. However once you have spent a few minutes in his company showing that you are safe he quickly warms up to you and jumps all over you for love and attention. We suspect he may have lived in a home before and then returned to the breeder hence his being unsure of people initially which is fair enough, poor boy! Margate already walks on a lead and would probably prefer to be an only dog.  Margate will need a cat free home as he is far too interested in them and a home without children or visiting children as he would find them too much. Margate may need help learning to live in a home and being taught housetraining skills. Margate is such a poor soul who just wants to be loved and to feel safe. Margate would need a home that is experienced in resource guarding and can help Margate work through his struggles. Margate can resource guard when he has food or high value treats/chews/bones around both dogs and people so this would need to be managed with an environment set up to ensure lovely Margate is set up for success.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Juice
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

18-07-26 Juice has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin the next chapter of her life.

She is a wonderful little lady who is feeling a little shy and overwhelmed at the moment, but she is trying so hard to be brave. Juice is already showing lovely signs that she wants to trust people. She will quietly hover nearby, watching you with interest and looking as though she would really like to come over for a gentle fuss, but at the last moment her worries get the better of her. We think that with time, patience, love and plenty of reassurance, her confidence will continue to grow and her true personality will begin to shine through.

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time and who will let her make progress without putting any pressure on her. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her that life is full of good things.

As Juice has never lived in a home before, everything will be a brand new experience for her. She will need help with housetraining, learning about household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to all the sights and sounds of family life. She is also yet to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, so her adopters will need to introduce this gently and positively as her confidence grows.

Juice is a lovely girl with so much potential. With a patient family by her side and a canine friend to guide her, we are sure she will blossom into a happy and much-loved companion.

She has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Juice has been given the Gift of Life by Holly Kantolinna

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Buck
description:
I would like an active home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with a calm female dog.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I can walk well on a harness and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have no tail, but this doesn't bother me!

Please meet the very handsome Buck, who has travelled all the way from Romania in the hope of finding his forever home. Since arriving here a few months ago, Buck has truly blossomed! Initially a little shy with new people, he now settles quickly and happily shows off his affectionate, gentle nature. He loves attention, enjoys fuss, and is more than happy to make new friends once he feels comfortable.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that brightens even the hardest of days.

Buck absolutely loves his food. You’ll hear his excited bark echo around the rescue at mealtimes without fail. He also really enjoys his walks and having a good run around the big yard, where he can let out all that happy energy. Buck also has the most cuddly side to him; he loves nothing more than resting his head on your lap while he slowly dozes off to sleep.

Buck was briefly adopted but was sadly returned as he didn't get along with the resident dog. Buck enjoys the company of well mannered female does and does enjoy sharing his kennel with another dog, so we would consider homing him with a laid back female dog if they were the right match. He can get a little jealous of sharing attention with another dog, but in the right home with experienced adopters this could be managed. That said, Buck would be equally happy to be homed as the only dog and get all the love and attention for himself.

Buck will be looking for an adult only home and would be best suited to adopters who have experience of owning dogs from a similar background before and who are around most of the time, so they can spend lots of time with him. He would love to find an active home where he can be kept both physically and mentally stimulated and enjoy plenty of walks and adventures with his new family.

Although Buck had never lived in a home before being adopted, he settled in wonderfully and was clean in the house. He wasn’t phased by the TV or radio and quickly found the sofas and beds! He can still be a little shy when first meeting men, but it doesn’t take him long to warm up. Buck also isn’t keen on sudden loud noises or sticks and brooms, so this is something his adopters will need to work on desensitising him to. He doesn’t like having his front paws touched, but he will politely let you know by gently pulling them away.

Buck is a truly special boy with so much love to give. He is absolutely wasted in kennels and will make a loyal, devoted companion for a very lucky family. He arrived with no tail, but this doesn’t bother him in the slightest and only adds to his charm. Please don’t overlook this wonderful lad, as Buck is more than ready to find his forever home.

Buck has received negative test results for Brucellosis, Leishmania, Giardia, Heartworm, Ehrlichia canis, Borrelia burgdorferi and Anaplasma.

Buck will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Buck has now been with us for 7 months and is still patiently waiting for his forever home.

Buck absolutely loves the people he knows and trusts. If Buck is unsure of someone, it will take him awhile to come out of his shell and get to know them, but once they've built a bond with him, he is the most loving gentle boy, who loves attention!

Buck has plenty of doggy friends and enjoys socialising outside of his kennel environment, although he definitely has a preference for the ladies and gets on best with female dogs.

Buck can potentially live with another calm female dog who will respect his space when he needs it.

Buck is looking for an adopters who will give him the time he needs to settle and understand that he can be a very worried boy at first.

I do genuinely love Buck with my entire heart. I would love nothing more than seeing him finally settling into home life, with people who will cherish him just as much as I do!

For the past few weeks, Buck has been front and centre in our big yard play group! This is a great chance for our people-shy new dogs to meet and play with more confident long-stayers like Buck, and he's met a lot of new dogs this way, which suggests that once he's settled into his new home, he might benefit from a dog park or opportunities to meet up with friends.

Buck's best friend is another Romanian dog called Olive. You rarely see one without the other, in their yard, the big yard, or on walks! Sometimes in big yard play group, Bucky and Olive will separate from the other dogs and chase and wrestle each other for a while, and it's lovely to see. Unfortunately, Buck and Olive don't like to be kenneled together as they prefer their own space to unwind after all that time spent playing.

However, Buck has really come out of his shell with people around the rescue. He has a few people he's very close to, and is always up for cwtches with them. How can you say no that handsome face? He's also happier now to meet new people than he used to be, and now goes on walks with volunteers (accompanied, of course, by Olive) most days.

Buck can still get possessive over his favourite people, which is something we have to be aware of in big yard play group and that his adopters will need to bear in mind. He may grumble at other dogs in warning if they get too close when he's having his cuddles, though this does not usually escalate beyond a warning snap. It's likely that our sweet Bucky may not have had stable affection in his past, so he feels the need to guard that love from other dogs.

Luckily for Buck, we have plenty of love to go around at Many Tears! Hopefully, as he settles, he'll realise he is safe and loved and doesn't have to guard anyone anymore.

I’ve had the absolute pleasure of working with Buck, or “Buckaroo” as I like to call him, since the very day he arrived with us. I know you’re not supposed to have favourites, but if I’m honest, Buck has completely stolen a place in my heart.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that can turn even the hardest days into better ones.

Buck’s kennel friend, who he came over from Romania with, has recently been adopted. He adored her so much, and since she left, there’s been a little piece of him missing. Now he is the one still waiting, and it is heartbreaking knowing he doesn’t understand why it is not his turn yet.

Although Buck has shared his kennel and enjoys playdates with other dogs, always greeting them nicely out on walks, he would also thrive as the only dog in a home. He loves human attention so deeply and would really benefit from having people around most of the time to give him the love, comfort, and reassurance he deserves.

I recently took Buck out for a day to a local beach. From the moment we arrived, he was in his absolute element and enjoyed every second of it. Buck spent the majority of the time on a long line; although he ran around and explored, he also came back to me when called and always turned to make sure I was still close. This just shows how much of a loyal companion he can be.

I honestly love Buck with my whole heart, and it breaks me a little every single day knowing he is still waiting for his people to come for him. He has so much love, loyalty, and joy to give; he just needs someone to give him that chance.

It’s been a few weeks since Bucks arrival, and oh my has he made his presence known. Every single staff member who has had the pleasure of meeting this boy is utterly obsessed, and it’s very clear as to why!

Buck’s energy is infectious, he is the happiest, bounciest, most adoring little man and whoever adopts him will be truly lucky!!! When you meet him you’d never assume he is 6 years old - he exudes puppy energy.

Buck loves to play with his fellow Romanian buddy Jenny and they get along great. He also goes for play dates with the lovely Orietta, and he thoroughly enjoys it. He would like adopters who have experience with owning dogs before and who are around most of the time.

This sweet sweet boy is absolutely wasted in kennels, he is bursting with love to give and he’ll make a very lucky someone the happiest person in the world. Our foreign dogs are often overlooked and tend to hang around in kennels much longer than needed - please don’t let this be the case for our lovely Buck.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lady
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need another kind resident dog in my new home. I haven't met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 1 tooth extracted and am ready to find my forever home!

Lady has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a sweet and gentle girl who was a little worried to find herself here when she first arrived, but did start to soon become very inquisitive and was trying so hard to be brave. She has since moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in well and learning all about home life for the first time ever.

Lady is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle at her own pace and build her confidence, she would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs. Her confidence is starting to grow and she will now allow her fosterer to gently stroke her and seems to enjoy this.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her feel secure as she settles in. She can guard her food bowl from other dogs, so she will need to be feed separately in her new home and will need adopters who are confident managing this, but she hasn't shown any signs of guarding treats.

Lady had never lived in a home before moving to foster, she is starting to learn all about home life and house training and is toileting on newspaper at the moment, so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice first around the home and garden before venturing further.

With time, kindness and encouragement, we believe Lady will blossom into a wonderful companion. Lady is a truly sweet girl, and we can’t wait to see her thrive in a loving home.

She has had one tooth extracted at the time of her spay.

Lady has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Lady has now been in her foster home for just over a week and is settling in well. She is a gentle, sweet girl who will now stand for gentle strokes and, after just a few days, was comfortable enough to allow her foster carer to clean and trim around her eyes. She is also doing well with her house training and will use newspapers when indoors.

Lady won't take long to settle into a forever home, as long as she's given the time and space to get to know her new family and surroundings. Once she feels safe, her lovely personality really begins to shine.

Lady has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a sweet and gentle girl who is a little worried to find herself here, but she has been easy to handle and is already becoming a very inquisitive little girl! It's clear that she is trying so hard to be brave and really wants to come and say hello, so we don't think it will take her too long to come out of her shell in her new home.

Lady is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle at her own pace and build her confidence, she would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs. We would consider homing her with gentle dog savvy older teenagers.

Lady has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters who can help her learn all about home life. She will need support with the basics such as house training, learning to walk on a lead, and discovering that the world isn’t such a scary place. With time, kindness and encouragement, we believe Lady will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Lady is a truly sweet girl, and we can’t wait to see her thrive in a loving home.
