name: Lily May
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a male resident dog in my new home and I am fine with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am being treated for a ear infection.

Lily May has come to us from a breeder and is now hoping to find her own special forever home. When she first arrived, she was a very worried little girl who was feeling quite overwhelmed by her new surroundings. Its clear she hasn’t had much socialisation before, so she will need lots of love and TLC as she settles into her new life.

Lily May did move briefly to a foster home, where she began to find her paws and settle into home life. Unfortunately she didn't get on with one of the female resident dogs in her foster home so she has had to come back to the rescue where she has settled back in well. She has since shown that she can be picky with which female dogs she likes to share her space with and so for this reason she will now be looking for a home with a male resident dog as she much prefers the company of male dogs. She was in foster with a cat and so could possibly be homed with a dog savvy cat.

Lily May will be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will help her settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers.

She is still very timid, but is taking everything gently in her stride. She can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area when she is settled in.

She meets other dogs well on walks and is even getting comfortable greeting their owners as well, showing just how brave she is!

As she has had limited experience in a home, Lily May will need patient and understanding adopters to gently introduce her to everyday routines. She will need support with learning about house training, however, she was already starting to do really well with this in her foster home.

She remains sensitive to everyday noises and movements, but is beginning to cope better with gentle reassurance and support. Lily May does tolerate being handled, and this will continue to improve as her trust develops.

Lily May is a sweet little girl who simply needs patience, love and reassurance. With the right family by her side, she will continue to grow in confidence and become a devoted and loving companion.

She has been treated for an ear infection, and has followed up with the vets that have said it has cleared up now.

Lily May is growing in confidence every day. She will happily come over to say hello and really enjoys a gentle fuss and being handled. She's doing well with her harness training and is making great progress on her walks.

Lily May loves spending time with her kennel mummies, and one of the sweetest parts of her day is greeting them with a happy, wagging tail whenever they come into her kennel. It's been wonderful to watch her confidence blossom, and she's becoming more affectionate every day.

I have seen Lily May make wonderful progress during her time with us. She is an incredibly sweet-natured dog who has formed a lovely bond with her kennel companion, Coan, and clearly enjoys his company.

Lily can be dominant around other dogs at times and would be best suited to a home with a compatible male dog. She walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, making her a pleasure to take out and about. She also loves attention, affection, and treats, which makes building a bond with her very rewarding.

Overall, Lily May is an absolute superstar. She is a lovely dog with so much to offer and can be handled when needed, continuing to show what a wonderful companion she will make in the right home.

Lily May has arrived in her foster home and is beginning to find her paws as she settles into her new surroundings. She is currently a very timid little girl, but is taking things gently in her stride. She has already accepted a harness well, and we will now slowly begin introducing lead walking at her own pace, which we hope will help build her confidence and support her ongoing progress with sensitivity.

Lily May would be best suited to a calm and quiet household where she can continue to build her confidence without pressure. She will need to live with another kind and confident, male dog, who will help reassure her and show her the way as she adjusts to home life.

She is still sensitive to everyday noises and movements, but is learning to cope with gentle support and reassurance. Lily May does tolerate being handled, and this will continue to improve as her trust grows.

She is also currently living happily with a cat in her foster home.

Lily May has come to us from a breeder and is now hoping to find her own special forever home. Lily May is a very worried girl who is feeling rather overwhelmed at the moment. She clearly hasn't had much socialisation before and so will need lots of love and TLC as she settles in to her new life.

Lily May will be looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to settle at her own pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and take her under their wing, but this dog would need to be male as she doesn't want to share her space with a female dog.

As she has never lived in a home before, Lily May will need kind and understanding adopters who can gently introduce her to everyday life. She will need support with learning all about house training and will need to practice walking on a lead in the safety of the garden before she is ready to explore further afield.

Lily May is a sweet little girl who simply needs patience, love and reassurance. With the right family by her side, she will grow in confidence and become a devoted and loving companion.

She is currently being treated for a ear infection.

Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Berry
description:
I need a quiet, adult only home that understands ex-breeders.

I need to be the only dog in the home, and cannot live with cats!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead but I can be frightened, so I will need to take it slow.

I have lived in a home for a short period and may already know the bascis.

I am being treated for dermatitis around my paws.

02-07-26 Berry originally came to us from a breeder in 2022 and was adopted into a home, but she has unfortunately been returned as she was still struggling to live with the resident dog. While she socialises well with other dogs when out and about, she is looking for a home where she can be the only dog, as she has shown resource guarding behaviours around high-value items such as food and treats within the home.

When Berry arrived back here, she was a very worried little girl who preferred to keep her distance. Since then, Berry has made some lovely progress. Although she can still be a little nervous in new situations and with unfamiliar people, she has grown so much in confidence with the people she knows. She now actively seeks out fuss from her handler and, if they stop, she'll gently paw at them and even have a little cry to ask for more attention.

In her previous home, Berry displayed resource guarding behaviours around both dogs and people. Around people, this can be managed by giving her a little space and swapping the item for something of higher value, rather than trying to take it away. Her guarding comes from insecurity and likely reflects a life where she never truly had anything of her own. Because of this, Berry is looking for an adult-only home with adopters who understand resource guarding, have ex-breeder experience and are committed to using kind, positive management techniques.

We have been told that Berry is clean in the home, although she may need a few reminders while settling into a new routine. She walks nicely on the lead and doesn't pull, although she can be timid and easily startled, so she will benefit from gentle encouragement as she continues to gain confidence in the world around her.

Despite her worries, Berry has so much love to give. She is simply looking for a calm, patient home where she can finally feel safe, build trusting relationships, and enjoy life at her own pace. With understanding, consistency, and plenty of kindness, Berry will blossom into a wonderfully loyal and loving companion.

Berry is currently being treated for some dermatitis around her paw area.

name: Gala
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home with no visiting kids to keep me stress-free.

I need at least one resident dog to help me feel safe, preferably a female my size.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I enjoy secure enclosed areas where I can run around, but the lead still worries me.

I’m learning to walk on the lead, it's scary for me but I am toilet trained!

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

Gala is an extremely sweet but incredibly sensitive girl who originally came to us from a breeder. Sadly, she has already been adopted twice and returned both times, as the homes simply weren’t the right fit for her. Because of this, Gala is now searching for a very special forever home with people who truly understand her needs and are committed to giving her the time, patience, and stability she has never had.

When she first arrived, she was an extremely scared, flighty, and shut-down girl who wanted nothing to do with us humans. Since then, Gala has made some lovely, if small, steps forward. She will now allow a gentle stroke while she is on the sofa, usually for around a minute before she chooses to move away. This is huge progress for her and shows just how brave she is becoming.

On one occasion, she even chose to jump up onto the sofa and sit beside someone. Although she ran off as soon as there was a slight movement, it was still a big milestone and a really positive sign of her growing confidence.

That said, Gala is still a very worried girl who carries a lot of fear, and she has a long way to go. She is still frightened of interaction and will run away when approached. However, once she has settled into one of her beds, she will stay still to be gently picked up or have her lead put on.

She remains very nervous of the harness and lead. While she settles a little once it is on, the process of putting it on is still very scary for her. This will need to be built up slowly and gently to avoid overwhelming her or setting her back. She does know how to walk on a lead, but finds it quite daunting, and the outside world is still very overwhelming. She will need time and patience, starting in a secure garden to help build her confidence before any bigger adventures.

Gala takes great comfort from other dogs and truly thrives in their company. She loves to snuggle up with them and will be happiest in a home with other female dogs — the more, the better if possible. She has already shown that she forms particularly strong bonds, often choosing a favourite companion and looking to them for guidance. A kind, confident, and playful female dog of a similar size would be ideal for her, as she finds reassurance and happiness with other dogs while humans are still a source of uncertainty.

She also has a lovely playful side beginning to emerge, and she enjoys carrying around and playing with cuddly toys, which seem to bring her comfort and contentment.

Gala cannot live with cats and will need a calm, child-free home, including no visiting children, where she can feel safe and secure.

Gala has never truly known security, so what she needs most now is patience, kindness, and someone who will never give up on her. There won’t be any overnight miracles, and she may never become a confident, outgoing dog, but with the right person by her side, we know she can continue to grow in confidence, heal from her past, and finally understand what it means to feel safe and loved.

Gala has visited the vets regarding a small mass of inguinal fat. This is not causing her any harm and is currently being left alone, but it may need monitoring in the future.

Gala has made a few small improvements over the past month. She will now allow us to give her a short stroke while she’s on the sofa, usually for about a minute before she moves away. This is massive progress for her and shows how brave she’s becoming.

On one occasion, she even jumped up onto the sofa and sat beside me. As soon as I moved slightly, she ran off, but it was still a big step forward and she did so well.

She is still very scared of the harness. Once it’s on, she settles a little, but the process of putting the lead on frightens her. It’s going to be a very slow process, as we don’t want to push her too far and risk setting her back.

She also loves carrying around and playing with a cuddly toy, which seems to make her feel more content and happy.

Gala is still happiest when surrounded by other female dogs — the more, the better if possible. She has chosen a favourite and looks to her for guidance. A confident, playful female companion would be ideal for her, as she finds comfort in other dogs while humans are still a source of fear.

Gala has been back in foster for a few weeks and she seems to be happy and loves being with her dog friends. She settles very quickly and will happily sleep on a comfy chair. But she is still a very worried girl, as although looking settled, If one of us gets up, she'll be up and running to hide out of our  way. We have found routine is the best thing for her, she is more confident with this.

She very quickly learns what to do and does get animated when certain times arrive, such as breakfast and dinner - as long as she doesn't need to be too near a human. She will definitely need a very stable home without changes and without expectation. At the moment she will interact with us from a distance ok but doesn't get close. If you approach slowly she will stay put and you can stroke her or pick her up but she's not comfortable with it and would much rather escape from you...

On the positive side, she has started to show signs of enjoying a tummy rub, she will lift her leg for more to show she's liking it - almost like her doggy instincts are getting the better of her, this is the only time she happily excepts touching that she seems to enjoy.

Putting her harness on she shakes with fear when she sees her harness and it needs putting on very very slowly. She then is happy to walk in her own surroundings on a lead, but is so scared of being outside in the big world on it and will try to escape.

However she does love being taken to a secure field where she can run around playing with her furry friends. She loves all our other dogs and interacts very well with them all. Plus she is house trained.

Her new home must be one who gives her patience and time and expects nothing in return, this could be for a long time. She needs a very stable quiet home without too many changes happening and a good routine She wouldn't react well to things like doggy day care or holidays. She needs some very gentle persuasion to gain trust on humans but without expectations so she is not pushed too far and regressed.

Gala has been back at the rescue with me for just about two months now. I also looked after her when she was at the rescue originally, around a year and a half ago. Seeing her arrive back was hard for me, but it was nice to see how much progress she’s made during her time away. When I knew her all that time ago, she was an extremely scared, flighty, and shut-down girl who wanted nothing to do with us humans. It’s very clear she has gained confidence since then and has (sort of) learnt that she can trust us humans, so it is lovely to see the difference in her. Having said that, she does still carry a lot of worry and fear, and she still has a long way to go. Steps have been made in the right direction, so hopefully she can continue learning and growing, and eventually try to put her past behind her.Gala’s biggest love is food, so this is the main thing I’ve been using to get her comfortable around me. She has learnt how to ‘sit’ and also how to give the best puppy dog eyes that I can never say no to! She waits patiently for her turn for a treat, and takes them nice and gently too.Gala does still have quite a big fear of human hands and won’t approach me for a fuss, but she is good when it comes to things such as being groomed. When I need to pick her up, she’ll usually jump into one of her beds and then stay still for me to scoop her. She knows how to walk on a harness, but the outside world is another one of her fears, so this is something that needs to be taken slowly with her. I doubt very much she’ll be up for big adventures any time soon and will need a lot of practice in the garden and very quiet areas for a good while, so this is something her future adopters will need to take into consideration.After a life full of uncertainty and confusion, her next home HAS to be the right one for her. She really needs adopters who will love her regardless of her worries and work with her through them. Most importantly of all, she can’t be given up on again. She deserves to know where she’s going to wake up in the morning and not have to worry about being passed from pillar to post. She deserves love, trust, and commitment … and not a smidge less.

Sadly, Gala has returned to the kennels after her recent adoption. Although her new family cared deeply for her, it turned out not to be the right match. This decision was made with everyone's best interests at heart, and she’s now back with us while we look for her perfect forever home. Gala is a wonderful dog who just needs the right environment to truly thrive, and we’re hopeful that her special someone is out there waiting for her.

Gala is still in foster and gradually making progress. She is still extremely hand-shy but has started to come up and let her nose touch your hand before running off! She will then come back wanting to do it again and wagging her tail (huge progress!).Gala is looking for a forever home to offer her patience and lots of time to help her get over her fears. She is fully house trained and very happy to follow our other dogs around copying what they do. She is an escape artist on a harness as she is still nervous walking on a lead, but we have found taking her to a secure dog run field is amazing for her and she absolutely loves her freedom running around. Gala is ideally looking for some playmates in her new home as she does love to run and play with other dogs.

Gala is doing brilliantly in her foster home. She loves the company of other dogs and loves to play with them but is still very hand-shy with us humans and very wary.Gala would love a home with one or more furry friends who love playing, but what she also needs is a home which would help her understand to not be frightened anymore and people who will understand it's going to take time and patience until you get any affection or love back from her.Gala has big trust issues and needs a selfless home to get her over this hurdle she is facing.

Gala has sadly returned to the kennels through no fault of her own after a six month adoption. Her adopter made the difficult decision to bring her back due to a change in their personal circumstances, and she was much loved during her time with them. She’s now back with us and receiving lots of care and attention while we help her find another loving home. Gala is a lovely dog who truly deserves her second chance.

Gala came to us from a breeder a few months ago. We are told she is a Poodle cross Cavalier cross Bichon and she is the cutest little girl but is very overwhelmed and nervous so does need an experienced home who have had scared ex-breeding dogs before.Sadly Gala was returned after a short adoption due to a change in her adopters circumstances but was lucky enough to go to a foster home. She will need a calm and quiet home and is very scared of children so will need an adult only home with no visiting children. She will need a secure garden as she is so worried she can be a flight risk.Gala will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog to be her friend and help her to settle in. She is house trained, but may need some reminders in her new home and walking on a lead is a little scary for her, so she will need more practice with this. She LOVES food and that's the way to her heart, she will take a treat from our hand, but other than that she is very hand shy and will run away if we go to stroke or approach her.This little lady just needs to find her perfect home for she can learn that people can offer her kindness and love. She is a sweet girl who with time, love and kindness will soon start to blossom.

Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Ursula
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never been on walks, but I would love to learn!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation & a hernia that will be repaired.

17-07-26 Ursula is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is confident enough to come over and greet you when you approach, but she can lose confidence when it comes to being handled and may retreat until she feels safe again. With patience and gentle reassurance, she is continuing to grow in confidence every day.

Ursula could be the only dog in a home, provided her adopters have plenty of time to help build her confidence and support her as she settles into family life. She could also happily live with a kind and confident resident dog who she can look to for reassurance as she learns about home life and continues to gain confidence.

Ursula could live with sensible, dog-savvy older children who will give her the time, space, and patience she needs to settle into her new surroundings.

Having never lived in a home before, Ursula will need patient and understanding adopters to help her with house training and lead walking and all the new experiences that come with family life.

Ursula is a gentle, affectionate little lady who simply needs a family willing to give her the time she deserves. With kindness, patience, and understanding, she is sure to blossom into a wonderful companion.

Ursula has arrived with a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation that may improve with gentle exercise but will need to be monitored in the home. Her adopters will need to be aware of this as it may not be covered by insurance. She has also arrived with an umbilical hernia that will be repaired during her spay.

Ursula has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Whispy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 2 mammary lumps removed and 2 teeth extracted.

16-06-26 Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down, and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes be a little grumbly, but this was simply because she is so frightened and overwhelmed by her surroundings.

Since then, she has started to settle in and is trying so hard to be brave.She can be vocal with people and is still nervous to approach you but with patience and kind handling she has been joining in on yard times and taking treats, but she still has a ways to go. Whispy has never known the kindness of people so will retreat to a corner when she feels stressed.

Whispy will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her all the time, patience and understanding she needs to settle and learn to trust.

She relies on other dogs for reassurance and so she will need at least one other confident, laid back resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and provide reassurance as she begins to build confidence.She can be selective over the dogs she enjoys spending time with however once she takes to a friend, she does so well with them and it boosts her confidence. She will need a very placid dog in the home who won’t worry when she is scared. She has had a few grumbles when meeting new dogs but she is just scared and needs time to develop a bond with them.

As she has never lived in a home before, Whispy will need kind and understanding adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will be too overwhelming for her at the moment and once she is more comfortable she can begin learning in a secure garden until she feels brave enough to venture further.

Whispy is a very special lady looking for an equally special home. She has missed out on so much in her life and will need a home who will take things day by day with her and give her the support and love she’s so desperate for.

She has had two mammary lumps removed at the time of her spay and has also had two teeth extracted.

Whispy has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Smith

name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would love a good sized garden to explore!

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was quite overwhelmed when he first arrived, but is starting to come out of his shell more and more each day. He can be worried when he first meets new people, but will now greet his kennel mummy with a wagging tail every day! Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

Cooper would love to find adopters who are experienced with dogs and, whilst not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who is quite overwhelmed to find himself here, but is starting to settle in and adjust to his new surroundings. Understandably, he is feeling quite scared at the moment, especially when he first meets new people. With those he knows, he is starting to come out of his shell and its lovely to see his confidence growing. Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Zinc
description:
Zinc is not ready for adoption at this time. Keep checking back for updates.

I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe but I haven’t met cats yet so I'm not sure

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am learning about house training in my foster home!

Please read below for more information about my health!

Zinc is a truly sweet and gentle older lady who came to us from a breeder. Sadly, Zinc arrived to us with very limited vision as she had cataracts in her left eye and no sight in her right eye. After visiting a specialist, Zinc underwent cataract surgery, and having some sight again has made a wonderful difference to her life. While she was always a happy, waggy-tailed little dog even without vision, she is now much more confident and curious about the world around her, happily exploring her surroundings, meeting new people and dogs, and even enjoying short walks along the beach with her foster family and their dog.

Zinc has previously had an abdominal hernia successfully repaired and has had two teeth extracted. She has very few teeth remaining and therefore may benefit from a softer diet depending on her comfort when eating. She also previously received treatment for itchy skin, which has now improved greatly,  her skin is in very good condition and her coat is now soft and shiny.

Zinc is in a loving foster home where she has settled in beautifully. Despite having never lived in a home before arriving with us, Zinc took to home life like a duck to water and has remained clean both day and night with regular trips into the garden.

According to her foster mummy, Zinc absolutely loves exploring and being involved in daily life. She is very food-motivated and will happily supervise any activity in the kitchen in the hope that something tasty might appear. In fact, she loves food and treats, really anything edible! She also enjoys pottering around the garden, keeping an eye on anyone doing the gardening, and will occasionally burst into playful zoomies around the house or garden, acting more like a puppy than a senior dog.

Zinc gets on very well with other dogs and would be happiest living with dog-friendly companions of any size or breed. She enjoys meeting other dogs out and about and is comfortable sharing her space, as long as they are kind and tolerant.

Other than food, Zinc’s absolute favourite thing is human contact. She actively seeks out cuddles and will let you know she wants to be picked up by gently pawing at your legs. She loves joining her people on the sofa in the evenings and happily accepts cuddles from visitors too. Zinc is incredibly easy to handle and truly doesn’t have a bad bone in her body, everyone who meets her falls a little bit in love with her.

Zinc is a gentle, loving soul who is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can enjoy her golden years surrounded by love, comfort, and cuddles. Whilst she is an older dog, she now has a wonderful new lease of life and her tail rarely stops wagging.

Anyone considering adopting Zinc must be prepared to continue her eye drop routine and attend occasional follow-up appointments with an eye specialist to monitor and protect her remaining eye. Please note that this eye would not be covered by insurance.

Zinc will make a devoted and affectionate companion for someone with a big heart and a loving home.

Having sight has made a big difference to Zinc, whilst she was a very happy Waggy tailed little dog without sight, now, she explores everywhere, loves meeting other dogs, and people, even having short walks along the beach, with our own dog (a big GSD).

Zinc would be happiest living with dog friendly dogs, any size or breed.  She loves her food and treats in fact anything edible, her skin is now in very good condition plus she's no longer skinny and her coat is soft and shiny.

She loves to join us on the sofa at night and really enjoys a cuddle, even from visitors, letting us know by pawing at our legs to be lifted up. Zinc is very easy to handle with not a bad bone in her body plus rarely has a toilet accident indoors.Whilst Zinc is an older dog, she acts at times like a puppy, doing zoomies around the garden or indoors, she's also keen to supervise us gardening, or anyone in the kitchen cooking as she loves food.

Anyone considering adopting Zinc must be prepared to carry on her eye drop schedule plus visit an eye specialist for future tests to make sure her one remaining eye is maintained, her eye would not be covered by insurance.Zinc is really enjoying her new lease of life as her tail never stops Wagging..

Little Zinc has settled into living in a home like duck to water. She has been clean both day and night with regular garden trips.

Zinc's eyes will be assessed again in January, she is aware of what's around her, and nothing stops her from getting around, especially if  she can smell food, as she has a very good appetite.

Zinc is still stiff in her back legs, but it doesn't stop her getting around and exploring.

Zinc is great with other dogs, she's needs mates that are tolerant for her bumping into them now and again.

Other than food, Zinc's favourite pastime is seeking out a human to be picked up and cuddled. They don't come much sweeter than this little girl. Everyone who meets her are smitten.

Zinc is a truly sweet and gentle older lady who has come to us from a breeder. She may be a little unsure of the world at first, but once she knows you, she’s all love and wags. If you call her name and she’ll happily waddle over with her tail going a mile a minute, ready for a cuddle or to curl up in your lap. She adores a good snuggle and would love nothing more than to share your bed or snooze beside you.

Zinc has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient adopters who can gently guide her through house training and all the new experiences of family life. She relies heavily on the company of other dogs, so she must have a kind, confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the ropes and give her reassurance.

Zinc is an older girl with a few age-related challenges. She has full cataracts in her left eye and no sight in her right, and has been seen by a specialist who has determined that she may need cataract surgery in one of her eyes if she is deemed as a candidate, and may need the other removed. She is anaemic so nothing can be done for her at this time, but if things do improve, we will consider moving forward with the surgeries. Her adopters will need to be aware of this and will need to be in the position to support her financially as it will not be covered by insurance. Her back legs are slightly twisted and her stifle joints a little weak due to age. She has also had an abdominal hernia successfully repaired, as well as 2 teeth extracted, and is currently receiving treatment for itchy skin. She does not have very many teeth left and may benefit from a soft diet depending on her comfortability levels while eating.

Despite everything, Zinc’s spirit shines through, she’s affectionate, gentle, and loves nothing more than being close to her people. She will make a wonderful, devoted lap dog and a loyal companion for someone with a kind heart and the patience to help her enjoy her golden years in comfort and love.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I cannot live with cats.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, the new environments, and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed, and even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience, and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him, and he was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and unfortunately making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet adult-only home without resident or visiting children to ensure he can get the structure he is needing. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house so will need a home without too many visitors and the ability to put him in a different room when people do some over. He will need adopters who are willing to meet him multiple times to develop a bond with him!

Gabriel requires a highly structured, boundary-focused home with experienced owners who are confident, calm, and consistent. He is not a dog who should be allowed on the sofa or cuddling up with toys and we would not want him to be set up for failure. Instead, he needs clear rules, his own space, and guidance that helps him feel secure and understand what is expected of him. His adopters will need to understand that he has potential to guard high value items or sleeping spaces and will need to work with him. Respecting his boundaries is essential to his wellbeing and success.

He will need both physical and mental stimulation every single day, whatever the weather. Regular walks, enrichment, and brain games are a must to keep his active mind engaged and to help him remain balanced and settled.

Despite his difficult start, Gabriel has made remarkable progress. These days, he can’t wait for his walks and becomes visibly excited when he sees his lead come out. He now allows his harness to be put on and walks beautifully, thoroughly enjoying his outdoor adventures.

Gabriel is a very clever boy and a true foodie, which makes training both rewarding and enjoyable. He already knows cues such as “sit” and “paw” and loves learning new skills. He thrives with clear guidance, consistency, and ongoing training, and will do best with an experienced owner who enjoys working with dogs and building a strong, structured relationship.

Gabriel forms very strong bonds with his people and is deeply loyal once trust is established. Because of this, he has shown signs of separation anxiety and will need adopters who are home for the majority of the time. He is not suited to being left alone for long periods and will thrive best with someone who can make him a central part of their daily routine. While he is not a dog who seeks constant physical closeness, once a bond is formed he does enjoy affection and gentle fuss in his own way.

He could live as the only dog, enjoying one-to-one attention, or potentially alongside a calm, confident resident dog who respects his space. He will need a home with no cats or small furries.

Gabriel has worked incredibly hard to overcome his fears and has already come so far. He is now searching for a forever home that will offer him understanding, structure, commitment, and the chance to live a fulfilled life. For the right, experienced person, Gabriel will be a loyal and rewarding companion.

Gabrielwill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs, or he can be homed with a resident companion that he can continue to learn and grow from, but will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

name: Topps
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I would like a daily walk and lots of cuddle time.

I'm learning house training and building confidence on the lead.

I have a slight click in my left stifle joint, read below for more info!

Topps arrived with us from a breeder and, at first, was an extremely worried and shut-down little girl. Everything was overwhelming for her, and she found human contact very frightening, as she didn’t yet understand how gentle and loving hands could be. With time, patience, and kindness, Topps has started to blossom and has already made such wonderful progress. From barking at her kennel mummy and wanting little to do with people, she now feels comfortable sitting close, taking treats, giving sweet nose nudges, and even sharing little kisses. She has recently begun to accept gentle ear tickles when she is feeling brave, a huge step for her!

Topps has now moved to a foster home, where she is starting to learn all about home life and new skills like house training for the first time. In the home, she is still a little nervous as she adjusts to her new environment. Despite this, she will spend time in the same room as her carers, happily follow for food or to venture outside, and is comfortable moving throughout the home. Although she approaches her carers with encouragement from her canine friend or the help of a treat, she will avoid close contact at times. However, she is still very waggy-tailed and really gains confidence from her furry friends.

Topps still has a way to go and will need an experienced, adult-only home where she can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. She must have at least one kind and confident resident dog, who will play an important role in showing her the ropes and helping her feel safe. A secure garden is essential for her as she continues to learn about lead walking and house training. Topps will tolerate being handled for check overs or to have her harness put on, but she is wary and needs slow handling and reassurance.

This lovely girl may be worried at first in her new home, but with patience, reassurance, and love, she has every chance of blossoming further into the happy, content little dog she was always meant to be. Topps has already shown us what she is capable of; now she just needs someone to take a chance on her and give her the forever home she so truly deserves.

Our vet has noted a slight click in her left stifle joint on palpation. This is not currently causing her any discomfort and does not require treatment at this time, but it may need monitoring in the future. We recommend being mindful of excessive jumping on and off furniture or other jarring movements. Gentle exercises to help build and maintain muscle, such as controlled walking and stepping up and down kerbs, will be beneficial.

Topps is coming along really well, although she is still quite cautious at times. Despite this, she is such a happy girl and will happily come over when she would like some attention. She absolutely loves going out for walks and gets very excited as soon as the harness comes out. She also really enjoys seeing other dogs while out and about, often going over to greet them, and she has even started to approach people on walks too. Topps is very food-motivated and takes treats from people very gently.

Topps is a happy, tail-wagging girl who has settled in wonderfully with the other dogs in the house. She loves cuddling up and sleeping alongside her canine friends, and she gets along well with other dogs she meets too.

While Topps is confident around dogs, she is still a little cautious and hesitant around people. That said, when she feels ready, she will happily come over for a gentle chin scratch or an ear rub, all on her own terms.

Topps would thrive in a home that is patient and understanding, giving her the time she needs to build trust and feel completely comfortable. With her cheerful nature and love for canine company, she is sure to bring joy and companionship to the right family.

My cheeky little lady Topps has been with me for just over a month now and she’s come out of her shell SO much in that time. When she arrived on my section she really didn’t want anything to do with me and would more or less bark at me constantly. Progress has been slow and steady over the past few weeks, but now she’s very comfortable being around me, she’ll sit near me, she’ll take treats from me, she’ll give me little kisses and nudges with her nose, AND she’s just started to accept a little tickle under her ears when she’s feeling brave … which is huge!!! I’m super happy with how well she’s doing and it gives me great hope for her future. If she can progress this much in a kennel environment, just imagine what she could do in a home with her own humans!?Topps will still need a resident dog in her new home and still no children as I do think that would be too overwhelming for her. She may be quite worried when she first gets home, but with lots of reassurance and patience, I do think she will blossom in time. She really just needs somebody to take a chance on her now, and show her how beautiful life can actually be. She deserves the world and more, so please don’t keep her waiting much longer.

Topps has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is an extremely worried and shut down girl at the moment who is finding everything very overwhelming. She is very frightened of being handled, as she doesn’t yet understand that human hands can be gentle and loving.

Topps is looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs. She will need lots of patience, time and understanding to help her slowly come out of her shell.

She must have at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and take her under their wing. This will play a vital role in helping Topps build confidence and settle in to life in a loving home.

Topps has never lived in a home before, and she will likely find this new environment very overwhelming at first. She will need gentle support and encouragement as she begins to learn about house training, and her adopters will need to take things at her pace.

She does not yet walk on a lead and will need to start slowly, practicing in a secure garden once she is ready. Because of how fearful she currently is, a secure garden is essential for her safety and confidence building.

Topps has a long journey ahead of her, but with the right family, she has the potential to transform into a happy and content dog. If you have the time, love, and experience to help her on this journey, please consider offering Topps the second chance she so desperately deserves.

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger.

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home! Read below for more!

Maggie is a sweet girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

When Maggie returned to our care, she was a very shy and sensitive girl who was quite worried about meeting new people. Since then she has settled in wonderfully and has well and truly come out of her shell! We would absolutely love to see her back in a home as soon as possible.

Maggie is now confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She could also live with another calm and confident resident dog, but they would need to be her size or larger.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead and will enjoy going for walks with her new family.

Maggie can be particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are ensuring she socialises with males here and she does have a male staff member as part of her care team and has bonded well with him, which is lovely.

Maggie will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace. Unfortunately on one occasion, Maggie became tangled in her harness and in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was purely through fear, but due to this, Maggie will be looking for an adult only home.

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and become the most lovely companion.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Nimbus
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Nimbus is a beautiful girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived, she was very nervous and found everything quite overwhelming. Since then she has started to settle in and has come out of her shell more each day. Nimbus has now moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time.

While she is still nervous, she has settled into her foster home well. She really loves her food and will sleep all night quietly with the resident dog. She has been clean so far in the home, so is doing really well with her toilet training too. She has started learning all about walking on a lead and harness and now loves to explore quiet areas, so we think she will really enjoy going on walks with her new family.

Nimbus will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and take her under their wing. It's clear how much she relies on her canine companions for reassurance.

It's clear that she hasn't been used to much socialisation or handling prior to arrival with us and she is still quite wary of people and isn't keen on being handled, but once in your arms she does begin to relax and settle.

As Nimbus had never lived in a home before moving to foster, her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to settle in and learn all about home life. With patience, kindness, and plenty of reassurance, she will slowly begin to flourish.

Nimbus has been given the Gift of Life by Scott Ferguson

Nimbus or Nell as she is known here, has been in foster with us for a week.  Nell is a sweet timid little girl and needs time and patience to help her settle into home life.

She has been clean in the house since she arrived and will now sleep all night with my dog. She loves her food, and is walking on a lead and harness in quiet areas. She really is enjoying her walks and loves meeting other dogs.

She is still wary of people and is not keen on being handled, but once you do pick her up she will settle.

She does rely on my dog and follows him everywhere, so she will need another dog or dogs in her new home, which would need to be a quiet, adult only home.

It will take Nell time to build her confidence, she has done really well so far so hopefully she will find her forever home.

With the recent heatwave, Nimbus has had a much needed and well overdue groom and I think we can all agree she looks absolutely beautiful!

She definitely appreciated being cooler in the hot weather, and it’s allowed her to enjoy the lovely weather the last couple of weeks (within reason of course!!)

Nimbus has been slowly finding her feet here at the rescue, and taking her time with opening up to us. She was incredibly frightened when she first arrived, but with time and patience from her kennel mums and dads, her true personality is slowly coming to the surface.

We find that a lot of our ex-breeders struggle more in the presence of men, but Nimbus is opening up to her kennel dad too. They’re not at the cuddling stage as of yet, but she happily comes up to him and gives him hand kisses so we think with routine, TLC and quality time spent together they’ll get there in no time!

Nimbus is a nervous, flighty little girl who has come to us from a breeder and finds the world quite overwhelming. She is touch-sensitive and clearly hasn’t been used to much handling, so she will need kind, patient adopters who can gently show her that human hands can be kind and reassuring. Despite her worries, once she is in your arms she does begin to relax and settle.

Nimbus relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of her kennel friends, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide and support her as she learns about life in a home and continues to build her confidence. When she feels unsure, she will often retreat to her bed or a quiet corner where she feels safe.

As Nimbus has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient, gentle, and understanding while she learns all about home life and house training. Walking on a lead may feel overwhelming for her at first, so starting with gentle garden sniffs and allowing her to explore at her own pace will help her gain confidence.

Nimbus is looking for a calm and understanding home with adopters who understand the needs of ex-breeding dogs and are willing to give her the time and space she needs to come out of her shell. With patience, kindness, and plenty of reassurance, we are hopeful she will slowly begin to flourish.

name: Olive
description:
I'd like a calm and quiet, adult only home.

I could be the only dog or live with a male resident dog. I can't live with cats.

I would like a secure garden that I can explore.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

Olive originally came to us from Romania as a puppy with her siblings and was quickly adopted. Sadly, she was recently returned as she was finding life in a busy city and busy household too overwhelming.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace. We feel she would really benefit from adopters with experience of Romanian dogs. Since being back with us, Olive has shown us just how sociable she is with other dogs and now happily shares her kennel with a lovely male dog called Cooper. The two get along brilliantly and spend much of their time together, often alongside Olive's best friend, Buck. We now feel Olive would happily live with another friendly male dog, although she can also be homed as the only dog. She does occasionally show some guarding behaviours around food with other dogs, but this is easily managed by feeding separately or giving her plenty of space at mealtimes. She cannot share her home with cats or small furries.

Olive can struggle with busy environments and traffic, so we feel she would be much happier in a quieter area where she can enjoy more rural walks. She can also bark at loud noises and strangers visiting the home, so this is something her adopters will need to be willing to work on with her. Her adopters will need to be patient, calm and consistent, helping her gradually build confidence and feel secure in her new environment.

Olive is house trained but may need gentle reminders as she adjusts to a new routine. She walks nicely on the lead and would love an active home where she can enjoy plenty of walks and adventures. She is a clever girl who already knows basic commands such as "sit" and "paw". Olive is a very sweet girl who enjoys being close to her people, happily sitting beside you, though she isn't overly fond of cuddles.

When Olive first arrived back with us, she was quite nervous and wouldn't approach us, but she has grown enormously in confidence during her time here. She now eagerly greets her kennel mummy every morning and has become an absolute joy to care for. She loves going out for walks with our volunteers, which has really helped her confidence continue to blossom, and she absolutely adores chasing balls around our big play yard. She is often at the centre of our larger play groups, encouraging all of the other dogs to run around and play with her. Watching Olive run freely and enjoy herself is truly heartwarming.

After spending the last seven weeks getting to know Olive, we can honestly say she has been an absolute angel. She has settled beautifully into kennel life, but it breaks our hearts knowing she has experienced the comforts of a home and is now waiting for another family to find her. She deserves so much more than kennel life and has so much love to give.

With time, love and TLC, we know Olive will blossom into the most wonderful companion. She really will make one very lucky family complete, so please don't leave this special girl waiting any longer.

Olive has tested negative for Brucella Canis.

Olive has now been with us for 7 weeks, and what an absolute angel she has been, it’s a pleasure being able to care for Olive everyday but it makes me so sad knowing that she has lived in a home and is now waiting in kennels for her forever home to find her!

Olive is always at the centre of the big play group, encouraging all the other dogs to run around and play with her, it is so heart warming watching Olive run freely!

Olive does now also share a kennel with a lovely male dog called Cooper, and the two get along brilliantly. They spend much of their time together, along with Olive's best friend, Buck.

From getting to know Olive during her time with us, we are now happy that she  could happily  with another male dog. With a few gentle introductions, she builds lovely relationships with male dogs and enjoys their company. She also gets on well with female dogs, but if there is already a resident dog in the home, we feel Olive would be happiest sharing her space with a male companion.

Olive can show a little guarding behaviours around food time when it comes to other dogs, but as long as she is fed at distance she is absolutely fine!

Olive deserves so much more than kennel life, she will really make your life’s complete!

Olive has now been here a whole month and has sadly had little to no interest!

I’ve been working with Olive since she first arrived, at the beginning, she was a very nervous girl who wouldn’t really approach me, but over time she has grown so much in confidence. Now, every morning when I arrive, she’s waiting at the front of her kennel to greet me.

Olive also now enjoys going for walks with volunteers it’s really helping her confidence build! She also absolutely loves chasing a ball down our big yard!

Olive does socialise really well with other dogs here at the rescue, however we feel she would be happiest as the only dog in the home where she can have all the attention she deserves, but she could share her home with a calm male dog.

Olive will make the most perfect companion for someone, please don’t leave her waiting much longer.
