Primrose will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will understand that she needs to be allowed to settle in and progress at her own pace, with no pressure or expectations.

She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog who will take her under their wing, cuddle up with her and offer her the reassurance she needs as she settles in to her new home. She seems to prefer smaller dogs and dogs around her size and is less comfortable around larger dogs.

Her adopters must be prepared to dedicate the time, patience, and kindness needed to help her continue building confidence. A quiet environment with no visiting young children is essential. Her fosterer will support the adopter through this process.

With patience, understanding, and love, Primrose has the potential to blossom fully and show the happy, affectionate dog she should have always had the chance to be. She just needs the right family to help her take the next steps.

Primrose has been given the Gift of Life by an Anonymous Supporter

Primrose is a very special little dog who will need a very special home.

She is an incredibly frightened ex-breeding dog whose past has clearly left her deeply traumatised. When she first arrived in foster five months ago, she was utterly petrified of people. For several weeks she would bury her head into her chest and hide under a cupboard just to avoid looking at her foster carer. Although she is still very fearful of humans, she has come a long way since then.

Primrose is probably the gentlest dog her foster carer has ever looked after, but also the most emotionally damaged. She is sweet, patient, and completely unassuming. She never causes any trouble, joins in with nothing, and asks for very little. She doesn’t interact with people or other dogs, but she does find enormous comfort in calm, affectionate little dogs who choose to cuddle into her. She seems to especially like small dogs and appears less comfortable around larger ones.

In foster, Primrose’s little canine housemates have gently helped her in their own way. They share her bed, steal her treats, pinch her food, take her spot on the sofa, and she accepts it all with quiet patience. If placed on the sofa or bed, she will happily snuggle down beside them. She does not actively seek dogs out for play or socialising, but she clearly takes comfort from being close to kind, cuddly companions.

Primrose spends most of her time in her safe places and will usually only move from one safe space to another if encouraged. She does not yet venture out confidently on her own. However, at night, when the house is quiet and her foster carer has gone to bed, Primrose becomes a different little soul. Caught on camera, she carefully empties every toy out of the toy box, and plays by herself. It is a lovely glimpse of the happy dog she may become once she feels truly safe.

Over the past month, Primrose has started to show small but meaningful signs of progress. She now looks to her foster carer for treats, especially when sitting together on the sofa, and she has rested her head on her a couple of times. These moments may seem tiny, but for Primrose they are huge steps forward.

Primrose is currently using puppy pads, as she is still too frightened to go outdoors of her own accord. When placed outside, she will usually tuck herself into a corner of the garden. More recently, if carried around the garden, she has started to show some interest in her surroundings. She is now happy to wear a harness, although she is not yet ready for walks.

Primrose will need an exceptionally kind, patient, and understanding adopter with experience of ex-breeding dogs or very fearful dogs. She must be allowed to go at her own pace, with no pressure and no expectations of quick progress. She needs a calm home with at least one small, affectionate dog who loves to cuddle, as canine companionship is essential for her confidence and comfort.

She also seems wary of men, particularly men with beards, and appears to feel safer with women.

Primrose is both the sweetest and the most broken little dog her foster carer has ever known. But after five months, she is slowly starting to come alive. She needs someone who can see the beauty in the smallest steps and who will cherish every tiny piece of trust she gives. For the right person, helping Primrose heal will be an extraordinary privilege.

Given the chance, Primrose will choose to sit on her own in one of her three “safe places” in her foster home. Whilst it is common for ex-breeding dogs that have never lived in a home before to not want to be near humans, Primrose unusually chooses not to be with the other dogs living in the house either.Whilst she has progressed significantly since going into care, we have decided that there is still a little way to go before we make her available for adoption.Primrose flees from one of her “safe places” to another keeping her body close to the ground. Her foster mum wants to see her walking upright as well as expose her to areas beyond her comfort zones, including outdoors which she currently fears, so she is better prepared for adoption.Whilst her progress is slow, she has still come along way from the early days when she would bury her head in her chest or hide behind or under furniture. She’s even played with a ball for about a minute, which her fosterer said was possibly the most moving experience she’s seen with a dog in years, suggesting there is a happy dog “inside” Primrose wanting to come out.She also uses a puppy pad if placed close to her bed. She eats well, is very gentle, and allows her quieter foster brothers and sisters to cuddle up to her. She also likes her tummy rubbed, is happy to be carried for short periods, and if put next to her foster mum, will lay down and sleep.Before Primrose will be made available for adoption we would like to see Primrose walking upright as well as walking outdoors which she still fears.Anyone applying to adopt Primrose will need experience with very frightened ex-breeding dogs that have never lived in a home. They will need to have at least one confident gentle dog,  ideally no larger than her, and a quiet home with no visiting young children. Importantly they will need to be prepared to dedicate the time it will take to help develop Primrose’s confidence, Her fosterer is happy to help guide the adopter going forwards.

Primrose is a very scared little girl and is unsure of her new surroundings. She hasn’t yet found the courage to leave her bed but she finds comfort in cuddling close to her kennel friends because that’s the only comfort she’s ever known.

Primrose needs a calm, adult only home with at least one gentle dog to guide her and give her the reassurance she needs and who will allow her to cuddle up to them for support and comfort if she wants to. She has never lived in a home, so everything will feel overwhelming at first. She will have no idea about house training and the garden may be as scary as being in the home at first so she will need adopters who have plenty of time and patience to help her.

Lead walking will be a new experience for her and should start in the garden before venturing into the outside world.

With endless patience, kindness and time, her new family will see Primrose slowly open up and blossom into the happy girl she was always meant to be.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Peanut
description:
Peanut is a four month old female cross-breed puppy, and she and her siblings were brought into the shelter as an abandoned litter when they were just a month old.

They were so tiny, they looked like baby otters – just piles of fluff that napped on each other for the majority of the day. As the pups got older, more playful and independent, one by one they were adopted locally.

Unfortunately, Peanut is now the only one left behind. All her brothers and sisters have left, and she’s been adopted into another litter of new arrivals so she’s not alone.

We would love to find her forever home now and give her the chance her siblings have had.

Peanut is never the loudest of the bunch or the first puppy to come dashing over to you. She’s a little more reserved and sensitive, and sometimes a little unsure around new people.

She was always used to her siblings stealing the limelight while she hung back, so when she does get some 1-2-1 attention she realises just how great it is and suddenly has a burst of excitement!

Peanut has spent some time with children around the age of eight, and she absolutely loved them. She was a tiny but shy to start with, but then climbed into their laps and gave them loads of kisses.

She was loving all the attention and cuddles, and we think that she would be a lovely addition to a home with gentle kids.

Around other dogs Peanut just makes friends with everyone. Because she is a more submissive character she can sometimes get trampled or bullied, but she’s learning to hold her own and stand her ground!

She has integrated alongside multiple new puppies that have arrived during her time, and she’s made friends with them all. She’s playful, loves a bit of rough and tumble, and likes having company to snuggle up with at nap time.

She would be great with another resident dog and would learn so much from having a confident company to follow in the footsteps of.

Peanut would be best suited to a calm household with a moderately active lifestyle and access to a garden. She needs reassurance, patient and time as she is adapting to a companion lifestyle.

This will be a very new concept for her, as she’s never lived in a home before. And as with any puppies, she will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Peanut has the sweetest, most charming personality and it’s so sad that she’s been left behind, but perhaps they’ve left the best til last!

name: Serena
description:
*** SERENA WILL COME TO FOSTER IN BANSTEAD, SURREY ON 13TH SEPTEMBER 2026 ***

Our extra special girl Serena is approximately two years old and a medium sized cross breed perhaps with something of a hound content.

Serena weighs thirteen kilos and measures ten inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned on the streets, Serena has been in our Cyprus shelter for around four months.

Our shelter manager describes Serena as very sweet and she has an exceptionally loving personality. Serena enjoys amazing eye contact with her favourite human and constantly wins numerous hearts.

Her sandy coat is beautifully enhanced with a white flash to her chest along with four white toe tips. Her ears are gorgeous and probably award winning, leaving Serena as visually stunning.

Serena is the ideal adoption candidate and will make a perfect addition to her forever family. She is so deserving.

Serena enjoys her time in the car and walks nicely on her lead. She also seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 3.5 month old chihuahua cross girl who is expected to be smaller medium size when fully grown. Lucy’s had a difficult start in life, she was found with her mum and sister in a deprived area where her mum had been badly treated.

Her past could have made her fearful, but luckily it didn’t, and Lucy is full of trust and love.

This beautiful girl is a happy, friendly puppy who loves cuddles and being close to people, she is a true lapdog. She is a true puppy, full of life, loves to play and explore. She is jolly happy girl with a fun character.

Lucy is a sweet affectionate puppy, she loves dogs and could happily live with a doggie mate or be the only dog in the home.

She is also happy around children and could live with older dog savvy kids.

We can also cat test her for the right applicant.

Lucy dreams of cuddles in bed, fun adventures, belly rubs and a family to love for the rest of her life.

Lucy is in Hungary and will travel to the UK once a home has been secured for her.

name: Kabo
description:
Kabo is a four year old German Pointer. He arrived at the shelter along with two other pointers, all of whom were found roaming as strays at the end of the hunting season.

The three of them are happy in each other’s company, and now they share a kennel together. As their individual personalities have emerged we’ve been getting to know them, and now we would love to find each of them their perfect forever home.

Kabo is around four years old and has no idea how beautiful he is. He’s sweet, soft and sensitive, and has a gentle, affectionate and curious nature.

He can be a little apprehensive with new people, but he’s a sucker for treats so that really helps to earn his trust.

Unfortunately, the hunting culture in Cyprus dictates the treatment of a lot of hounds, so we’re not sure that Kabo has ever truly experienced the love, security and compassion that he has deserved throughout the past few years.

Around other dogs, Kabo is great. He is friendly, very silly, playful but also provides gentle guidance to the younger dogs.

He is good with both males and females, and we definitely think that he would really enjoy a home where he had another resident dog to learn from and play with.

Without another dog, it may take longer for Kabo to settle in properly, but it wouldn’t be impossible as long as his family are prepared to give him the time and patience he needs.

Kabo would be best suited to a semi-rural home where he’s surrounded by lots of places to explore. Being a pointer, he loves to follow his nose and he’s always curious about his surroundings.

He would also be best suited to a home with a garden, as it’s likely that he has spent the vast majority of his life living outdoors in some capacity. A garden will provide Kabo with a safe outdoor space where he can acclimatise to living indoors little by little.

Once settled, Kabo will be the perfect companion for an outdoorsy family who enjoy an active lifestyle, but also want a best friend who’ll be happy snuggling on the sofa.

Pointers are fantastic cuddlers, and you won’t be able to get enough of Kabo’s velvet ears and soft muzzle.

He will need a gentle introduction to his new lifestyle, but with reassurance and understanding, he will form a deep and devoted bond with his new family. Watching him grow into a confident boy will be so rewarding!

name: Nala
description:
Nala is a 9-week-old female Presa Canario. She is a gorgeous puppy who has had the very best start in life after being born at Ravenswood alongside her brothers and sister.

Raised in a caring environment from birth, she has received plenty of attention and care during her early weeks.

Nala has been well socialised and regularly handled, helping her grow into a happy and confident young puppy. She has also been wormed regularly, ensuring she has received the routine care needed as she prepares for life with her new family.

As she begins her search for a forever home, Nala will need owners who have experience with large breed dogs.

Presa Canarios are powerful dogs that require knowledgeable owners who understand their needs and are committed to providing the right guidance.

Her new family should be prepared to continue her socialisation and training throughout her life. Consistent training and positive experiences will help Nala develop into a well-mannered and confident adult dog.

Because Presa Canarios are large and strong, they thrive in homes where their owners are ready to take on the responsibilities that come with the breed. A patient and committed approach will give Nala the best opportunity to reach her full potential.

Nala has already received her first vaccination and has been microchipped before leaving for her new home. She will also need to be neutered when she is old enough, and her new owners will be required to provide proof that this has been completed.

Nala is ready to start the next chapter of her life with a loving family that can offer her a secure and permanent home.

If you believe you can provide the care, commitment, and lifelong support she needs, Nala would love to find her forever home with you.

name: Zayla
description:
Zayla is a 9-week-old female Presa Canario. She is a gorgeous puppy who has enjoyed the very best start in life after being born at Ravenswood alongside her brothers and sister.

Having been raised in a caring environment from birth, she has benefited from excellent early care and attention.

During her first weeks of life, Zayla has been well socialised and regularly handled, helping her become a happy and confident young puppy.

She has also been wormed routinely, ensuring she has received the care needed during these important early stages of development.

Now ready to find her forever home, Zayla is looking for owners who understand the needs of large breed dogs. As a Presa Canario, she will require a home with previous large breed experience and people who are committed to helping her reach her full potential.

Her new family should continue her socialisation and provide consistent training throughout her life. Ongoing guidance, patience, and positive reinforcement will help her mature into a well-balanced and well-behaved adult dog.

Presa Canarios are powerful, strong dogs that thrive with confident and responsible owners who are prepared for the commitment that comes with the breed.

Zayla will benefit from a home that is ready to provide the structure, leadership, and lifelong training she needs.

Before leaving for her new home, Zayla has received her first vaccination and has been microchipped. She will also need to be neutered when she is old enough, and her new owners will be required to provide proof that this has been completed.

Zayla is ready to begin the next chapter of her life with a family that can offer her love, stability, and the ongoing support she deserves.

If you feel you can provide this beautiful Presa Canario with a permanent and caring home, she would love to meet you.

name: Indie
description:
Indie is a three year old Shepherd mix who was brought into the shelter after locals notified the dog warden that she had been roaming freely around the village for a few weeks.

No one seemed to know where she’d come from, or was able to advise who she belonged to. With no microchip to help us connect the dots she ended up in the shelter, and is now waiting for a new home.

Indie is a beautiful girl who just blends in at the shelter.

She doesn’t ask for much, she doesn’t demand attention, and she shares her kennel with two very silly male dogs who she is extremely tolerant and gentle with, despite their complete lack of spatial awareness or manners!

She is very patient with other dogs and gets on well with them, but equally would be fine to be homed as the only resident dog, as she’s quietly confident and independent.

Indie is a very clever girl and loves her treats. As she’s food motivated this will really help with any further training her new family might want to do with her, as she responds really well to positive reinforcement.

It’s likely that Indie is a shepherd mix, so she will enjoy training, enrichment and brain games, as dogs like her thrive with focus and direction.

The ideal home for Indie would be an active family who can offer her plenty of opportunities to explore and are looking for a loyal, devoted companion to accompany them on their adventures.

Indie bonds with new people quickly and is a very loving dog, so we think she will adapt to a companion lifestyle well.

Indie would be happiest in a semi-rural setting where she’s surrounded by nice places to walk, fields to roam through or woods to wander in.

She would welcome trips to the beach or long hikes at the weekend, and she will be able to keep up with a more active pace of life. We’re sure she’ll be very excited to experience home comforts as well though!

We don’t know if Indie has ever had the opportunity to have her own bed or even live indoors before, so her family need to be patient while she adjusts in her own time. For anyone looking for a loyal best friend, Indie would be perfect.

name: Jordan
description:
Jordan is a three year old Pointer mix. He’s super shiny, super sleek, this gorgeous boy is Jordan He arrived at the shelter along with two other pointers, all of whom were found roaming as strays at the end of the hunting season.

The three of them are happy in each other’s company, and now they share a kennel together. As their individual personalities have emerged we’ve been getting to know them, and now we would love to find each of them their perfect forever home.

Jordan is around three years old and such a nice boy! Unfortunately, we don’t think that Jordan has experienced the kindest treatment throughout his life, and it has meant that it’s taken us a little more time to convince him that we’re to be trusted.

He has however responded so well to reassurance and kindness, and is now much more confident and sociable. He now really likes going out for little walks with the shelter volunteers, and he always looks to them for a bit of guidance or a cuddle.

Around other dogs, Jordan is really friendly. He is a bit of a goon and loves to play, but he’s also friendly and gentle, especially when meeting new dogs.

He is good with both males and females, and we definitely think that he would really enjoy a home where he had another resident dog to learn from and play with.

Having another dog to observe and learn from will allow Jordan to adapt at his own pace, and with someone to look up to, to boost his confidence.

Jordan would be best suited to a semi-rural home where he’s surrounded by lots of places to explore. Being a pointer, he loves to follow his nose and he’s always curious about his surroundings.

He would also be best suited to a home with a garden, as it’s likely that he has spent the vast majority of his life living outdoors in some capacity.

A garden will provide Jordan with a safe outdoor space where he can acclimatise to living indoors little by little.

Jordan has already started to show us that when he trusts someone he is super affectionate and sweet, and given proper time to bond with a new family we know that he is going to develop a really strong, loyal connection with them.

Pointers are such fantastic companions and given the opportunity to settle into a secure and loving environment, we know Jordan will really blossom in confidence.

name: Frank
description:
Frank is a 9-week-old male Presa Canario. He is a handsome puppy who has enjoyed the very best start in life after being born at Ravenswood alongside his brothers and sisters.

Having spent his early weeks in a caring environment, he has been given every opportunity to grow into a happy and confident young dog.

From an early age, Frank has been well socialised and regularly handled, helping him become comfortable around people and everyday interactions.

He has also been wormed routinely as part of his early care, ensuring he has received the attention every puppy deserves.

As a cheerful and confident puppy, Frank is now ready to find a loving forever home.

Because he is a Presa Canario, he will need owners who have previous experience with large breeds and understand the commitment involved in raising such a powerful dog.

His new family should be prepared to continue his socialisation and training throughout his life. Ongoing guidance, positive reinforcement, and consistent handling will help Frank develop into a well-mannered and balanced adult.

Presa Canarios are large, strong dogs that thrive with knowledgeable owners who are willing to invest time and effort into their upbringing.

Anyone considering Frank should be confident in providing the structure, training, and lifestyle that a breed of this size requires.

Frank has already received his first vaccination and has been microchipped before leaving for his new home. He will also need to be neutered when he is old enough, and his future owners will be required to provide proof that this has been carried out.

Frank is looking for a permanent home where he can continue to learn, grow, and become a valued member of the family.

If you believe you can offer this handsome young Presa Canario the loving and committed home he deserves, he would be delighted to meet you.

name: Jasmine
description:
Our extra special girl Jasmine is approximately one year old and a delightful small cross breed. Jasmine weighs a humble seven kilos and measures eleven inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Jasmine has been in our Cyprus shelter for three weeks.

Jasmine is stunningly attractive. She has incredibly delicate features and the most beautiful facial expressions. This blends so well with her bubbly and fun-loving disposition.

Jasmine’s coat and markings are sublime. She has some classic black and tan with a distinctive white flash to her chest. And then there’s the gorgeous half tone brindle along her back. If ever a dog were to stand out from the crowd it would be Jasmine.

She is youthful, fun loving, affable and affectionate. Jasmine so yearns for human interaction and will make a glorious family dog.

Jasmine will benefit from more lead training but so enjoys her time in the car. She seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs and children but has a strong desire to chase cats.

name: Bonnie
description:
Bonnie is a two year old Pointer mix who was found as a stray and had been hiding in abandoned buildings across open farmland for a while before she was able to be caught.

The vet confirmed she had not been microchipped, and as she’d been roaming for a while it was clear she’d not come from a home.

She was rescued from agricultural land where strays are often found, and unsurprisingly, no one came to the shelter to claim her as their own.

Bonnie arrived just after Christmas and has been in the shelter without any interest ever since. She was absolutely terrified when she first arrived, and was so avoidant of people.

She didn’t want anyone to touch her, and would hide in the back of her kennel when anyone approached. She was then paired up with a confident male dog who has zero fear of anyone or anything, and slowly she started to realise that she was safe.

Bonnie is now a different dog. She’s still a little bit reserved and needs time to trust new people, but she’s much more friendly, so much happier, and she’s really come out of her shell in the past few months.

She is more confident in the company of other dogs, and she’s really benefitted from having a kennel friend to learn from and follow their lead. This in mind, we think she would be better suited to a home with another calm, resident dog.

Bonnie would struggle in a loud home in a busy area, so we’re looking for a laid-back home atmosphere based in a calmer residential, or semi-rural location.

She would love to be surrounded by fields and nature walks, rather than roads and buildings, and she is definitely looking for a home with direct access to a secure garden.

We know that given the time she needs, and a gentle, patient approach, Bonnie will absolutely blossom and she’ll make an amazing companion with a little time and understanding.

Bonnie has had some introductory lead training, and has responded well, but still needs a bit more work. She is a relatively active dog and would welcome long walks, but is also quite happy basking in the sun on a warm day.

Given that she’s a shyer dog, we are looking for a home with children aged 8+, so as not to overwhelm her. There’s not a bad bone in her body, but she’d struggle with a very unpredictable household, and would prefer a calm home.

Bonnie absolutely deserves a second chance and we know that given the patience that she needs, she will do so well in a new home.

She spent a long time in survival mode, so she just needs a secure environment to understand that she doesn’t have to look out for herself all the time – she’ll be treated with kindness, love and affection.

She’s already grown in confidence and made great progress in the shelter, so in a proper home she’s going to do just fine.

name: Sully
description:
Sully is a 5 year old medium size male cross breed. He looks like someone accidentally shrunk a Rottweiler in the wash. He’s handsome, compact, and has mastered the art of looking at you as if he’s contemplating the meaning of life.

Sully’s story didn’t begin so happily, he was surrendered in Hungary by a British family along with several other dogs.

They arrived frightened of people, fearful of new experiences, and clearly hadn’t been shown the love, kindness and guidance that every dog deserves.

For Sully the world was a scary place initially. But then he saw people who were kind to him, spoke gently, and gave him time. And it didn’t take long for him to realise that not all humans let you down.

Today Sully is a completely different dog, he enjoys life and likes human company, and although he still has his moments of insecurity, he is now curious and not fearful of the world around him.

He is a loyal, kind natured boy, quite placid in temperament. He isn’t a high energy dog either who would need endless adventures and entertainment all through the day, but he will happily join you on your walks and then enjoy home time sharing the sofa with you.

What he really wants though is a family who won’t give up on him.

Sully is friendly with most dogs with sensible introductions, very excitable dogs are probably not the best match for him but he could happily live with a friendly placid dog.

He is friendly around children, too, but he would probably be best suited to an adult-only home as he is not used to the noise and chaos that can come with young children.

We can cat test him for the right applicant.

He would really love to leave his shelter days behind and start a new life.

And he comes with a special bonus in that he understands English!

Sully is in Hungary and will travel to the UK once the right family is found for him.

He comes neutered, microchipped, fully vaccinated, with an EU pet passport.

name: Lana
description:
Lana is a 3 month old chihuahua cross girl from Hungary who is expected to be smaller medium size when fully grown.

Lana has already had a difficult start in life, she was found with her mum and sister in a deprived area where her mum had been badly treated. Despite everything they have been through, Lana has chosen love over fear.

This beautiful girl is a happy, friendly puppy who loves cuddles and being close to people, she is a true lapdog. She has a slightly calmer nature than her sister, but still enjoys playing, exploring and having fun.

She is a sweet affectionate puppy who could happily live with a doggie mate or be the only dog in the home.

She is also happy around children and can live with older dog savvy kids.

We can also cat test her for the right applicant.

Lana has never known what it’s like to belong to a family of her own, but she’s ready to learn. She dreams of cuddles in bed, fun adventures, belly rubs and people to love for the rest of her life.

Lana is in Hungary and will travel to the UK once a home has been secured for her.

name: Grace
description:
Grace is a four month old cross-breed. Grace’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Grace is one of the most confident pups in the litter, and even within the first couple of days after she arrived in the shelter she has been brave enough to approach new people, interact and cuddle.

Some of the other pups follow her lead as she’s a very sociable little thing and loves to be in the company of people. She warms to anyone and everyone very quickly and is definitely ready to find a family of her own.

Grace is very food motivated and was the first of the litter to learn ‘sit’. She is also accepting of the lead, which can sometimes be a bit scary for new puppies to adapt to, but she’s taken everything in her stride and learns new things fast.

She loves a belly rub, any excuse to be as close to you as possible, and she’s also very playful – the perfect all rounder!

Grace is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with. She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Grace would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and as she clearly loves to learn she’d also benefit from (and enjoy!) some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Grace has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be absolutely great living alongside kids. She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties!

But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend. She’s a wonderful young dog and we can’t wait to find her the perfect family to grow up with.

name: Godfrey
description:
Godfrey is a four month old cross-breed. Godfrey’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Godfrey is a sweetheart and it took us a little bit longer to earn his trust than some of his siblings. The girls are definitely more confident than their brothers in this litter!

Once Godfrey realised that he was safe, he ventured out to explore his new surroundings and he has been quite taken with the toys, the paddling pool (or the water bowl if the pool isn’t filled!) and the fact that so many treats are on offer! He’s realised it’s not so bad after all.

Godfrey is really cute when he gets to spend some 1-2-1 time with the volunteers, and he really enjoys being the centre of attention for a little while.

Although you can tell he’s a little unsure, he revels in the fuss and loves being cuddled and tickled. He’s a very loving little dog and once his initial nerves have subsided he’s quite the snuggler, and he also gives excellent kisses.

He’s not familiar with the lead just yet, but when he’s outside in the yard sniffing about he’s very curious about other dogs, and bravely approaches to give them a little sniff before running back to safety! He’s also one of the smaller pups of the litter.

Godfrey is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that he can learn from and play with.

He’s a very friendly boy and reads other dogs very well, and we think he would probably prefer a home with another dog, but we’re open to considering placing him on his own if we think it’s the right fit.

The ideal home for Godfrey would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. He would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As he grows into an adult dog, he will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and he would also do well with some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Godfrey has had some initial exposure to children and we think he would be suitable to live alongside slightly older children, as he can still sometimes be a little skittish.

He is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if he’s living alongside kids, for both parties! Godfrey is such a little heartbreaker and we know that someone isn’t going to be able to stop themselves falling in love with his charming little face – and we don’t blame you!

name: Gina
description:
Gina is a four month old cross breed. Gina’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gina is very confident among the group and can be a bit bossy with her siblings! She is a girl who knows what she wants, and sometimes that is the limelight!

She is always very eager to say hello to passing visitors that walk by her kennel, and she loves any opportunity to be be cuddled or played with.

She also loves chasing after a toy, a pebble or a stick – it doesn’t matter what it is, she can make a game out of anything!

Gina isn’t familiar with the lead just yet, but she’s starting to learn that it’s a positive thing now. She is super excitable and bouncy when she gets the chance to interact with people, and she bonds fiercely with those that she loves.

She is definitely going to be a very loyal companion, we have no doubt about that.

Gina is good with other dogs and on the most part she gets along well with her siblings, but she needs a bit of work on sharing. She could definitely live alongside a resident dog, and an older, calmer dog would be a great influence on her.

However, we also think she is confident enough to be the only dog in the household.

The ideal home for Gina would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and of course being a puppy she will both enjoy and benefit from some introductory training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gina has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be great for a family with school age children. She can be a bit nippy in her play, but that is purely to do with her age.

She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties! Given the opportunity, we know Gina is going to grow up into a lovely young dog with a great personality and nothing but devotion for her new family.

name: Grant
description:
Grant is a four month old cross-breed. Grant’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

At a glance, Grant looks just as confident as his siblings. He’s always at the bars of the kennel jumping up to meet new people with his brothers and sisters, and the fact that he’s the only pup in the litter with huge ears also draws a lot of attention to him.

However, Grant is actually the most nervous of the pups. As soon as he’s separated from his siblings, he is very unsure of what to do.

He is such a sweet, soft and gentle boy, and he just needs a slightly more patient, calm and understanding home who can go at his pace. We’ve seen so many pups like Grant in our time and the power of the perfect home cannot be underestimated!

Grant is a submissive boy and he’s always a little unsure around new people until he knows that they’re going to treat him with kindness.

When he gets to know you, he likes to just sit beside you and chill, and he loves an ear scratch or a belly rub.

He’s not confident on the lead yet so that will take a bit of work, but there’s not a bad bone in his body and he really does want to trust people, he just takes a little longer than his siblings.

Grant would be better suited to a home with another resident dog that he can learn from and play with. As soon as he’s away from his siblings, he panics and is visibly less confident.

Another dog would definitely help his transition from shelter to sofa, and help him feel less overwhelmed and confused.

The ideal home for Grant would be a loving, patient family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city.

As Grant is more nervous than his siblings, a calm home in a quieter area would be great for him, and we’re sure his confidence will grow once he’s settled and feeling more secure.

As he grows into an adult dog, he will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Grant is just a baby and has never had an adverse reaction to a child, but in order to keep things predictable for him we’re looking for a home with older children only.

He just needs some time and understanding to come out of his shell, and he’s only a few months old right now – he will change so much within the first few months of his adoption and it will simply take a special, caring family to give him the love and support he needs.

We’re already seeing glimpses of the silly, charming and playful little pup he is, and it will be so rewarding to see him really flourish with his new family.

name: Gilly
description:
Gilly is a four month old cross-breed. Gilly’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gilly is such a cutie and has a really joyful energy about her that makes it impossible not to love her. She gets so excited to spend time with people, and she gives so many kisses!

She’s also quite happy worming her way into your lap for a little rest while she takes in everything going on around her – she just loves being involved.

Gilly is a clever girl and is quick to learn new things. She has pretty much learned to sit for a treat already, and although she’s a bit suspicious of the lead at the moment she’s started to trust that it’s not a bad thing anymore.

She has an every wagging tail and a very happy personality, and as she’s very sociable we’re sure it won’t take long for her to make plenty of new friends!

Gilly is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Gily would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and as she clearly loves to learn she’d also benefit from (and enjoy!) some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gilly has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be absolutely great living alongside kids. She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties!

But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend. She’s a super little character and we know she’s going to make someone very happy!

name: Gaia
description:
Gaia is a four month old cross-breed. Gaia’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gaia was very shy when she arrived at the shelter and would hang back inside her kennel rather than coming out to say hi. She was very suspicious of new people, and after their rough start it made complete sense for her to be wary.

After a few weeks, and a lot of treats, we managed to reassure Gaia that we were okay to be trusted, and since then she’s never looked back!

Gaia is now a cuddly, silly, goofy and playful puppy who is so much happier than before. She has no issues being held or cuddled, and she welcomes a fuss from new people with little hesitation.

She’s not the loudest or the most front and centre of the litter, but there’s a quiet confidence about her and that will only continue to grow in a home where she has lots of focus and love.

Gaia is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Gaia would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and she’ll really enjoy the opportunity to engage in basic training, as she’s very switched on.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gaia has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be happy living with them, although would prefer a little more predictability, so school age children might be more suitable.

She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties! But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend.

Gaia is a gorgeous young dog and has all the makings of a loyal best friend.

name: Pille
description:
Pille is a 2 year old female Cross-Breed, a tiny and gentle girl with so much love in her heart.

Life hasn’t always been kind to Pille. She was found abandoned with two other little dogs and, because of her past, she can still be a little timid initially.

She is looking for a patient and understanding family and a calm, peaceful home where she can feel completely safe and loved.

Pille is a very quiet, sweet-natured little dog who adores affection. In fact, she’s the kind of little angel who will happily fall asleep in your arms.

She gets along well with other dogs, but she does not pay too much attention to them and would also be perfectly happy as an only dog, soaking up all the love and attention for herself.

Being so small, she would barely take up any room at all and she’d fit perfectly in someone’s bed.

We hope Pille won’t have to wake up in the shelter for much longer.

Pille is in Hungary, ready to travel once a home has been secured for her.

She comes fully vaccinated, microchipped, spayed, and with an EU pet passport.

name: Loki
description:
Loki, a beautiful 2 year old Siberian Husky needs a new home through no fault of his own.

The owner has serious health problems and is unable to give him the care and attention he needs and deserves. He is spending more and more time in kennels which is far from ideal.

Loki is a lovely boy, he loves his toys and he has a kind nature. He is currently the only dog in the household, but he is friendly with dogs and wants to play on walks so he has the potential to live with another friendly dog.

He is also used to living with older children.

He is fully vaccinated and microchipped and up to date with flea and wormingtreatments.

Loki is in Chorley, Lancashire where he is visitable upon arrangement.

name: Fred
description:
Fred is a 9 year old male Golden Retriever Cross.

Our poor golden retriever beauty, Fred, was surrendered to the shelter days before his ninth birthday, after spending his entire life being owned.

Unfortunately, his family wouldn’t let him live indoors and refused to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate him living outdoors (which is legal in Cyprus), and veterinary services ended up getting involved.

Fred was extremely stressed when he was brought into the shelter and we’ve spent the last few weeks getting to know him and realising how much he’s actually missed out on over the years.

He may have had a family, but he has had minimal socialisation, very little training, no one to rely on and a lot of instability. In fact, three years ago we actually found Fred miles away from home.

He’d been living on a picnic site for weeks before he was reunited with his family via his microchip.

So now, in his senior years, Fred needs an entirely new beginning. He is looking for a patient, understanding and confident family who recognise that he needs time to adapt.

Although he’s nine years old, he’s very active, strong and bouncy, especially when he gets overexcited. He is therefore not suitable for a home with young children as he has no concept of his size and strength.

Being part retriever, Fred is absolutely obsessed with food. He knows how to sit, and he also offers a very gentle and polite paw, but he inhales his food and any kind of treat is welcome!

He also loves water and loves splashing around in the paddling pool on a hot day. And despite his older age, he’s really still a puppy at heart.

He loves his toys, especially a teddy that he can rip apart as he loves taking the stuffing out of things. He also enjoys playing tug with a rope toy, and chasing after a ball (although he’s not sure on the concept of fetch).

Fred hasn’t been very well socialised with other dogs and this is an area that needs some continued work. He is generally good with females, but the first time we introduced him to other dogs we could see in his body language that he just had no idea what to do.

He’s had very limited interactions with other dogs sadly, so he’s not ready to just go into any home and mingle with lots of resident dogs.

Fred does bond quickly with people though and responds really well to kindness. He is a silly, goofy boy with a huge heart and ultimately all he wants is to be adored. He loves a belly rub, he loves playing, and he is sociable and friendly.

He is looking for a family who recognise that he’s been let down over the years and needs a little more guidance, patient and understanding. There is SO much love in this dog, and in the right home he will absolutely blossom.

name: Frodo
description:
Frodo is a one year old male terrier cross. He and his brother, Sam, came to the shelter after they were found wandering in a little pack.

There were four of them in total, and it was very obvious that the boys were brothers right away. They are the cutest duo and both of them are more than ready to find their new homes.

Frodo is the smaller brother. He initially arrived with an eye infection and an abscess, and was feeling quite sorry for himself. His eyes are now fine, but we’re still treating the access, but he’ll be ready to travel once it’s all cleared up.

Although not quite as forthright as his brother, Frodo is still a quietly confident little boy and enjoys the company of people. He is always close behind Sam, tail wagging and eager to make friends.

He also really loves to sit beside you and enjoy a head massage and an ear rub.

Because Sam is always front and centre, Frodo often follows his lead and sometimes doesn’t get quite as much attention because he’s happy to stay in the background.

When he does get his moment to shine, he absolutely loves it. His whole bum wiggles when he wags his tail and he just has the sweetest little face. He responds so well to kindness.

At just over a year old, Frodo will remain small in size and would be ideal for someone looking for a little dog that’s easy to handle.

He has no issues being picked up when needed, and once he’s formed a strong bond with his new family we imagine that he will be really well behaved and eager to please.

Frodo has no issues with other dogs and shares his kennel with his brother and a female dog at present. He shares his bed kindly, and loves snuggling up with them at night.

He also knows to take turns when it comes to food, and he doesn’t show any signs of resource guarding or jealousy.

He would maybe struggle a little more in a very busy home with a lot of noise, but with a little time and a more predictable routine we think Frodo will settle into a companion lifestyle just fine.

Frodo’s ideal home would be with someone who was around frequently, as he wouldn’t enjoy being left alone for long periods of time.

He’d be very happy in the company of another dog as he enjoys being around them, and they do seem to boost his confidence a bit.

But, in the right home he could also be the only resident dog. Frodo can also live in a home with children as he’s very sweet, gentle and polite.

We know that this little guy is going to really come out of his shell given the opportunity and will make such a gorgeous little companion.

name: Jessie
description:
Jessie is a four month old female Labrador cross. Her litter arrived in the shelter when they were just one month old, after their mum was found as a stray.

Unfortunately, their mum was absolutely terrified and it took a while for her to accept the shelter volunteers, but thankfully as the puppies started getting more independent and venturing out of their kennel on their own, they were much more sociable and keen to engage with people.

It took a little while to work on their confidence, but they’re all doing so well and are now ready to find their new homes.

Jessie is the most confident of her siblings and she’s always the first to lead the way for her brothers and sisters. She’s brave, inquisitive and playful, and she’s the most likely to investigate a new environment or unfamiliar toy first.

She is friendly, silly and affectionate, and once she’s made friends with you she really loves your company. She’s eager to interact with new people and given a little time to adjust, we think she will absolutely shine in a new home.

Jessie is playful and friendly with other dogs, and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

We also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home, and although it might take her a little longer to adapt, with patience and understanding she will be okay.

Jessie’s ideal home would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city, who they can dedicate time to training and socialising.

Her balanced temperament at her young age is really promising and we think she’s going to grow into an amazing dog with a very human oriented nature.

Each of the pups will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Jessie has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be suitable to live alongside slightly older children, as she can still sometimes be a little skittish, but she really does enjoy the attention.

She loves to play with anything that squeaks, chew on a rope toy or lollop after a ball, and she would be best suited to a moderately active lifestyle.

name: Topi
description:
Topi is a 10-month-old medium sized cross breed boy. He is a real bundle of joy, very people-centred, affectionate and kind natured. He loves cuddles, attention, and being involved in whatever his humans are doing.

Topi is lovely friendly pup who loves to run, explore and play. He learns quickly, especially when there are treats and praise involved. His eagerness to please makes him a lovely dog to train and grow with.

He would thrive with an active family who enjoys daily walks, adventures in nature or even hiking. Topi would happily join in on family outings and would love to be part of everyday life rather than left on the sidelines.

Topi is brilliant with other dogs, and enjoys playing with them. He is very sociable and makes friends easily.

He would probably be happiest living with another friendly, playful dog, but may as well enjoy being the only dog in the home, soaking up all the attention.

Because he is still young, Topi will need time and patience to settle into a new environment and learn the routines of his new home. With kindness and guidance, he will quickly blossom into a truly wonderful companion.

He could live with older, dog-savvy children who understand how to interact respectfully with a puppy. He can also be tested with cats for the right applicant.

Topi is currently in Hungary and will travel to the UK once a home has been secured for him.

He comes fully vaccinated, microchipped, with an EU pet passport.

name: Ariel
description:
Ariel is a 6-year-old small-medium sized girl with a big personality and an even bigger heart. This feisty little terrier has been waiting in the shelter for over 3 years… far longer than any dog should have to wait.

Ariel is full of character – a true terrier spirit. She’s lively, expressive and not afraid to let you know when she’s excited – it’s all part of her charm!

She is affectionate with people and loves children, happily soaking up attention and enjoying being part of the action. Ariel forms lovely bonds and will be a loyal and loving companion to her family.

With other dogs, she is friendly with most and enjoys their company, though like many terriers, she appreciates respectful introductions and a good match in energy.

After spending such a long time in the shelter, Ariel truly deserves a home where she can finally relax, feel safe, and be loved every day.

She would love a family who will embrace her fun personality, include her in their lives, and give her the attention she’s been missing for so long.

Ariel is in Hungary, ready to travel to the UK once a home has been secured for her.

name: Trixy
description:
Trixy is a 1.5-year-old, smaller medium crossbreed girl with a heart full of love. She was rescued from the streets alongside her mum (a Dachshund cross) and four siblings.

Three of the pups, including Trixy, are still waiting for their happy ending in a shelter in Hungary.

Trixy is a lively, playful young girl who sometimes shows a little shyness at first. But once she feels safe, her sweet, cuddly side shines through — she only needs love, patience, and kindness to truly thrive.

She adores playing with her doggie friends and gets along well with them.

She is friendly with people, including children, and enjoys her walks, trotting happily on the lead. Trixy would be happiest in a family where she isn’t left alone for long hours and is treated as a true member of the family — joining in on adventures, cuddles, and daily life.

She could easily share her home with another playful, gentle dog, or be the only pet, soaking up all the love and attention. Like all rescue dogs, she will need time, patience, and commitment from her new family to settle and blossom into the wonderful companion she is meant to be.

Trixy is currently in Hungary and can travel to the UK once her perfect family is found. She will come spayed, fully vaccinated, microchipped, and with an EU pet passport.

Adoption is subject to a home check and adoption fee. Full RBU provided.
